Serum Uridine levels
Serum Orotate levels
Plasma Citrulline levels
Blood Ammonia levels
correctOption: Blood Ammonia levels
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Beta-alanine is a degradation product of pyrimidines; its levels would be low in a synthesis defect but do not specifically differentiate the two conditions in the context of hyperammonemia.
Incorrect. While uridine might be used as treatment, its serum level is not the standard diagnostic tool for differentiating between the urea cycle and pyrimidine synthesis defects.
Incorrect. Orotate will be elevated in the urine in both UMP Synthase deficiency and Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency, making it non-discriminatory.
Incorrect. While citrulline is part of the urea cycle, it is not the primary differentiator mentioned in the text for these two specific causes of orotic aciduria.

Correct. OTC deficiency (urea cycle) causes hyperammonemia because ammonia cannot be processed into urea; UMP Synthase deficiency is a pure nucleotide metabolism defect and does not affect ammonia clearance.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): Blood ammonia level would expected to be elevated in ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency but not in UMP synthase deficiency.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 4-month-old infant is brought to the clinic due to recurrent severe pneumonia and persistent oral candidiasis. Laboratory evaluation reveals a near-total absence of T cells, B cells, and Natural Killer (NK) cells. Which autosomal recessive enzyme deficiency is most consistent with this global lymphocytopenia?
options: Adenine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT)
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP)
Xanthine oxidase (XO)
Adenosine deaminase (ADA)
Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT)
correctOption: Adenosine deaminase (ADA)
optionExplanations: APRT deficiency leads to the formation of 2,8-dihydroxyadenine stones in the kidney but is not associated with immunodeficiency syndromes.
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency is rarer and typically affects T cells more selectively than ADA deficiency, which causes the more profound T, B, and NK cell depletion.
Xanthine oxidase deficiency (xanthinuria) leads to low uric acid levels and potential xanthine stones, but it does not affect immune cell counts.

ADA deficiency is the classic cause of SCID affecting all three lymphocyte lineages (T, B, and NK cells) because the dATP toxicity impacts the shared precursors and the highly proliferative nature of these cells.
HGPRT deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, characterized by hyperuricemia and neurologic symptoms, but it does not cause severe combined immunodeficiency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In its most severe form, this autosomal recessive disorder causes a type of severe combined immunodeficiency disease (SCID), involving a decrease in T cells, B cells, and natural killer (NK) cells.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Most enzymes of the de novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway are cytosolic. Which enzyme of this pathway is uniquely associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane?
options: CTP synthetase
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
Orotidylate decarboxylase
Aspartate transcarbamoylase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
correctOption: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: CTP synthetase converts UTP to CTP in the cytosol.
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, the enzyme that oxidizes dihydroorotate to orotate, is the only enzyme of the pyrimidine pathway located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Orotidylate decarboxylase is part of the bifunctional UMP synthase located in the cytosol.
Aspartate transcarbamoylase is part of the CAD trifunctional protein located in the cytosol.
CPS II is the first enzyme of the pathway and is located strictly in the cytosol (unlike CPS I).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): [The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. All other enzymes in pyrimidine biosynthesis are cytosolic.]

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
coreConcept: Nitrogen Source Specificity of CPS I and II
statement: In the regulated synthesis of pyrimidines, carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II) utilizes a specific nitrogen donor. How does this donor differ from the one utilized by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS I) in the urea cycle?
options: CPS II utilizes glycine, while CPS I utilizes the amide group of glutamine.
CPS II utilizes glutamate, while CPS I utilizes N-acetylglutamate.
CPS II utilizes free ammonium ions, while CPS I utilizes aspartate.
CPS II utilizes the γ-amide group of glutamine, while CPS I utilizes free ammonia.
CPS II utilizes carbamoyl aspartate, while CPS I utilizes carbamoyl phosphate.
correctOption: CPS II utilizes the γ-amide group of glutamine, while CPS I utilizes free ammonia.
optionExplanations: Glycine is a nitrogen/carbon donor for purine synthesis, not pyrimidine synthesis; CPS I uses ammonia, not glutamine.
Glutamate is a product of the CPS II reaction after glutamine donates its nitrogen; N-acetylglutamate is an allosteric activator, not a nitrogen source.
Ammonium ions are used by CPS I, not CPS II; aspartate provides nitrogen later in both the urea and pyrimidine cycles, but not at the CPS step.
This is the fundamental nitrogenous distinction: CPS II (cytosolic) requires glutamine's amide nitrogen, whereas CPS I (mitochondrial) uses free ammonia (NH3).
Carbamoyl aspartate is the product of the second step of pyrimidine synthesis; carbamoyl phosphate is the product of both CPS I and CPS II.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [Figure 22.20 Summary of the differences between carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) I and II] Source of nitrogen: CPS I - Ammonia; CPS II - γ-Amide group of glutamine

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: Which class of medications is specifically indicated for patients who are 'underexcretors' of uric acid and have normal renal function?
options: Purine analogs
Antioxidants
Folate analogs
Uricosuric agents
Anti-inflammatory steroids
correctOption: Uricosuric agents
optionExplanations: Purine analogs like allopurinol are typically used for overproducers, as they inhibit the production of uric acid.
Uric acid itself has antioxidant effects, but antioxidants are not a standard treatment class for managing hyperuricemia.
Folate analogs like methotrexate inhibit nucleotide synthesis and can actually cause hyperuricemia due to increased cell turnover during cancer treatment.
Uricosuric agents like probenecid specifically target the renal tubules to increase the amount of uric acid excreted in the urine.
Steroids like prednisone treat the inflammation of an acute flare but do not address the underlying hyperuricemia or excretion defects.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): Uricosuric agents, such as probenecid or sulfinpyrazone, that increase renal excretion of uric acid, are used in patients who are “underexcretors” of uric acid.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A 4-year-old male with severe cognitive deficits and hyperuricemia is found to have a mutation in the enzyme that produces 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP). To distinguish this from Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, the clinician measures intracellular IMP levels. Which of the following profiles would point specifically to Lesch-Nyhan syndrome?
options: Low PRPP and high IMP
Low PRPP and low IMP
Normal PRPP and normal IMP
High PRPP and low IMP
High PRPP and high IMP
correctOption: High PRPP and low IMP
optionExplanations: Low PRPP and high IMP would lead to feedback inhibition of the de novo pathway and low uric acid levels.
Low PRPP would not cause hyperuricemia via increased synthesis, as PRPP is the essential activator of the purine pathway.
Normal values for these metabolites would rule out both HGPRT deficiency and PRPP synthetase mutations as the cause of the pathology.
Lesch-Nyhan is unique because the block in salvage causes PRPP to accumulate (high) while the failure to produce IMP via salvage, combined with its rapid degradation, leads to low IMP levels.
High PRPP and high IMP might suggest a PRPP synthetase mutation with increased Vmax where both the precursor and the products are elevated.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): The enzyme deficiency results in increased levels of PRPP and decreased levels of IMP and GMP, causing increased de novo purine synthesis.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Which enzyme is characterized by having broad specificity, allowing it to interconvert various nucleoside diphosphates and triphosphates regardless of the nitrogenous base?
options: Guanylate kinase
Nucleoside diphosphate kinase
Adenylate kinase
IMP dehydrogenase
PRPP synthetase
correctOption: Nucleoside diphosphate kinase
optionExplanations: Guanylate kinase is a base-specific nucleoside monophosphate kinase that specifically converts GMP to GDP using ATP.
Nucleoside diphosphate kinase is relatively non-specific for the base (purine or pyrimidine) or the sugar (ribose or deoxyribose), facilitating the general pool of NTPs.
Adenylate kinase is base-specific, acting only on AMP and ATP/ADP to maintain equilibrium in tissues with high energy turnover.
IMP dehydrogenase is highly specific for IMP and is involved in the committed branch toward GMP synthesis, not general phosphate transfer.
PRPP synthetase catalyzes the formation of PRPP from ribose 5-phosphate and ATP, which is a regulated step for the start of the de novo pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): Nucleoside diphosphates and triphosphates are interconverted by nucleoside diphosphate kinase—an enzyme that, unlike the monophosphate kinases, has broad specificity.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The synthesis of Cytidine Triphosphate (CTP) represents a crucial branch point in pyrimidine metabolism. Which reaction correctly describes the formation of CTP?
options: Methylation of dUMP by Thymidylate synthase
Amination of UTP by CTP synthetase using glutamine as a nitrogen donor
Phosphorylation of CDP by Nucleoside diphosphate kinase
Decarboxylation of OMP by Orotidylate decarboxylase
Reduction of Cytidine diphosphate by Ribonucleotide reductase
correctOption: Amination of UTP by CTP synthetase using glutamine as a nitrogen donor
optionExplanations: Methylation of dUMP produces dTMP (Thymidine), not Cytidine.
CTP is synthesized directly from UTP. The reaction requires ATP as an energy source and uses the amide group of glutamine to replace the keto group on the uracil ring.
While NDP kinase can phosphorylate CDP to CTP, the *de novo* synthesis of the cytosine base occurs at the triphosphate level (UTP to CTP).
Decarboxylation of OMP produces UMP, not CTP.
Ribonucleotide reductase acts on CDP to produce dCDP (deoxy-form) for DNA synthesis, it does not create the CTP base itself.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): CTP is produced by amination of UTP by CTP synthetase (Figure 22.22), with glutamine providing the nitrogen.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A patient undergoing methotrexate therapy for rheumatoid arthritis experiences severe oral ulcerations and gastrointestinal distress. Which cellular characteristic of the affected tissues explains this drug-induced toxicity?
options: Rapid rate of cell division and nucleotide turnover
High expression of UMP synthase
High concentration of xanthine oxidase
Increased salvage of dietary purines
Low levels of dihydrofolate reductase expression
correctOption: Rapid rate of cell division and nucleotide turnover
optionExplanations: Antimetabolites like methotrexate are most toxic to rapidly dividing cells (like GI mucosa) because these cells have the highest demand for DNA synthesis and nucleotide pools.
UMP synthase is involved in pyrimidine synthesis; while relevant to nucleotide metabolism, its expression level is not the primary determinant of methotrexate's tissue-specific toxicity profile.
Xanthine oxidase is primarily in the liver and intestine, but its concentration does not dictate methotrexate toxicity; methotrexate targets folate metabolism.
Increased salvage would actually protect cells from methotrexate; however, many rapidly dividing tissues rely heavily on de novo synthesis for their expansion.
Methotrexate inhibits DHFR; tissues with high turnover need more DHFR activity, making them more sensitive to its inhibition, not less.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Inhibitors of human purine synthesis are extremely toxic to tissues... to cell types that normally replicate rapidly, including those of bone marrow, skin, gastrointestinal (GI) tract, immune system, or hair follicles.

category: Interpret the role of PABA analogs and mycophenolic acid in purine biosynthesis
statement: A pharmacological study compares the effects of sulfonamides on bacterial and human purine biosynthesis. Why is the de novo purine synthesis in humans largely unaffected by these PABA analogs?
options: The human version of IMP dehydrogenase is resistant to PABA-mediated inhibition.
Humans rely on preformed dietary folic acid and cannot synthesize it de novo.
Sulfonamides are rapidly degraded by human intestinal mucosal cell nucleotidases.
Human purine synthesis is primarily dependent on salvage pathways rather than de novo synthesis.
Human cells lack the enzymes required to convert PABA into active folate metabolites.
correctOption: Humans rely on preformed dietary folic acid and cannot synthesize it de novo.
optionExplanations: IMP dehydrogenase is the target of mycophenolic acid, not PABA analogs (sulfonamides).
Sulfonamides inhibit the synthesis of folic acid from PABA. Since humans must ingest preformed folate as a vitamin, they lack the pathway that sulfonamides target.
Sulfonamides are not substrates for nucleotidases, which specifically handle the removal of phosphate groups from nucleotides.
While humans do use salvage pathways, de novo synthesis is essential in many tissues; however, the lack of PABA analog toxicity is strictly due to the dietary requirement for folate.
The issue is not the lack of conversion enzymes, but the fact that humans do not possess the metabolic machinery to synthesize folate from PABA at all.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): Humans cannot synthesize folic acid, and must rely on external sources of this vitamin. Therefore, sulfa drugs do not interfere with human purine synthesis.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
coreConcept: IMP to GMP Branch Point Enzyme
statement: In the de novo synthesis of purine nucleotides, which enzyme is responsible for the first committed step in the conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) to xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)?
options: Adenylosuccinate lyase
GMP synthetase
Adenylosuccinate synthetase
IMP dehydrogenase
Adenylate kinase
correctOption: IMP dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Adenylosuccinate lyase is incorrect because it is involved in the conversion of adenylosuccinate to AMP, releasing fumarate as a byproduct.
GMP synthetase is incorrect because it catalyzes the second step of the pathway, converting XMP to GMP by adding an amide group from glutamine.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is incorrect because it catalyzes the first step in the conversion of IMP to AMP, not GMP, by adding aspartate to IMP.
IMP dehydrogenase is the correct enzyme that oxidizes IMP at the C-2 position to form XMP, using NAD+ as a cofactor, representing the first step toward GMP synthesis.
Adenylate kinase is incorrect as it is a nucleoside monophosphate kinase that interconverts AMP, ADP, and ATP, rather than acting on IMP derivatives during de novo synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): [Figure 22.8] IMP is converted to Xanthosine monophosphate by IMP dehydrogenase using NAD+.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A 14-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department with hematuria. Renal ultrasound reveals multiple radiolucent stones. Physical exam is notable for dystonia and noticeable scarring on the patient's lower lip. Laboratory studies show a serum uric acid level of 12 mg/dL (normal < 7 mg/dL). Which of the following biochemical alterations is a direct consequence of the primary enzyme defect in this child?
options: Failure to convert guanine to guanosine monophosphate (GMP)
Accumulation of xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)
Increased conversion of adenosine to inosine
Inhibition of the enzyme xanthine oxidase
Excessive conversion of PRPP to ribose 5-phosphate
correctOption: Failure to convert guanine to guanosine monophosphate (GMP)
optionExplanations: The primary defect in LNS is a deficiency of HGPRT. HGPRT normally catalyzes the salvage of hypoxanthine to IMP and guanine to GMP. A lack of this enzyme directly results in the failure to produce GMP from the free base guanine.
XMP is an intermediate in the conversion of IMP to GMP. In Lesch-Nyhan, GMP levels are low because the salvage of guanine is blocked, not because XMP is accumulating.
The conversion of adenosine to inosine is mediated by adenosine deaminase (ADA). This pathway is not the primary defect in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome; ADA deficiency causes SCID.
Xanthine oxidase is actually highly active in these patients as it processes the excess hypoxanthine and guanine that cannot be salvaged, leading to high uric acid.
PRPP is synthesized from ribose 5-phosphate by PRPP synthetase. In LNS, PRPP accumulates because it isn't used by the salvage pathway; the reaction doesn't reverse to form ribose 5-phosphate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): This deficiency results in an inability to salvage hypoxanthine or guanine, from which excessive amounts of uric acid, the end product of purine degradation, are produced.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: According to the allosteric model of ribonucleotide reductase, what occurs when ATP binds to the 'activity sites' of the enzyme?
options: The enzyme specifically increases only the reduction of CDP.
The enzyme specifically increases only the reduction of GDP.
The enzyme is activated, promoting the reduction of nucleoside diphosphates.
The overall catalytic activity of the enzyme is inhibited.
The enzyme undergoes degradation by the proteasome.
correctOption: The enzyme is activated, promoting the reduction of nucleoside diphosphates.
optionExplanations: Similar to GDP, the specific reduction of CDP is managed by the substrate specificity site, whereas the activity site controls 'on/off' status.
Substrate-specific shifts (like increasing GDP reduction) are mediated by the substrate specificity sites, not the general activity sites.
ATP binding to the activity sites serves as a signal that cellular energy is high and the cell is ready for DNA replication, thus activating RNR to produce dNTPs.
Inhibition of the overall activity site is caused by dATP, not ATP. This is a crucial feedback mechanism where high dATP levels signal that no more deoxyribonucleotides are needed.
Allosteric binding is a reversible regulatory mechanism and does not result in the permanent degradation of the enzyme by the proteasome.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): In contrast, ATP bound to these sites [activity sites] activates the enzyme.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase is unique in its ability to reduce multiple distinct substrates using a single complex. Which of the following is a pyrimidine ribonucleoside diphosphate that serves as a direct substrate for this enzyme?
options: Uridine diphosphate (UDP)
Deoxycytidine diphosphate (dCDP)
Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
Thymidine monophosphate (TMP)
Cytidine triphosphate (CTP)
correctOption: Uridine diphosphate (UDP)
optionExplanations: UDP is one of the four primary ribonucleoside diphosphate substrates (along with ADP, GDP, and CDP) that ribonucleotide reductase reduces to produce the deoxy-precursors for DNA.
dCDP is the product of the ribonucleotide reductase reaction acting on CDP; as it is already in the deoxy-form, it cannot be a substrate for the reduction of a 2'-hydroxyl group.
IMP is the parent purine monophosphate and is a key intermediate in de novo purine synthesis, but it is not a substrate for ribonucleotide reductase, which requires diphosphates.
TMP is a monophosphate and a deoxy-nucleotide already; it is not a substrate for the reduction reaction of ribonucleotide reductase, which acts on ribonucleoside diphosphates.
CTP is a nucleoside triphosphate used in RNA synthesis and as a precursor for other pyrimidines, but ribonucleotide reductase specifically requires the diphosphate form (CDP) for reduction.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): Ribonucleotide reductase... is specific for the reduction of purine nucleoside diphosphates (ADP and GDP), and pyrimidine nucleoside diphosphates, cytidine diphosphate (CDP) and uridine diphosphate (UDP) to their deoxy-forms.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Mycophenolic acid is a potent immunosuppressant used to prevent graft rejection. What is its specific molecular mechanism within the purine metabolic pathway?
options: It is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.
It acts as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase.
It prevents the salvage of adenine by adenine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT).
It inhibits the conversion of PRPP to 5-phosphoribosylamine.
It inhibits the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate.
correctOption: It is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.
optionExplanations: Mycophenolic acid targets IMP dehydrogenase, the enzyme that converts IMP to XMP on the way to GMP. This specifically starves T and B cells which rely heavily on this pathway for proliferation.
Thymidylate synthase is a pyrimidine pathway enzyme inhibited by 5-fluorouracil, not mycophenolic acid.
Mycophenolic acid does not target the salvage pathway of adenine; it targets the de novo synthesis of guanine nucleotides.
The conversion of PRPP to phosphoribosylamine is inhibited by end-products AMP/GMP, not directly by mycophenolic acid.
Dihydrofolate reductase inhibition is the mechanism of methotrexate, not mycophenolic acid.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): MYCOPHENOLIC ACID: The drug is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase. The drug deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of key components of nucleic acids.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 45-year-old female receiving methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis presents with mouth ulcers and a low red cell count. Biopsy shows megaloblastic changes. Methotrexate interferes with both purine and pyrimidine synthesis. Which specific pyrimidine-related reaction is most compromised by the reduction in tetrahydrofolate (THF) levels caused by this drug?
options: The decarboxylation of OMP to UMP
The amination of UTP to CTP
Carbamoyl phosphate synthesis by CPS II
The reduction of UDP to dUDP
The methylation of dUMP to dTMP
correctOption: The methylation of dUMP to dTMP
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Orotidylate decarboxylase (part of UMP synthase) does not require THF.
Incorrect. CTP synthetase uses glutamine as a nitrogen donor, not THF.
Incorrect. CPS II does not require THF; it requires glutamine and CO2.
Incorrect. Ribonucleotide reductase uses thioredoxin as a reducing agent, not THF.
Correct. Thymidylate synthase requires N5,N10-methylene THF to convert dUMP to dTMP. Methotrexate depletes THF, thus halting this methylation.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): By decreasing the supply of THF, these folate analogs [methotrexate]... also lower the cellular concentration of this essential component of DNA [dTMP]... preventing methylation of dUMP to dTMP.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
coreConcept: Allosteric Regulation of Ribonucleotide Reductase Activity
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase is highly regulated to ensure a balanced supply of the four dNTPs. What is the effect of ATP binding to the activity site of this enzyme?
options: It activates the enzyme, signaling that the cell has sufficient energy for DNA synthesis.
It induces the degradation of the R2 subunit to terminate the S-phase.
It changes the substrate specificity to favor the reduction of pyrimidines over purines.
It causes the enzyme to switch from using thioredoxin to using glutathione.
It inhibits the enzyme, preventing the overproduction of deoxyribonucleotides.
correctOption: It activates the enzyme, signaling that the cell has sufficient energy for DNA synthesis.
optionExplanations: This is correct. ATP binding at the activity site (on the R1 subunit) acts as a positive allosteric effector, promoting the overall activity of the enzyme.
ATP binding is a reversible allosteric event and does not lead to the proteolytic degradation of the enzyme subunits.
Substrate specificity is controlled by the binding of various nucleotides to a separate specificity site, not the primary activity site.
The coenzyme preference for thioredoxin is determined by the enzyme's structure and is not altered by allosteric regulators at the activity site.
dATP is the inhibitor at the activity site; ATP is the activator.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): In contrast, ATP bound to these sites [activity sites] activates the enzyme.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A researcher is studying the precursors of nucleic acid synthesis in human hepatocytes. Which set of molecules is entirely responsible for contributing the carbon and nitrogen atoms to the pyrimidine ring during de-novo synthesis?
options: Aspartic acid, Glycine, and Glutamine
Glycine, CO2, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Aspartic acid, Glutamine, and CO2
Glycine, N10-formyltetrahydrofolate, and CO2
Glutamine, CO2, and Ammonia
correctOption: Aspartic acid, Glutamine, and CO2
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Glycine is specific to purine synthesis and does not contribute atoms to the pyrimidine ring.
Incorrect. This combination of glycine and formyl-THF is characteristic of the purine biosynthetic pathway, not pyrimidines.
Correct. In pyrimidine de-novo synthesis, the amide nitrogen of glutamine, the carbon of CO2, and the entire aspartic acid molecule provide the atoms for the six-membered ring.
Incorrect. Glycine and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate are precursors for the purine ring, not the pyrimidine ring.
Incorrect. While glutamine and CO2 are involved, aspartic acid is missing, and ammonia is typically the nitrogen source for CPS I in the urea cycle, not CPS II in pyrimidine synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): The sources of the atoms in the pyrimidine ring are glutamine, CO 2 , and aspartic acid (Figure 22.19).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Hydroxyurea is a pharmacological agent used in the management of chronic myelogenous leukemia and sickle cell disease. Which of the following describes its primary mechanism of action regarding nucleotide metabolism?
options: It promotes the oxidation of NADPH, depriving the cell of reducing equivalents
It prevents the conversion of dUDP to dTMP by thymidylate synthase
It acts as a competitive inhibitor of the thioredoxin reductase enzyme
It destroys the free radical required for the activity of ribonucleotide reductase
It inhibits the binding of ATP to the activity site of the R1 subunit
correctOption: It destroys the free radical required for the activity of ribonucleotide reductase
optionExplanations: While NADPH is required for the cycle to continue, hydroxyurea does not directly interact with NADPH; it targets the enzyme-bound radical intermediate.
This is the mechanism of 5-fluorouracil (via 5-FdUMP), not hydroxyurea. Hydroxyurea acts upstream at the stage of dNDP production.
Hydroxyurea does not target thioredoxin reductase; it targets the ribonucleotide reductase enzyme directly.

The activity of ribonucleotide reductase (specifically the R2 subunit) depends on a tyrosyl free radical. Hydroxyurea quenches or destroys this free radical, thereby inactivating the enzyme and preventing the formation of deoxyribonucleotides.
Hydroxyurea does not interfere with the allosteric activity site; it is a catalytic inhibitor that targets the chemical mechanism (the free radical) of the enzyme.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): The drug hydroxyurea destroys the free radical required for enzymic activity of ribonucleotide reductase, and thus inhibits the generation of substrates for DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: In the metabolic loop converting Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to other purines, how are the energy requirements for the synthesis of AMP and GMP cross-regulated?
options: AMP synthesis is powered by the hydrolysis of pyrophosphate, while GMP requires GTP.
Both AMP and GMP synthesis require ATP exclusively to ensure consistency.
The conversion to GMP requires NADH, while AMP synthesis requires FADH2.
Both pathways are strictly anaerobic and do not require nucleoside triphosphates.
AMP synthesis requires GTP as an energy source, while GMP synthesis requires ATP.
correctOption: AMP synthesis requires GTP as an energy source, while GMP synthesis requires ATP.
optionExplanations: While pyrophosphate hydrolysis often drives reactions, the specific energy donors for these two branches are GTP and ATP.
Only GMP synthesis uses ATP as the energy source; AMP synthesis specifically requires GTP.
NADH is involved in the IMP dehydrogenase step for GMP synthesis, but the question asks about the energy (triphosphate) requirements for the overall conversion.
Nucleotide synthesis is an energy-intensive process that absolutely requires nucleoside triphosphates (GTP and ATP).
To maintain a balance between the two purine nucleotides, the synthesis of AMP is powered by GTP, and the synthesis of GMP is powered by ATP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: In a patient with a functional salvage pathway, Allopurinol therapy reduces de novo purine synthesis by decreasing PRPP levels through hypoxanthine salvage. Why is this specific regulatory benefit lost in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome?
options: Allopurinol cannot be converted to oxypurinol in these patients.
Allopurinol acts as an activator of glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase in the absence of HGPRT.
PRPP synthetase is irreversibly inhibited by the HGPRT deficiency itself.
Xanthine oxidase is naturally absent in patients with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
The absence of HGPRT prevents the salvage of hypoxanthine, which would otherwise consume PRPP.
correctOption: The absence of HGPRT prevents the salvage of hypoxanthine, which would otherwise consume PRPP.
optionExplanations: The conversion of allopurinol to oxypurinol is catalyzed by xanthine oxidase, which is present in Lesch-Nyhan patients; this metabolic step is not impaired.

Allopurinol (or its metabolite oxypurinol) does not activate the amidotransferase; it is a structural analog of hypoxanthine used to inhibit uric acid production by xanthine oxidase. It does not directly affect the committed step in this way.
HGPRT deficiency does not inhibit PRPP synthetase; rather, it leads to an accumulation of PRPP because the 'activated' pentose is not being utilized by the salvage pathway.
Xanthine oxidase is present and hyperactive (in terms of throughput) in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome due to the massive supply of purine degradation products; it is not absent.

In healthy individuals, allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, leading to hypoxanthine accumulation. This hypoxanthine is salvaged by HGPRT, consuming PRPP and lowering its concentration. In Lesch-Nyhan, HGPRT is missing, so PRPP levels remain high despite allopurinol use.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.

category: Interpret the role of PABA analogs and mycophenolic acid in purine biosynthesis
statement: A patient with a recent heart transplant develops a bacterial urinary tract infection. The physician considers using a sulfonamide antibiotic but must be cautious of the patient's existing immunosuppressant, mycophenolate mofetil. Which statement correctly distinguishes the biochemical targets of these two drugs within the purine pathway?
options: Sulfonamides inhibit the formation of the purine ring, while mycophenolate inhibits the maturation of IMP to GMP.
Sulfonamides are purine base analogs, while mycophenolate is a folate analog.
Sulfonamides target the purine salvage pathway, while mycophenolate targets de novo synthesis.
Sulfonamides inhibit the reduction of ribose to deoxyribose, while mycophenolate inhibits PRPP synthesis.
Sulfonamides target the mitochondria, while mycophenolate targets the nucleus.
correctOption: Sulfonamides inhibit the formation of the purine ring, while mycophenolate inhibits the maturation of IMP to GMP.
optionExplanations: Sulfonamides deplete THF, which is required for steps 3 and 9 of the purine ring assembly. Mycophenolate inhibits IMP dehydrogenase, which occurs after the IMP 'parent' nucleotide is already formed, blocking its conversion to GMP.
This is incorrect; sulfonamides are PABA analogs and mycophenolate is an inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase. Methotrexate is a folate analog.
Neither drug primarily targets the salvage pathway (APRT/HGPRT).
Ribose reduction is the job of ribonucleotide reductase (inhibited by hydroxyurea). PRPP synthesis is inhibited by high levels of purine nucleotides.
Most steps for both targets are cytosolic; only dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (pyrimidine synthesis) is mitochondrial.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page)-303: Sulfonamides... competitively inhibit bacterial synthesis of folic acid. Because purine synthesis requires tetrahydrofolate as a coenzyme, the sulfa drugs slow down this pathway... [Mycophenolic acid] is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: A 2-day-old male neonate presents with lethargy and poor feeding. Laboratory findings reveal severe hyperammonemia and significantly elevated levels of orotic acid in the urine. A deficiency in ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) is suspected. Which mechanism explains the elevated orotic acid in this patient?
options: Direct activation of CPS I by orotic acid
Primary deficiency of UMP synthase
Failure of PRPP to activate CPS II
Shunting of mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate into the cytosol
Overactivity of CPS II due to lack of feedback inhibition
correctOption: Shunting of mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate into the cytosol
optionExplanations: Orotic acid is a product of the pyrimidine pathway, not an activator of CPS I.
Primary UMP synthase deficiency (hereditary orotic aciduria) also causes high orotic acid, but it would not be associated with severe hyperammonemia as seen in a urea cycle defect.
PRPP is an activator of CPS II; its failure would decrease, not increase, pyrimidine production.

When OTC is defective, carbamoyl phosphate produced by CPS I in the mitochondria accumulates and diffuses into the cytosol, where it enters the pyrimidine pathway, bypassing the regulated CPS II step.
While CPS II activity might contribute, the primary cause of the surge in orotic acid in OTC deficiency is the overflow of carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondria.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: Which of the following characterizes the bifunctional enzyme UMP synthase, the deficiency of which results in hereditary orotic aciduria?
options: It is a mitochondrial enzyme responsible for the closure of the dihydroorotate ring.
It consists of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II and aspartate transcarbamoylase domains.
It combines the catalytic activities of orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase.
It functions primarily to salvage free pyrimidine bases like uracil and thymine.
It requires ammonia as a direct nitrogen donor to synthesize uridine monophosphate.
correctOption: It combines the catalytic activities of orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase.
optionExplanations: UMP synthase is a cytosolic enzyme. Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is the only enzyme in the de novo pyrimidine pathway that is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II and aspartate transcarbamoylase are parts of the CAD multifunctional polypeptide, not UMP synthase. CAD catalyzes the first three steps of the pathway, whereas UMP synthase catalyzes the final two.

UMP synthase is a single polypeptide with two distinct catalytic domains: orotate phosphoribosyltransferase, which attaches the ribose-5-phosphate from PRPP to orotate, and orotidylate decarboxylase, which converts OMP to UMP.
UMP synthase is part of the de novo synthesis pathway, not the salvage pathway. While it does use PRPP like salvage enzymes, its substrates are intermediates synthesized within the de novo sequence.
UMP synthase uses orotic acid and PRPP as substrates. Ammonia is used by CPS I in the urea cycle, whereas the pyrimidine pathway uses the amide group of glutamine via CPS II.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Orotate phosphoribosyl transferase and orotidylate decarboxylase are also catalytic domains of a single polypeptide chain called UMP synthase. Orotic aciduria—a rare genetic defect—may be caused by a deficiency of one or both activities of this bifunctional enzyme.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
coreConcept: Immunological Profile of ADA vs PNP Deficiency
statement: In contrasting the two major inherited immunodeficiencies of purine degradation, which finding is unique to Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency compared to Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency?
options: Development of recurrent bacterial and viral infections
Accumulation of dGTP within the mitochondrial matrix
Profound depletion of T cells, B cells, and Natural Killer (NK) cells
Inheritance via an autosomal recessive pattern
Association with neurodevelopmental delay and motor deficits
correctOption: Profound depletion of T cells, B cells, and Natural Killer (NK) cells
optionExplanations: Both ADA and PNP deficiencies lead to immunodeficiency and recurrent infections, so this is not a distinguishing factor between them.
ADA deficiency is associated with the accumulation of dATP, not dGTP. PNP deficiency involves different purine metabolites.
ADA deficiency causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID), affecting the entire lymphocyte lineage (T, B, and NK cells), whereas PNP deficiency primarily impacts T cells.
Both ADA deficiency and PNP deficiency are inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, so this does not serve as a point of contrast.
According to the text, neurodevelopmental delay is specifically highlighted as a feature of the rarer PNP deficiency, not the classic ADA presentation.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): ADA ... deficiency causes a type of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), involving a decrease in T cells, B cells, and natural killer (NK) cells. ... PNP deficiency results in a less severe immunodeficiency involving T-cells primarily.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: The rate of the committed step in de novo purine biosynthesis, catalyzed by glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase, is primarily regulated by the intracellular concentration of PRPP because of which biochemical factor?
options: PRPP is required for the stabilization of the enzyme's quaternary structure.
The enzyme is covalently modified by PRPP levels.
PRPP acts as a competitive inhibitor of the end-product AMP.
High PRPP levels induce the expression of the amidotransferase gene.
The intracellular PRPP concentration is normally far below the Km of the enzyme.
correctOption: The intracellular PRPP concentration is normally far below the Km of the enzyme.
optionExplanations: While many enzymes have structural requirements, the primary kinetic reason for PRPP's regulatory role is its low physiological concentration relative to the enzyme's Km.
The regulation by PRPP is based on substrate availability and allosteric effects, not covalent modification like phosphorylation.
PRPP is a substrate and activator, while AMP is an inhibitor; they do not compete for the same site in a way that makes PRPP a competitive inhibitor of AMP.
The text describes biochemical regulation (feedback/substrate flux), not transcriptional induction of the enzyme by PRPP.

In kinetics, if the substrate concentration is much lower than the Michaelis constant (Km), the reaction rate is highly sensitive to changes in substrate concentration, allowing PRPP to effectively control the pathway's flux.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): The intracellular concentration of PRPP is normally far below the Km for the amidotransferase. Therefore, any small change in the PRPP concentration causes a proportional change in the rate of the reaction.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: A patient with hereditary orotic aciduria presents with megaloblastic anemia. This specific hematological abnormality occurs because the lack of UMP leads to a deficiency in which of the following, which is essential for DNA synthesis?
options: Beta-aminoisobutyrate
N5, N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate
Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
2'-Deoxythymidine monophosphate (dTMP)
Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
correctOption: 2'-Deoxythymidine monophosphate (dTMP)
optionExplanations: Beta-aminoisobutyrate is a soluble degradation product of the pyrimidine ring; it is not involved in DNA synthesis and would likely be decreased, not increased, in this synthesis defect.

N5, N10-methylene THF is a coenzyme for thymidylate synthase. While its lack also causes anemia, orotic aciduria causes anemia by blocking the production of the substrate (dUMP) for dTMP synthesis, not the folate coenzyme.
IMP is the parent nucleotide for purines. While essential for DNA, its synthesis is not impaired by a block in the UMP synthase enzyme of the pyrimidine pathway.
UMP is the precursor for dUMP, which is then methylated to form dTMP. Without dTMP, DNA synthesis is impaired, leading to the characteristic large, immature red blood cells of megaloblastic anemia.
HGPRT is a purine salvage enzyme. Its deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, not the megaloblastic anemia associated with orotic aciduria (which involves pyrimidines).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): By preventing methylation of dUMP to dTMP, they also lower the cellular concentration of this essential component of DNA. DNA synthesis is inhibited and cell growth slowed. [Note: ... Low activities of... UMP synthase result in... megaloblastic anemia.]

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A first-year medical student is asked to identify the atoms that constitute the pyrimidine ring during a biochemistry seminar. Which of the following sets of compounds directly contribute the atoms required for the de novo synthesis of the pyrimidine ring?
options: Glycine, Glutamine, and CO2
Aspartic acid, Glutamine, and CO2
Aspartic acid, Glycine, and CO2
Aspartic acid, Ammonia, and CO2
Glutamine, Tetrahydrofolate, and CO2
correctOption: Aspartic acid, Glutamine, and CO2
optionExplanations: Glycine is a major precursor for the purine ring, providing carbons 4 and 5 and nitrogen 7, but it is not utilized in the pyrimidine ring synthesis.

Correct. In pyrimidine biosynthesis, the nitrogen at position 1 and carbons at positions 4, 5, and 6 come from aspartic acid, while carbon 2 comes from CO2 and nitrogen 3 comes from the amide group of glutamine.
Glycine is characteristic of purine synthesis; pyrimidines rely on aspartate and glutamine.
Free ammonia is the nitrogen source for Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (Urea cycle), but CPS II (Pyrimidine synthesis) specifically utilizes the amide group of glutamine.
N10-formyl-tetrahydrofolate is required for carbons 2 and 8 of the purine ring, but it is not a direct atom donor for the initial pyrimidine ring structure.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): The sources of the atoms in the pyrimidine ring are glutamine, CO2, and aspartic acid (Figure 22.19).

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
coreConcept: Reciprocal Regulation of Purine Nucleotide Synthesis
statement: The conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to either Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP) or Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) utilizes a reciprocal energy-coupling mechanism. Which statement accurately describes the regulation of this branch point?
options: IMP dehydrogenase, the first enzyme in GMP synthesis, is irreversibly inhibited by Mycophenolic acid.
AMP synthesis requires GTP, while GMP synthesis requires ATP.
The synthesis of AMP requires ATP as an energy source to provide positive feedback.
GMP synthesis is inhibited by ATP, while AMP synthesis is inhibited by GTP.
The synthesis of GMP requires GTP to ensure balanced purine ratios.
correctOption: AMP synthesis requires GTP, while GMP synthesis requires ATP.
optionExplanations: Mycophenolic acid is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase, not an irreversible one. It is used as an immunosuppressant.
This is the classic definition of reciprocal regulation in purine metabolism: ATP is the energy donor for GMP synthesis, and GTP is the energy donor for AMP synthesis.
Actually, AMP synthesis requires GTP. This reciprocal use of a different triphosphate ensures that if GTP (and thus GMP) is abundant, AMP synthesis is promoted.
The end products (AMP and GMP) inhibit their own respective first steps from IMP (adenylosuccinate synthetase and IMP dehydrogenase), but the energy sources are the alternative triphosphates.
GMP synthesis requires ATP as the energy source for the GMP synthetase reaction, not GTP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: An elite researcher is studying the allosteric regulation of the initial phase of purine synthesis. In his experiments, he observes that the enzyme responsible for synthesizing the 'activated pentose' required for both purine and pyrimidine pathways is uniquely stimulated by a specific inorganic ion. Which of the following molecules acts as an obligatory activator for this specific enzyme?
options: Uridine triphosphate (UTP)
Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
Citrate
Inorganic phosphate
Guanosine monophosphate (GMP)
correctOption: Inorganic phosphate
optionExplanations: UTP is an inhibitor of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II) in the pyrimidine pathway, but it does not serve as an activator for PRPP synthetase.
ATP is a substrate for the PRPP synthetase reaction, not an allosteric activator. It provides the pyrophosphate group transferred to ribose 5-phosphate.
Citrate is an intermediate of the TCA cycle and a regulator of fatty acid synthesis, but it has no direct regulatory role in PRPP synthesis.

Inorganic phosphate (Pi) is the primary allosteric activator of PRPP synthetase. High levels of Pi signal a need for more nucleotides or energy, thus driving the synthesis of 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP).
GMP is a purine nucleotide that serves as an end-product inhibitor of PRPP synthetase, not an activator.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): [PRPP synthetase] is activated by inorganic phosphate and inhibited by purine nucleotides (end-product inhibition).

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
coreConcept: Kinetic Regulation of Purine Synthesis in Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
statement: In the context of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, why does the resultant elevation of intracellular 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) lead to a disproportionately large increase in the rate of de novo purine synthesis?
options: PRPP acts as a non-competitive inhibitor of the salvage enzymes.
The normal intracellular concentration of PRPP is significantly lower than the Km of the amidotransferase.
Elevated PRPP stabilizes the structure of the parent purine nucleotide, IMP.
Increased PRPP concentrations induce the expression of the HGPRT gene.
PRPP prevents the hydrolysis of pyrophosphate by pyrophosphatase.
correctOption: The normal intracellular concentration of PRPP is significantly lower than the Km of the amidotransferase.
optionExplanations: PRPP is an activator/substrate, not an inhibitor, of the pathway enzymes.

Since the baseline concentration of PRPP is well below the Michaelis constant (Km) of the committed step enzyme (amidotransferase), any increase in PRPP levels leads to a direct and proportional acceleration of purine synthesis.
PRPP provides the ribose 5-phosphate moiety but does not act as a stabilizer for the final nucleotide structure.
Lesch-Nyhan is characterized by a deficiency or absence of HGPRT activity; PRPP does not induce gene expression to correct this defect.
Pyrophosphatase activity is independent of PRPP concentration and is required for the irreversibility of salvage reactions.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): The intracellular concentration of PRPP is normally far below the Km for the amidotransferase. Therefore, any small change in the PRPP concentration causes a proportional change in the rate of the reaction.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A comparison is made between Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency and Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency. Which diagnostic feature most accurately distinguishes these two autosomal recessive purine degradation disorders?
options: PNP deficiency results in the overproduction of uric acid, whereas ADA deficiency results in hypouricemia.
PNP deficiency is characterized by self-mutilation, unlike ADA deficiency.
ADA deficiency prevents the salvage of guanine, whereas PNP deficiency prevents the salvage of adenine.
ADA deficiency only manifests in geriatric patients, whereas PNP deficiency is neonatal.
ADA deficiency leads to severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) affecting T, B, and NK cells, while PNP deficiency primarily affects T-cells.
correctOption: ADA deficiency leads to severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) affecting T, B, and NK cells, while PNP deficiency primarily affects T-cells.
optionExplanations: Both disorders are associated with defects in the degradation pathway leading to uric acid, but neither is primarily defined by hyper- or hypouricemia as their chief diagnostic differentiator; rather, they are defined by their specific immune cell deficits.
Self-mutilation is the hallmark of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (HGPRT deficiency), not PNP or ADA deficiency.

ADA converts adenosine to inosine; PNP converts inosine/guanosine to their bases. Their role is in degradation, though their absence affects the availability of salvageable substrates indirectly through metabolic imbalance, their primary distinction is the clinical immune profile as per the text on page 308/309/310 references provided for purine degradation diseases/SCID specifically related to ADA and PNP respectively.
Both are autosomal recessive genetic disorders that typically manifest in early childhood, not in geriatric populations.

ADA deficiency causes a toxic buildup of dATP, which inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and leads to the depletion of T, B, and NK cells (SCID). PNP deficiency is rarer and specifically causes a selective T-cell immunodeficiency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): ADA deficiency accounts for approximately 14% of all cases of SCID. [Note: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency results in a less severe immunodeficiency involving T-cells primarily.]

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: Chronic tophaceous gout is characterized by the formation of 'tophi'. Which of the following best describes these structures?
options: Nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues
Erosive lesions caused by the overactivity of osteoclasts
Malignant transformations of the synovial membrane
Fluid-filled cysts containing high concentrations of calcium
Calcified deposits within the cardiac valves
correctOption: Nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues
optionExplanations: Tophi are pathognomonic for chronic gout and consist of aggregated urate crystals surrounded by chronic inflammatory cells and fibrous tissue in skin, cartilage, or joints.
Tophi can cause secondary bone erosion, but the tophus itself is the crystal mass, not the resulting bone lesion.
Tophi are inflammatory and crystalline deposits, not neoplastic or malignant growths.
While tophi are masses, they are composed of monosodium urate, not calcium, and are generally solid/chalky rather than simple fluid cysts.
Calcifications in cardiac valves are usually related to degenerative changes or rheumatic fever, not the urate deposition characteristic of gout.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): Nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals (tophi) may be deposited in the soft tissues, resulting in chronic tophaceous gout (Figure 22.16).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 55-year-old male with colorectal cancer is treated with 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU). Biologically, 5-FU is converted to 5-FdUMP, which leads to 'thymineless death' of the tumor cells. Which statement best describes the biochemical inhibition occurring in this patient?
options: Irreversible 'suicide' inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase
Allosteric inhibition of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II
Inhibition of Ribonucleotide Reductase by destroying free radicals
Competitive inhibition of Orotidine 5'-monophosphate decarboxylase
Reversible inhibition of Dihydrofolate Reductase
correctOption: Irreversible 'suicide' inhibition of Thymidylate Synthase
optionExplanations: 5-FU is converted to 5-FdUMP, which binds covalently and permanently to Thymidylate Synthase, preventing the methylation of dUMP to dTMP, thus halting DNA synthesis.
CPS II is regulated by UTP and PRPP; while 5-FU might theoretically impact downstream pools, its primary therapeutic target is not the first step of the de novo pathway.
Ribonucleotide Reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea via free radical destruction, or by dATP allosterically, not by 5-FU conversion products.
Orotidine 5'-monophosphate decarboxylase is a domain of UMP synthase; its deficiency causes orotic aciduria, but it is not the target of 5-FU.
Dihydrofolate Reductase is the target of Methotrexate, not 5-FU. Methotrexate prevents the regeneration of THF.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a “suicide” inhibitor.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: What is the primary source of the phosphate group used by nucleoside monophosphate kinases to convert NMPs to NDPs in most cellular conditions?
options: Creatine phosphate
Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
Phosphoenolpyruvate
Inorganic phosphate (Pi)
Guanosine triphosphate (GTP)
correctOption: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
optionExplanations: Creatine phosphate is an energy reserve in muscle that helps regenerate ATP from ADP, but it does not directly donate phosphate to NMPs in this pathway.
ATP is the most abundant nucleoside triphosphate in the cell and serves as the universal phosphate donor for the conversion of NMPs to NDPs via base-specific kinases.
Phosphoenolpyruvate is a high-energy intermediate in glycolysis used to form ATP from ADP, but it is not the direct substrate for nucleoside monophosphate kinases.
Inorganic phosphate is used by phosphorylases, but kinases specifically transfer a phosphate from a nucleoside triphosphate, usually ATP.
While GTP can serve as a donor in some reactions (like AMP synthesis), it is not the primary donor for monophosphate kinases.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): ATP is generally the source of the transferred phosphate, because it is present in higher concentrations than the other nucleoside triphosphates.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: What is the medical term for the nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals that may deposit in soft tissues during the progression to chronic gout?
options: Xanthomas
Rheumatoid nodules
Osteophytes
Tophi
Urinary calculi
correctOption: Tophi
optionExplanations: Xanthomas are deposits of lipids/cholesterol in the skin or tendons, associated with hyperlipidemia.
Rheumatoid nodules are associated with rheumatoid arthritis and are composed of fibrinoid necrosis and collagen, not urate crystals.
Osteophytes are 'bone spurs' associated with osteoarthritis, representing bony outgrowths rather than crystal deposits.
Tophi are pathognomonic for chronic gout and represent organized aggregates of urate crystals surrounded by chronic inflammation.
Urinary calculi (kidney stones) can be made of uric acid, but 'nodular masses in soft tissues' specifically refers to tophi.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 291 (Book Page): Nodular masses of monosodium urate crystals (tophi) may be deposited in the soft tissues, resulting in chronic tophaceous gout (Figure 22.16).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Diagnostic markers for UMP synthase deficiency
statement: Which of the following findings is considered a primary diagnostic criterion for Hereditary Orotic Aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency)?
options: Low blood urea nitrogen (BUN) with xanthine stones
High serum dATP with lymphopenia
Elevated urinary orotic acid with megaloblastic anemia
Microcytic anemia with hyperammonemia
Hypouricemia with self-mutilation
correctOption: Elevated urinary orotic acid with megaloblastic anemia
optionExplanations: Xanthine stones occur in xanthine oxidase deficiency or allopurinol therapy; pyrimidine disorders typically produce orotic acid crystals.
High dATP and lymphopenia are diagnostic markers for Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, a purine degradation disorder causing SCID.
Hereditary orotic aciduria is characterized by high levels of orotate in the urine and a megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to standard B12/folate therapy.
The anemia in orotic aciduria is macrocytic (megaloblastic), not microcytic, and the ammonia levels are typically normal in the primary enzyme deficiency.
Self-mutilation and hyperuricemia are diagnostic criteria for Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, which involves the purine salvage pathway enzyme HGPRT.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in poor growth, megaloblastic anemia, and the excretion of large amounts of orotate in the urine.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: How does the administration of Methotrexate specifically disrupt the one-carbon transfer cycle required for the synthesis of deoxythymidine monophosphate (dTMP)?
options: It directly competes with dUMP for the active site of thymidylate synthase.
It irreversibly binds to N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate.
It acts as a structural analog of uracil to prevent methylation.
It inhibits the conversion of serine to glycine, depleting methylene groups.
It prevents the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate.
correctOption: It prevents the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate.
optionExplanations: Competing with dUMP for thymidylate synthase is the mechanism for 5-FdUMP (the metabolite of 5-FU), not methotrexate.
Methotrexate inhibits the enzyme DHFR; it does not bind to the methylene-THF coenzyme itself, although it causes the concentration of these coenzymes to fall.
Methotrexate is an analog of folic acid (pteridine ring), not uracil. 5-Fluorouracil is the uracil analog.
While the serine-glycine conversion involves THF, methotrexate does not target the serine hydroxymethyltransferase enzyme; it targets DHFR to deplete the entire THF pool.

Methotrexate is a structural analog of folic acid that competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). This prevents the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate (THF) from dihydrofolate (DHF), which is produced during the thymidylate synthase reaction.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): DHF can be reduced to THF by dihydrofolate reductase... an enzyme that is inhibited by drugs such as methotrexate. By decreasing the supply of THF, these folate analogs... prevent methylation of dUMP to dTMP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
coreConcept: Reciprocal energy requirement in purine synthesis
statement: In the de novo synthesis of purine nucleotides, which specific high-energy phosphate donor is required for the conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) to adenylosuccinate?
options: Inosine triphosphate (ITP)
Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
Uridine triphosphate (UTP)
Guanosine triphosphate (GTP)
Cytidine triphosphate (CTP)
correctOption: Guanosine triphosphate (GTP)
optionExplanations: Inosine triphosphate (ITP) is a rare nucleotide formed from IMP but does not act as a high-energy cofactor for the enzymes of its own metabolic branch points toward AMP or GMP.

Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is incorrect because it is the energy source required for the synthesis of Guanosine monophosphate (GMP) from xanthosine monophosphate (XMP), not for the synthesis of AMP.
Uridine triphosphate (UTP) is a pyrimidine nucleotide that serves as a precursor for CTP and glycogen synthesis (UDP-glucose) but does not provide energy for purine ring modifications.

Guanosine triphosphate (GTP) is correct. In a reciprocal regulation mechanism, GTP provides the energy required to convert IMP to AMP, ensuring that the synthesis of one purine is balanced by the availability of the other.
Cytidine triphosphate (CTP) is a pyrimidine nucleotide involved in lipid synthesis (e.g., CDP-choline) and is not used as an energy donor in the IMP branching pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Which of the following describes the first biochemical reaction in the pathway that leads specifically from inosine monophosphate (IMP) to guanosine monophosphate (GMP)?
options: Amination of IMP using glutamine to form XMP.
Amination of IMP using aspartate to form adenylosuccinate.
Hydrolysis of IMP to inosine followed by phosphorylation.
Phosphorylation of IMP to IDP by a base-specific kinase.
Oxidation of IMP by an NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase to form xanthosine monophosphate.
correctOption: Oxidation of IMP by an NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase to form xanthosine monophosphate.
optionExplanations: Amination occurs in the second step of the GMP branch (XMP to GMP), not the first step; the first step is an oxidation, not an amination.
This describes the first step of the AMP branch, not the GMP branch.
Hydrolysis of IMP to inosine is a degradative step catalyzed by 5'-nucleotidase, not part of the synthetic pathway to GMP.
Kinases act on monophosphates to form diphosphates, but IMP must first be chemically modified to GMP or AMP before these kinases act.
The GMP branch begins with the oxidation of IMP at C-2 by IMP dehydrogenase, requiring NAD+ as a cofactor to produce Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): [Figure 22.8] IMP is converted to Xanthosine monophosphate by IMP dehydrogenase using NAD+ and H2O.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Unlike the purine ring which remains intact in humans, the pyrimidine ring is susceptible to opening and total degradation. Which of the following are the primary soluble end products of pyrimidine catabolism?
options: Succinyl-CoA and malonate
Xanthine and hypoxanthine
Beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate
Urea and ammonium sulfate
Uric acid and allantoin
correctOption: Beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate
optionExplanations: These molecules are not the primary end products of pyrimidine ring cleavage; the specific products mentioned in medical biochemistry are the beta-amino acids alanine and aminoisobutyrate.
Xanthine and hypoxanthine are intermediates in the purine degradation pathway, which lead to the formation of uric acid.
The catabolism of uracil and cytosine yields beta-alanine, while the catabolism of thymine yields beta-aminoisobutyrate; both are highly soluble and excreted.
While ammonia (NH3) is a byproduct of pyrimidine degradation, the unique carbon skeletons are converted to beta-amino acids rather than just urea.
Uric acid is the end product of purine degradation in humans. Allantoin is produced by urate oxidase in other mammals, but not typically in humans.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Unlike the purine ring, which is not cleaved human cells, the pyrimidine ring is opened and degraded to highly soluble products, β -alanine and β -aminoisobutyrate, with the production of NH 3 and CO 2 .

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: The conversion of Inosine Monophosphate (IMP) to either Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP) or Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) is tightly regulated. What is the metabolic consequence of a significant rise in intracellular Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) levels regarding this branching pathway?
options: Activation of IMP dehydrogenase by allosteric competition
Inhibition of adenylosuccinate synthetase
Activation of the conversion of IMP to GMP
Redirection of IMP toward the pyrimidine pathway
Immediate degradation of IMP to Hypoxanthine
correctOption: Activation of the conversion of IMP to GMP
optionExplanations: While IMP dehydrogenase is the first step toward GMP, the text specifies that the requirement for ATP in the second step (GMP synthetase) is the key cross-regulatory feature.
ATP is required for GMP synthesis; adenylosuccinate synthetase (for AMP synthesis) is inhibited by AMP and requires GTP, not ATP, for energy.
In the branching of IMP, ATP is specifically required for the synthesis of GMP. High ATP levels therefore promote the conversion of IMP toward GMP to balance the purine pool.
Purine and pyrimidine pathways are distinct; IMP is a purine intermediate and is not redirected into the de novo pyrimidine pathway.
High ATP signifies high energy and usually promotes biosynthetic pathways rather than triggering the degradation of essential nucleotide intermediates like IMP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: An 18-month-old male child is brought to the clinic for failure to thrive and severe anemia. Laboratory tests reveal a hemoglobin of 7 g/dL with increased mean corpuscular volume (MCV). Physical examination reveals developmental delay. Urinalysis shows significant crystalluria consisting of orotate. Despite treatment with Vitamin B12 and folate, the anemia persists. What is the most appropriate long-term therapeutic intervention?
options: Allopurinol
Weekly Hydroxyurea
Intravenous Arginine
Oral Uridine
Dietary protein restriction
correctOption: Oral Uridine
optionExplanations: Allopurinol is used to treat gout by inhibiting xanthine oxidase in the purine pathway; it has no role in treating pyrimidine synthesis defects.
Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and would further deplete deoxyribonucleotide pools, exacerbating the patient's anemia and DNA synthesis failure.
Arginine is useful in certain urea cycle defects to facilitate ammonia excretion, but it does not address the pyrimidine deficiency in UMP synthase deficiency.

Uridine is a pyrimidine nucleoside that can be salvaged into UMP by kinases, bypassing the defective UMP synthase enzyme, providing the necessary nucleotides and reducing orotic acid levels via feedback inhibition.
Protein restriction is a management strategy for hyperammonemia in urea cycle defects, but the persistence of megaloblastic anemia suggests a pyrimidine synthesis defect requiring replacement.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): Administration of uridine results in improvement of the anemia and decreased excretion of orotate. ... The salvage of pyrimidine nucleosides is the basis for using uridine in the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: A 10-month-old male infant presents with severe lethargy and failure to thrive. Laboratory evaluation reveals a profound megaloblastic anemia. Despite aggressive supplementation with Vitamin B12 and folic acid, the hematologic parameters fail to improve, and significant amounts of crystalline material are found in the urine. Which underlying biochemical defect is most likely?
options: Inhibition of Dihydrofolate reductase by methotrexate
Inherited deficiency of UMP synthase
Defect in the intestinal absorption of Vitamin B12
Complete deficiency of Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
Inability to oxidize hypoxanthine to xanthine
correctOption: Inherited deficiency of UMP synthase
optionExplanations: While methotrexate causes megaloblastic anemia, it would be secondary to drug exposure, not an inherited failure to thrive with orotic acid crystals.

Hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) causes megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to B12 or folate because the primary defect is a lack of pyrimidine nucleotides for DNA synthesis.
B12 absorption defects would cause megaloblastic anemia, but it would be corrected by parenteral B12 and would not present with orotic aciduria.
HGPRT deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, characterized by hyperuricemia and self-mutilation, not megaloblastic anemia.
The inability to oxidize hypoxanthine refers to xanthine oxidase deficiency, which leads to xanthinuria, not megaloblastic anemia or orotic aciduria.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in poor growth, megaloblastic anemia, and the excretion of large amounts of orotate in the urine.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
coreConcept: Clinical Diagnosis and Genetics of Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
statement: A 20-month-old male child is presented with delayed motor milestones and orange-colored sand-like crystals in his diaper. On physical examination, the child exhibits spasticity and choreoathetosis. The mother mentions he frequently bites his lower lip until it bleeds. Laboratory analysis shows a serum urate of 13.5 mg/dL and a significant increase in PRPP concentration in skin fibroblasts. What is the most likely mode of inheritance for this condition?
options: Autosomal dominant
X-linked recessive
Autosomal recessive
X-linked dominant
Mitochondrial inheritance
correctOption: X-linked recessive
optionExplanations: Autosomal dominant disorders typically appear in every generation and affect both sexes; Lesch-Nyhan is specific to males and requires two alleles for expression in females.
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder. The HGPRT gene is located on the X chromosome, so males (who have only one X) are affected, and females are usually asymptomatic carriers.
While many metabolic defects are autosomal recessive, Lesch-Nyhan is specifically linked to the X chromosome, explaining the male predominance.
In X-linked dominant inheritance, an affected male would pass the trait to all daughters and no sons; this does not match the pedigree of HGPRT deficiency.
Mitochondrial inheritance involves transmission only from the mother to all children; the nuclear location of the HGPRT gene precludes this pattern.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): This syndrome is a rare, X-linked, recessive disorder associated with a virtually complete deficiency of HGPRT.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 55-year-old male presents with excruciating pain and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Arthrocentesis is performed to obtain synovial fluid for analysis. Which of the following microscopic findings is considered the definitive diagnostic criterion for gout in this patient?
options: Elevated white blood cell count with predominant neutrophils
Identification of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposits
Presence of extracellular cholesterol clefts
Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals
Presence of rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals
correctOption: Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals
optionExplanations: While neutrophils are often present during an inflammatory response in gout, they are non-specific and can be seen in septic arthritis or other inflammatory conditions.
Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposits are the cause of pseudogout, which presents similarly to gout but is biochemically and crystallographically distinct.
Cholesterol clefts are typically found in atherosclerotic plaques or chronic inflammatory lesions, not in the acute synovial fluid of a gouty joint.
Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals of monosodium urate are the pathognomonic finding required for a definitive diagnosis of gout under polarized light microscopy.
Rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals are characteristic of pseudogout (calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease), not gout.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): The definitive diagnosis of gout requires aspiration and examination of synovial fluid (Figure 22.17) from an affected joint (or material from a tophus) using polarized light microscopy to confirm the presence of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals (Figure 22.18).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: In the salvage pathway of purine metabolism, the body reuses preformed bases to save energy. Which statement correctly contrasts the two primary salvage enzymes regarding their substrate specificity?
options: HGPRT is localized in the mitochondria while APRT is primarily a cytosolic enzyme.
APRT salvages hypoxanthine while HGPRT is specific only for adenine.
APRT produces nucleoside diphosphates while HGPRT produces nucleoside monophosphates.
HGPRT converts hypoxanthine and guanine to nucleotides, while APRT is specific for adenine.
APRT uses ribose 5-phosphate as a donor while HGPRT uses ATP directly.
correctOption: HGPRT converts hypoxanthine and guanine to nucleotides, while APRT is specific for adenine.
optionExplanations: Both salvage enzymes are primarily cytosolic enzymes; their localization is not a primary diagnostic contrast mentioned in the text.
This is reversed. HGPRT (Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase) salvages hypoxanthine and guanine, while APRT salvages adenine.
Both enzymes catalyze the formation of nucleoside monophosphates (NMPs) from a free base and PRPP.
Correct. HGPRT is responsible for salvaging the bases hypoxanthine (to IMP) and guanine (to GMP). APRT is responsible for adenine (to AMP).
Both enzymes use PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate) as the ribose 5-phosphate donor, not ATP or free ribose 5-phosphate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): Two enzymes are involved: adenine phosphoribosyltransferase ( APRT) and hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase ( HGPRT). ... [HGPRT deficiency] results in an inability to salvage hypoxanthine or guanine.
