citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The drug is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
coreConcept: Enzyme Tissue Distribution and Pathology Site
statement: In which of the following human tissues is the activity of the enzyme adenosine deaminase (ADA) naturally the highest?
options: Skeletal muscle myocytes
Lymphocytes
Mucosal cells of the small intestine
Hepatocytes of the liver
Renal tubular epithelial cells
correctOption: Lymphocytes
optionExplanations: Muscle has high turnover of ATP and uses enzymes like adenylate kinase and AMP deaminase, but it is not the primary site of ADA activity in the context of human pathology.
Lymphocytes have the highest ADA activity. This explains why ADA deficiency primarily manifests as a failure of the immune system (SCID) due to the localized toxicity in these cells.
Intestinal mucosal cells are active in degrading dietary nucleic acids to uric acid, but the text specifically highlights lymphocytes for ADA activity.
While the liver is a major site for de novo purine synthesis and some degradation, it does not possess the highest activity of ADA compared to lymphoid tissue.
Renal cells handle urate excretion and some metabolic tasks, but they are not the primary site of high ADA expression, which is concentrated in the lymphoid lineage.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): ADA is expressed in a variety of tissues, but, in humans, lymphocytes have the highest activity of this cytoplasmic enzyme.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: Which metabolic pathway is primarily served by the activity of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I)?
options: Pyrimidine de novo synthesis
Pentose phosphate pathway
Urea cycle
Heme biosynthesis
Purine de novo synthesis
correctOption: Urea cycle
optionExplanations: Pyrimidine de novo synthesis is the pathway for CPS II, not CPS I.
The pentose phosphate pathway produces ribose 5-phosphate and NADPH; it does not involve CPS enzymes.
CPS I is the entry point for nitrogen into the urea cycle, converting ammonia into carbamoyl phosphate within the mitochondria.
Heme biosynthesis starts with glycine and succinyl CoA (ALA synthase), not CPS I.
Purine synthesis starts with PRPP and glutamine via the amidotransferase enzyme, not CPS I.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [Figure 22.20 Summary of the differences between carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) I and II] Pathway involved: CPS I - Urea cycle; CPS II - Pyrimidine synthesis

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: In patients with Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the profound depletion of T, B, and Natural Killer cells is primarily attributed to the accumulation of dATP. What is the specific biochemical mechanism by which elevated dATP causes this cellular toxicity?
options: Direct competitive inhibition of DNA polymerase alpha
Induction of xanthine oxidase causing oxidative stress
Activation of 5'-nucleotidase leading to depletion of ATP pools
Feedback inhibition of PRPP amidotransferase leading to purine starvation
Inhibition of the activity sites of ribonucleotide reductase
correctOption: Inhibition of the activity sites of ribonucleotide reductase
optionExplanations: dATP does not primarily act by inhibiting DNA polymerase alpha; the metabolic bottleneck occurs much earlier in the synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides.
ADA deficiency leads to the accumulation of adenosine/dATP, not the activation of xanthine oxidase.
The toxicity is driven by the inability to produce deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs) for DNA replication, not by the depletion of the general energy currency (ATP) via 5'-nucleotidase.

While purine nucleotides inhibit PRPP amidotransferase, the specific pathology in ADA deficiency is the toxic accumulation of dATP and its effect on DNA synthesis substrates, not a lack of de novo purines.

dATP binds to the allosteric activity sites of ribonucleotide reductase, inhibiting the enzyme and preventing the reduction of all four ribonucleoside diphosphates into deoxyribonucleotides, which halts DNA synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): As dATP levels rise, ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited, thus preventing the production of all deoxyribose-containing nucleotides (see Page 289 (Book Page)). Consequently, cells cannot make DNA and divide.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: Unlike the purine ring, which is excreted as the relatively insoluble uric acid, the pyrimidine ring is catabolized into which highly soluble end products?
options: Urea and Creatinine
Xanthine and Guanosine
Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate
Ammonia and Orotic acid
Allantoin and Hypoxanthine
correctOption: Beta-alanine and Beta-aminoisobutyrate
optionExplanations: Urea is the end product of nitrogen metabolism from amino acids, and creatinine is a breakdown product of creatine phosphate; neither is the specific end product of the pyrimidine ring cleavage.
Xanthine and guanosine are intermediates of purine metabolism; purines are not cleaved into soluble products like beta-alanine in humans.
The pyrimidine ring is fully cleaved and degraded into soluble amino acids: beta-alanine (from uracil/cytosine) and beta-aminoisobutyrate (from thymine).
Ammonia is a byproduct of pyrimidine degradation, but orotic acid is a synthetic intermediate, not an end product of the catabolic pathway.
Allantoin is produced from uric acid in non-primate mammals (via urate oxidase), and hypoxanthine is a purine intermediate, not a pyrimidine degradation product.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Unlike the purine ring, which is not cleaved human cells, the pyrimidine ring is opened and degraded to highly soluble products, β -alanine and β -aminoisobutyrate, with the production of NH 3 and CO 2 .

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A clinician is deciding between allopurinol and uricosuric agents for the long-term management of a patient with chronic gout. How does the primary mechanism of allopurinol distinguish it from uricosuric agents like probenecid?
options: Allopurinol increases the solubility of uric acid in the renal tubules.
Allopurinol promotes the degradation of uric acid into allantoin.
Allopurinol specifically prevents the formation of microtubules in neutrophils.
Allopurinol acts by competitive inhibition of PRPP synthetase.
Allopurinol inhibits the synthesis of uric acid rather than its renal handling.
correctOption: Allopurinol inhibits the synthesis of uric acid rather than its renal handling.
optionExplanations: Allopurinol does not increase the solubility of uric acid itself; it leads to the accumulation of hypoxanthine and xanthine, which are naturally more soluble than uric acid.
Humans lack urate oxidase; therefore, we cannot convert uric acid to allantoin. Allopurinol inhibits production rather than enhancing degradation.
Colchicine, not allopurinol, prevents microtubule formation and neutrophil migration.

Allopurinol is a structural analog of hypoxanthine and targets xanthine oxidase; it does not directly inhibit PRPP synthetase as its primary clinical mechanism of action (though it may indirectly affect the pathway via salvage).

Uricosurics (probenecid) work by increasing the renal clearance (excretion) of uric acid. In contrast, allopurinol inhibits the enzyme xanthine oxidase, thereby reducing the actual production (synthesis) of uric acid.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): Uricosuric agents, such as probenecid or sulfinpyrazone, that increase renal excretion of uric acid, are used in patients who are “underexcretors” of uric acid. Allopurinol, a structural analog of hypoxanthine, inhibits uric acid synthesis and is used in patients who are “overproducers” of uric acid.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Mycophenolic acid is an important pharmacological agent used to prevent graft rejection in transplant patients. Through which specific mechanism does this drug achieve its immunosuppressive effect?
options: Direct incorporation into the DNA of T-cells as a guanine analog
Activation of Xanthine Oxidase to accelerate the degradation of purines
Irreversible inhibition of Ribonucleotide Reductase in bone marrow cells
Reversible, uncompetitive inhibition of Inosine Monophosphate Dehydrogenase
Competitive inhibition of Dihydrofolate Reductase, depleting THF stores
correctOption: Reversible, uncompetitive inhibition of Inosine Monophosphate Dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Mycophenolic acid is an enzyme inhibitor, not a nucleotide analog that gets incorporated into DNA (unlike 5-fluorouracil or certain purine analogs).
Accelerating xanthine oxidase would increase uric acid but would not prevent lymphocyte proliferation; mycophenolic acid blocks the synthesis of nucleotides, not their degradation.
Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase; mycophenolic acid targets a different enzyme in the purine pathway.
Correct. By inhibiting IMP dehydrogenase, mycophenolic acid prevents the conversion of IMP to XMP, thus blocking GMP synthesis. T and B cells are particularly dependent on this de novo pathway.
Methotrexate is the drug that competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The drug [Mycophenolic acid] is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase. The drug deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of key components of nucleic acids.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 2-year-old child presents with global developmental delay and recurrent infections. Laboratory analysis shows high levels of orotic acid in the urine. To differentiate between a defect in the urea cycle (Ornithine Transcarbamylase deficiency) and a defect in pyrimidine synthesis (UMP Synthase deficiency), which laboratory finding would most specifically indicate UMP Synthase deficiency?
options: Normal blood ammonia levels
Decreased levels of citrulline
Megaloblastic anemia
Presence of orotic acid in the urine
Elevated blood glutamine
correctOption: Megaloblastic anemia
optionExplanations: While normal ammonia points away from the urea cycle, it is a 'negative' finding. Megaloblastic anemia is a 'positive' diagnostic hallmark specific to the pyrimidine defect.
Decreased citrulline is seen in OTC deficiency, but it is not as direct a feature of pyrimidine synthesis defects as the hematological findings.
UMP synthase deficiency leads to a lack of pyrimidines for DNA synthesis in RBC precursors, causing megaloblastic anemia. OTC deficiency does not cause megaloblastic anemia.
Orotic aciduria occurs in both OTC deficiency (due to carbamoyl phosphate overflow) and UMP synthase deficiency.
Elevated glutamine is often associated with hyperammonemia in urea cycle defects, not specifically with UMP synthase deficiency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in poor growth, megaloblastic anemia, and the excretion of large amounts of orotate in the urine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is a hereditary disorder characterized by hyperuricemia and severe neurological symptoms. Which enzyme is virtually absent in patients with this syndrome?
options: Adenine phosphoribosyltransferase
Xanthine oxidase
Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
Adenosine deaminase
PRPP amidotransferase
correctOption: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
optionExplanations: Adenine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT) is involved in adenine salvage; its deficiency does not cause the neurological phenotype of Lesch-Nyhan.
Xanthine oxidase converts hypoxanthine to uric acid; its inhibition (not deficiency) is used as a treatment for the hyperuricemia found in Lesch-Nyhan patients.
HGPRT is the essential enzyme for salvaging hypoxanthine and guanine. Its absence leads to increased PRPP levels and increased de novo purine synthesis, resulting in massive uric acid production.
Adenosine deaminase deficiency leads to SCID, characterized by immune failure rather than the hyperuricemia and behavioral issues of Lesch-Nyhan.
PRPP amidotransferase is the regulated enzyme for de novo synthesis; its activity is actually increased in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome due to lack of feedback inhibition.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): This syndrome is a rare, X-linked, recessive disorder associated with a virtually complete deficiency of HGPRT. This deficiency results in an inability to salvage hypoxanthine or guanine.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: In mammalian metabolism, what is the primary regulated step in the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides, serving to control the flux of metabolites through the entire cytosolic pathway?
options: The conversion of orotate to OMP by orotate phosphoribosyltransferase.
The synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
The oxidation of dihydroorotate by dihydroorotate dehydrogenase.
The decarboxylation of OMP to UMP by orotidylate decarboxylase.
The formation of carbamoyl aspartate by aspartate transcarbamoylase.
correctOption: The synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
optionExplanations: The conversion of orotate to OMP is part of the second stage of the pathway but is not the initial regulated step.
In mammalian cells, the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine and CO2 by the cytosolic enzyme CPS II is the primary committed and regulated step of pyrimidine synthesis.
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is an important enzyme in the pathway, but it is not the primary site of feedback regulation by UTP or activation by PRPP.
The decarboxylation of OMP to UMP is catalyzed by UMP synthase, which is often deficient in orotic aciduria, but it is not the primary flux-controlling regulated step of the pathway.
While aspartate transcarbamoylase is the regulated step in prokaryotes, in mammals, it is the preceding step catalyzed by CPS II.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [VI. Pyrimidine Synthesis and Degradation] The regulated step of this pathway in mammalian cells is the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine and CO2, catalyzed by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) II.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: While most enzymes of the de novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway are located in the cytosol, one specific enzyme is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. What is the metabolic significance of this enzyme?
options: It oxidizes dihydroorotate to form orotic acid
It facilitates the attachment of the ribose 5-phosphate moiety from PRPP
It converts carbamoyl phosphate into carbamoyl aspartate
It catalyzes the regulated committed step of the pathway
It hydrolytically closes the open-chain ureidosuccinate ring
correctOption: It oxidizes dihydroorotate to form orotic acid
optionExplanations: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is the fourth enzyme in the pathway and is the only one located in the mitochondria, using FAD as a cofactor to produce orotate.
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase attaches the ribose moiety and is located in the cytosol.
The conversion to carbamoyl aspartate is done by aspartate transcarbamoylase, which is cytosolic.
The regulated step is catalyzed by CPS II, which is a cytosolic enzyme.
Dihydroorotase closes the ring and is a cytosolic enzyme (part of the CAD complex).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. All other enzymes in pyrimidine biosynthesis are cytosolic.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A researcher is studying the regulation of the committed step in purine synthesis. She observes that the rate of the reaction catalyzed by glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase increases significantly when the intracellular concentration of 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) rises. What is the biochemical basis for this observation?
options: The enzyme is only active when PRPP is covalently bound to the catalytic site
PRPP acts as a competitive inhibitor of the enzyme
The normal intracellular concentration of PRPP is well below the Km of the enzyme
PRPP induces the degradation of AMP and GMP to relieve feedback inhibition
PRPP increases the Vmax of the enzyme by three-fold
correctOption: The normal intracellular concentration of PRPP is well below the Km of the enzyme
optionExplanations: The enzyme does not require covalent modification by PRPP for activity; PRPP is a reactant that undergoes a displacement reaction with glutamine.
PRPP is a substrate, not an inhibitor; increasing its concentration drives the reaction forward rather than blocking it.

In metabolic pathways, if the substrate concentration is below the Michaelis constant (Km), the reaction rate is first-order with respect to that substrate. Thus, the enzyme is highly sensitive to fluctuations in PRPP availability.
While PRPP availability influences the pathway, it does not physically degrade existing nucleotides like AMP or GMP; those act as feedback inhibitors on the same enzyme.
The text states the rate change is proportional to concentration due to the Km relationship, not necessarily an alteration of the enzyme's maximum catalytic capacity (Vmax).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): The intracellular concentration of PRPP is normally far below the Km for the amidotransferase. Therefore, any small change in the PRPP concentration causes a proportional change in the rate of the reaction.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Regeneration of the reduced peptide coenzyme thioredoxin is essential for the continuous function of ribonucleotide reductase. Which enzyme is responsible for transferring electrons from NADPH + H+ to oxidized thioredoxin?
options: Thioredoxin reductase
Glutathione reductase
Ribonucleotide reductase itself
NADH dehydrogenase
Dihydrofolate reductase
correctOption: Thioredoxin reductase
optionExplanations: Correct. Thioredoxin reductase is a flavoenzyme that specifically uses NADPH to reduce the disulfide bond in oxidized thioredoxin, allowing thioredoxin to recycle and reduce ribonucleotide reductase.
Glutathione reductase reduces oxidized glutathione (GSSG) using NADPH. While similar in mechanism, it does not act on thioredoxin.
Ribonucleotide reductase is the enzyme that consumes the reduced thioredoxin; it cannot catalyze its own regeneration loop.
NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) is part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain and is not involved in the cytoplasmic reduction of thioredoxin.
Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) reduces dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate; it is targeted by methotrexate and is unrelated to the thioredoxin system.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): Thioredoxin must be converted back to its reduced form in order to continue to perform its function. The necessary reducing equivalents are provided by NADPH + H+, and the reaction is catalyzed by thioredoxin reductase.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: In the two-step conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) to adenosine monophosphate (AMP), what byproduct is released by the second enzyme, adenylosuccinate lyase?
options: Pyrophosphate (PPi)
CO2
Glutamate
NADH
Fumarate
correctOption: Fumarate
optionExplanations: Pyrophosphate is released during the synthesis of PRPP and the amidotransferase step, but not by adenylosuccinate lyase.
CO2 is released during OMP decarboxylation in pyrimidine synthesis, but not in the conversion of IMP to AMP.
Glutamate is a byproduct of the GMP synthetase reaction when glutamine is the nitrogen donor, not the AMP pathway.
NADH is a byproduct of the IMP dehydrogenase reaction in the GMP synthesis pathway, not the AMP pathway.
Adenylosuccinate lyase (also called adenylosuccinase) cleaves adenylosuccinate into AMP and fumarate. Fumarate is an intermediate of the TCA cycle.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Figure 22.8: Adenylosuccinate... Adenylosuccinase [to] Fumarate + AMP.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: A 4-day-old male neonate presents with severe lethargy, vomiting, and a rapidly declining level of consciousness. Laboratory investigations reveal a blood ammonia level of 600 µmol/L (normal <50 µmol/L) and markedly elevated urinary orotic acid. Given the link between the urea cycle and pyrimidine synthesis, which of the following enzymes is most likely defective?
options: Argininosuccinate lyase
Dihydroorotase
UMP synthase
Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II
Ornithine transcarbamylase
correctOption: Ornithine transcarbamylase
optionExplanations: While argininosuccinate lyase deficiency causes hyperammonemia, it does not typically cause the massive elevation of orotic acid seen in OTC deficiency because the metabolic block is further downstream in the cycle.
Dihydroorotase deficiency would prevent the formation of dihydroorotate and subsequent orotic acid, leading to a decrease in urinary orotate.
UMP synthase deficiency causes orotic aciduria but does not cause hyperammonemia, as the urea cycle remains intact.
Deficiency in CPS II would decrease orotic acid production, not increase it.

OTC deficiency leads to hyperammonemia (due to urea cycle failure) and orotic aciduria (due to carbamoyl phosphate overflow into the pyrimidine pathway). The combination of both is diagnostic for OTC deficiency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate. [Note: Explanation on Page 306 (Book Page) confirms ammonia distinguishes this from UMP synthase].

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A metabolic pathway requires the amination of Uridine Triphosphate (UTP) to form Cytidine Triphosphate (CTP). Which of the following molecules serves as the amide nitrogen donor in this specific reaction catalyzed by CTP synthetase?
options: Aspartic acid
Glycine
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Glutamine
Ammonium ion (NH4+)
correctOption: Glutamine
optionExplanations: Aspartic acid provides atoms for the pyrimidine ring (C4, C5, C6, and N1) but is not the nitrogen donor for the conversion of UTP to CTP.
Glycine provides a whole molecule to the purine ring (C4, C5, and N7) but does not participate in the synthesis or modification of pyrimidines.
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate is a one-carbon donor used in purine ring synthesis and the synthesis of thymidine, but not in the amination of UTP to CTP.
Glutamine serves as the amide nitrogen donor in several steps of nucleotide metabolism, including the first step of pyrimidine synthesis (CPS II) and the conversion of UTP to CTP.
Ammonium ion is the nitrogen source for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (the urea cycle enzyme), but CPS II and CTP synthetase both utilize the amide group of glutamine.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): CTP is produced by amination of UTP by CTP synthetase (Figure 22.22), with glutamine providing the nitrogen.

category: Interpret the role of PABA analogs and mycophenolic acid in purine biosynthesis
statement: Which specific enzyme in the de novo purine biosynthetic pathway is the primary pharmacological target of the drug mycophenolic acid?
options: Xanthine oxidase
Adenylosuccinate synthetase
PRPP synthetase
Glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase
Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
correctOption: Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Xanthine oxidase is involved in the degradation of purines to uric acid and is the target of allopurinol, not mycophenolic acid.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is the first step in the conversion of IMP to AMP (requiring GTP), whereas mycophenolic acid blocks the GMP-producing branch.
PRPP synthetase is responsible for the activation of ribose 5-phosphate to PRPP and is inhibited by purine nucleotides, but it is not the target of mycophenolic acid.
Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase catalyzes the committed step of purine synthesis and is inhibited by AMP and GMP, not mycophenolic acid.
Mycophenolic acid is a specific, reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase, which converts IMP to XMP in the pathway toward GMP synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The drug is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
coreConcept: Maintenance of DNA Integrity via dUTPase
statement: A deficit in the enzyme dUTP diphosphatase (dUTPase) would most likely lead to which of the following cellular consequences during DNA replication?
options: Accumulation of OMP due to feedback inhibition by dUTP.
The erroneous incorporation of uracil into the DNA strand.
Selective inhibition of the CAD complex by dUTP molecules.
Increased synthesis of dTMP from dUMP via thymidylate synthase.
Decreased availability of NADPH for ribonucleotide reductase.
correctOption: The erroneous incorporation of uracil into the DNA strand.
optionExplanations: OMP is an upstream intermediate in pyrimidine synthesis and is not directly inhibited by dUTP levels.
dUTPase hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP. If dUTP levels rise, DNA polymerase may mistakenly use dUTP instead of dTTP, placing uracil in DNA.
The CAD complex is regulated by UTP and PRPP, not dUTP.
Thymidylate synthase utilizes dUMP, not dUTP; dUTPase actually provides dUMP for dTMP synthesis.
dUTPase does not consume or regulate NADPH; NADPH is used by thioredoxin reductase to regenerate ribonucleotide reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): dUTPase, then, plays an important role in reducing availability of dUTP as a substrate for DNA synthesis, thus preventing erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: An infant is evaluated for failure to thrive and hyperammonemia. Laboratory tests reveal significantly elevated levels of orotic acid in the urine. Biochemical analysis suggests that a mitochondrial enzyme deficiency has led to the leakage of an intermediate into the cytosol, where it is consumed by the pyrimidine pathway. Which enzyme deficiency most likely explains the secondary activation of the cytosolic pyrimidine pathway?
options: UMP synthase
Ornithine transcarbamylase
Argininosuccinate synthetase
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I
correctOption: Ornithine transcarbamylase
optionExplanations: UMP synthase deficiency causes primary orotic aciduria, but it presents with megaloblastic anemia and *without* hyperammonemia.

In Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency, mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate (produced by CPS I) accumulates and leaks into the cytosol, where it is utilized by CPS II-bypassing steps of the pyrimidine pathway, causing orotic aciduria.
Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency causes citrullinemia but does not typically cause the massive shift of carbamoyl phosphate to the pyrimidine pathway seen in OTC deficiency.
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase deficiency is not a standard cause of the clinical combination of hyperammonemia and orotic aciduria.
CPS I deficiency would result in low levels of carbamoyl phosphate, which would not lead to an increase in orotic acid synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A researcher observes that following the administration of Methotrexate to a cell culture, there is a rapid shift in the ratio of folate derivatives. Which of the following best describes this metabolic shift?
options: The concentration of Tetrahydrofolate (THF) increases significantly.
Folic acid is converted directly to dTMP, bypassing the enzyme block.
Dihydrofolate (DHF) accumulates because it cannot be reduced to THF.
The concentration of N5,N10-Methylene THF accumulates to toxic levels.
The levels of PRPP decrease as they are consumed by the accumulating DHF.
correctOption: Dihydrofolate (DHF) accumulates because it cannot be reduced to THF.
optionExplanations: THF levels decrease because the enzyme responsible for its production from DHF (dihydrofolate reductase) is blocked by Methotrexate.
Folic acid cannot be converted to dTMP; it must be reduced to THF to serve as a carrier for the carbon unit required for dTMP synthesis.

In the thymidylate synthase reaction, THF is oxidized to DHF. Normally, DHF is reduced back to THF by DHFR. When Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, the DHF cannot be recycled, leading to its accumulation and a depletion of the functional THF pool.
N5,N10-Methylene THF levels drop because it is synthesized from THF, which is no longer being produced or recycled.
PRPP levels do not decrease due to DHF; PRPP levels generally increase in these states because purine synthesis is stalled and cannot utilize the PRPP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): [DHF can be reduced to THF by dihydrofolate reductase... an enzyme that is inhibited by drugs such as methotrexate. By decreasing the supply of THF, these folate analogs not only inhibit purine synthesis... but, by preventing methylation of dUMP to dTMP, they also lower the cellular concentration of this essential component of DNA.]

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which of the following compounds contributes the nitrogen atoms at positions 3 and 9 during the assembly of the purine ring structure?
options: Aspartate
Carbon dioxide
Glutamine
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Glycine
correctOption: Glutamine
optionExplanations: Aspartate contributes only a single nitrogen atom to the purine ring at position 1.
Carbon dioxide (CO2) provides only the carbon atom at position 6 of the purine ring.
Glutamine is the specific amide donor for the nitrogen atoms at both position 3 and position 9 of the purine ring.
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate provides the carbon atoms at positions 2 and 8 via one-carbon transfer reactions.
Glycine is a major donor, contributing carbons 4 and 5 as well as the nitrogen at position 7, but not at 3 or 9.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): The atoms of the purine ring are contributed by a number of compounds, including amino acids (aspartic acid, glycine, and glutamine), CO2, and N10–formyltetrahydrofolate (Figure 22.5).

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: A researcher is studying the subcellular compartmentalization of nucleotide metabolism. Which specific location is the site of action for the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis in human hepatocytes?
options: Cytosol
Endoplasmic reticulum
Nucleolus
Mitochondrial matrix
Inner mitochondrial membrane
correctOption: Cytosol
optionExplanations: Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) is the regulated, rate-limiting enzyme for pyrimidine synthesis and is located strictly in the cytosol of mammalian cells.
The endoplasmic reticulum is involved in protein folding and lipid synthesis, but not the cytosolic steps of nucleotide production.
The nucleolus is primarily involved in ribosome biogenesis and rRNA synthesis; it does not host the de novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway.
The mitochondrial matrix is the site for Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I (CPS I), which is involved in the urea cycle, not the rate-limiting step of pyrimidine synthesis.
While dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane, the rate-limiting enzyme CPS II is found in the cytosol.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): CPS II | Cellular location | Cytosol

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A clinician is examining a 2-year-old male with persistent hyperuricemia. To confirm a diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome rather than primary gout, the presence of which hallmark clinical sign is most critical?
options: Recurrent episodes of acute arthritic joint inflammation
Formation of monosodium urate crystals in the joints
Compulsive self-mutilation involving the lips and fingers
Development of uric acid stones in the kidney (urolithiasis)
High levels of uric acid in the serum and urine
correctOption: Compulsive self-mutilation involving the lips and fingers
optionExplanations: Acute arthritis joint inflammation is the primary symptom of gout; while it occurs in Lesch-Nyhan, it is also the defining feature of common primary gout.
Joint crystals are a common feature of all forms of gout and are not specific enough to distinguish Lesch-Nyhan from other causes of hyperuricemia.
Compulsive self-mutilation, specifically biting of the lips and fingers, is a unique behavioral hallmark of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and distinguishes it from other forms of hyperuricemia.
Urolithiasis is a complication of high uric acid levels regardless of the cause (overproduction or underexcretion) and is not diagnostic for HGPRT deficiency alone.
Hyperuricemia is the biochemical finding in both Lesch-Nyhan and gout; thus, it is not the distinguishing clinical feature for the syndrome's unique neurological component.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): [In addition, the syndrome is characterized by motor dysfunction, cognitive deficits, and behavioral disturbances that include self-mutilation (biting of lips and fingers, Figure 22.11).]

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
coreConcept: Differential Regulation of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetases
statement: How does the regulation of mammalian Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II) differ from that of CPS I?
options: CPS II is cytosolic and inhibited by UTP
CPS II is cytosolic and activated by inorganic phosphate
CPS II is mitochondrial and activated by N-acetylglutamate
CPS II is activated by ammonia and inhibited by glutamine
CPS II is mitochondrial and inhibited by UTP
correctOption: CPS II is cytosolic and inhibited by UTP
optionExplanations: CPS II is the cytosolic, rate-limiting enzyme for pyrimidine synthesis; it is feedback-inhibited by UTP and activated by the purine intermediate PRPP.
CPS II is cytosolic, but its primary activator is PRPP, not inorganic phosphate (which activates PRPP synthetase).
This describes CPS I, which is involved in the urea cycle and requires N-acetylglutamate as an essential activator.
CPS I utilizes ammonia as a nitrogen source, whereas CPS II utilizes the gamma-amide group of glutamine.
CPS II is not mitochondrial; the mitochondrial enzyme for the urea cycle is CPS I.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): CPS II is inhibited by UTP (the end product of this pathway, which can be converted into the other pyrimidine nucleotides), and is activated by PRPP. [Note: Carbamoyl phosphate, synthesized by CPS I, is also a precursor of urea... CPS I location: Mitochondria; CPS II location: Cytosol].

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: Methotrexate is a potent anticancer drug that acts as a structural analog of folic acid. Which specific step in the folate cycle does it inhibit, leading to a secondary deficiency of tetrahydrofolate?
options: Methylation of dUMP by thymidylate synthase
Transfer of formyl groups by formyltransferase
Conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate
Oxidation of NADPH during purine ring closure
Synthesis of N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate from THF
correctOption: Conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate
optionExplanations: Thymidylate synthase uses methylene-THF as a substrate; while methotrexate stops this reaction indirectly by depleting THF, it does not inhibit the enzyme itself.
Formyltransferase requires N10-formyl-THF; methotrexate limits the availability of this coenzyme but does not inhibit the transferase enzyme directly.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), the enzyme responsible for reducing dihydrofolate (DHF) to the active tetrahydrofolate (THF).
Methotrexate does not target NADPH oxidation in purine synthesis; it targets the reduction of DHF.
This step involves serine hydroxymethyltransferase; methotrexate does not directly inhibit this enzyme but limits its substrate availability by depleting the THF pool.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): DHF can be reduced to THF by dihydrofolate reductase (see Figure 28.3, Page 366 (Book Page)), an enzyme that is inhibited by drugs such as methotrexate.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Substrate specificity of ribonucleotide reductase is regulated by the binding of nucleoside triphosphates to specific allosteric sites. Binding of which molecule at these sites specifically promotes the reduction of GDP to dGDP?
options: dCTP
dGTP
dTTP
dATP
UTP
correctOption: dTTP
optionExplanations: dCTP is not cited in the text as the primary specificity regulator for the GDP-to-dGDP transition.
dGTP binding regulates the reduction of other nucleotides and generally provides feedback rather than promoting its own precursor's reduction.
The text provides the specific example that dTTP binding at the substrate specificity sites induces a conformation that favors the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
Binding of dATP at the activity site is inhibitory; at specificity sites, it has different effects than promoting GDP reduction.
UTP is a substrate for the pathway but it is the triphosphates of deoxyribonucleotides (like dTTP) that typically act as specificity regulators.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): For example, deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) binding at the specificity sites causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP to dGDP at the catalytic site.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: The de novo pathway for purine synthesis is regulated by feedback inhibition at the conversion of IMP to its derivatives. Which of the following correctly matches the enzyme with its inhibitory end-product?
options: Adenylosuccinate lyase is inhibited by GTP.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is inhibited by AMP.
IMP dehydrogenase is inhibited by AMP.
GMP synthetase is inhibited by IMP.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is inhibited by GMP.
correctOption: Adenylosuccinate synthetase is inhibited by AMP.
optionExplanations: Adenylosuccinate lyase is the second step of AMP synthesis; regulation primarily occurs at the initial synthetase step by AMP, and GTP actually acts as a substrate/activator for the branch, not an inhibitor here.
Correct. The first reaction in the synthesis of AMP from IMP (catalyzed by adenylosuccinate synthetase) is specifically inhibited by AMP to prevent overproduction.
IMP dehydrogenase is the first step in the GMP branch and is inhibited by GMP, not AMP.
GMP synthetase is the second step in the GMP branch; inhibition primarily occurs at the first step (IMP dehydrogenase) by GMP.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is the first step in the AMP branch and is inhibited by AMP, not GMP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Also, the first reaction in each pathway is inhibited by the end product of that pathway. [Figure 22.8 shows AMP inhibiting Adenylosuccinate synthetase].

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: A research scientist is studying the 'suicide inhibition' of thymidylate synthase. Which biochemical event best explains why 5-fluorouracil is classified as such an inhibitor?
options: It destroys the essential free radical required for the enzyme's catalytic activity.
It directly degrades the tetrahydrofolate coenzyme needed for the reaction.
It prevents the amination of UTP to CTP, halting pyrimidine interconversion.
It competitively binds to the N5, N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate binding site.
It is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which permanently binds to the enzyme.
correctOption: It is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which permanently binds to the enzyme.
optionExplanations: Destroying the free radical is the mechanism of action for hydroxyurea on ribonucleotide reductase, not 5-fluorouracil on thymidylate synthase.
The drug does not degrade tetrahydrofolate; rather, it prevents thymidylate synthase from utilizing the methylene-THF donor for dTMP synthesis.
CTP synthetase, which converts UTP to CTP, is not the target of 5-fluorouracil.
While 5-fluorouracil affects the pathway involving folate, it does not act as a simple competitor for the folate binding site; its efficacy relies on its conversion to 5-FdUMP.
5-fluorouracil must be converted to 5-FdUMP, which forms a covalent, irreversible bond with thymidylate synthase, effectively 'killing' the enzyme's activity permanently.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a “suicide” inhibitor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Unlike the purine ring, which remains intact and is excreted as uric acid, the pyrimidine ring is extensively degraded in humans. What are the primary highly soluble end-products of pyrimidine catabolism?
options: Beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate
Xanthine and hypoxanthine
Orotic acid and carbamoyl phosphate
Urea and ammonia
Uric acid and allantoin
correctOption: Beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate
optionExplanations: The pyrimidine ring is cleaved and reduced. Cytosine and uracil are degraded to beta-alanine, while thymine is degraded to beta-aminoisobutyrate. Both are highly soluble and easily excreted.
Xanthine and hypoxanthine are intermediates in the purine degradation pathway, eventually leading to uric acid.
Orotic acid and carbamoyl phosphate are intermediates in the synthesis (anabolism) of pyrimidines, not the degradation (catabolism) products.
While ammonia (NH3) is a byproduct of pyrimidine degradation, it is not the primary organic end-product of the ring itself. Urea is the product of the urea cycle for nitrogen disposal.
Uric acid is the end product of purine degradation in humans. Allantoin is produced from uric acid in other mammals by urate oxidase, but not in humans.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Unlike the purine ring, which is not cleaved human cells, the pyrimidine ring is opened and degraded to highly soluble products, beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate, with the production of NH3 and CO2.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: What is the primary allosteric inhibitor of the regulated step in the de novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway in human cells?
options: IMP
CTP
ATP
UTP
PRPP
correctOption: UTP
optionExplanations: Inosine monophosphate (IMP) is the parent purine nucleotide and does not regulate the pyrimidine synthetic pathway.
While CTP inhibits aspartate transcarbamoylase in prokaryotic cells, in human (mammalian) cells, the regulated step is CPS II, which is inhibited by UTP.
ATP acts as an activator for various steps in nucleotide synthesis but is not the specific allosteric inhibitor of the regulated step in human pyrimidine synthesis (CPS II).
UTP is the end product of the pyrimidine pathway and provides negative feedback by inhibiting CPS II, the rate-limiting step in mammalian cells.
PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate) is an allosteric activator of Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase II (CPS II), not an inhibitor.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): CPS II is inhibited by UTP (the end product of this pathway, which can be converted into the other pyrimidine nucleotides), and is activated by PRPP.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
coreConcept: Mechanism of dATP Toxicity in ADA Deficiency
statement: A patient with Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency suffers from severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). The underlying biochemical toxicity is caused by the accumulation of dATP, which directly inhibits which site of ribonucleotide reductase?
options: The activity site on the R1 subunit
The thioredoxin binding site on the R1 subunit
The free radical site on the R2 subunit
The catalytic site on the R2 subunit
The substrate specificity site on the R2 subunit
correctOption: The activity site on the R1 subunit
optionExplanations: The activity site, located on the R1 subunit, is the master switch for the enzyme; binding of dATP here causes a global inhibition of the reduction of all four NDPs.
dATP does not interfere with the binding of the thioredoxin coenzyme; its inhibitory effect is a conformational change that prevents the catalytic turnover of the enzyme.
Hydroxyurea targets the free radical site on the R2 subunit; dATP targets the allosteric regulatory site on the R1 subunit.
The catalytic site is where the substrate binds, but dATP acts as an allosteric inhibitor at a distinct regulatory site, not as a competitive inhibitor at the catalytic site.
The substrate specificity sites regulate which nucleotide is reduced, but the toxic inhibition by dATP is mediated through the general 'activity site' that shuts down the entire enzyme.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 289 (Book Page): The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme and, therefore, prevents the reduction of any of the four nucleoside diphosphates.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: The balanced production of the four different deoxyribonucleotides is critical for genomic stability. How does the binding of deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) to the substrate specificity site influence the activity of Ribonucleotide Reductase?
options: It facilitates the phosphorylation of dUMP to dTMP.
It acts as a required co-activator for the R2 subunit's free radical.
It inhibits the reduction of all four ribonucleoside diphosphates.
It prevents the conversion of ADP to dADP.
It stimulates the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
correctOption: It stimulates the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
optionExplanations: The conversion of dUMP to dTMP is catalyzed by Thymidylate Synthase, an entirely different enzyme that is not part of the Ribonucleotide Reductase complex.
The R2 subunit's free radical is generated by a binuclear iron center and is a structural/catalytic feature, not something that requires dTTP for its existence.
Inhibition of all four substrates is the role of the Activity Site when bound by dATP, not the substrate specificity site's role in fine-tuning specific nucleotide ratios.
The regulation by dTTP specifically targets the purine GDP; the text does not cite it as the primary mechanism for preventing ADP reduction in this specific cross-regulatory loop.

Binding of dTTP to the substrate specificity site induces a conformational change that specifically enhances the enzyme's affinity for GDP, promoting its reduction to dGDP to ensure balanced purine/pyrimidine pools.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): For example, deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) binding at the specificity sites causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP to dGDP at the catalytic site.

category: Interpret the role of PABA analogs and mycophenolic acid in purine biosynthesis
statement: Mycophenolic acid is particularly effective at depriving T and B cells of nucleic acid components compared to other tissues. What metabolic characteristic of these lymphocytes is exploited by this drug?
options: They cannot utilize dietary folic acid for the synthesis of tetrahydrofolate
They have a uniquely high rate of purine degradation to uric acid
They are exceptionally dependent on the de novo pathway for purine nucleotides during proliferation
They lack the enzyme HGPRT required for the purine salvage pathway
They possess an isoform of IMP dehydrogenase that is insensitive to feedback by GMP
correctOption: They are exceptionally dependent on the de novo pathway for purine nucleotides during proliferation
optionExplanations: All human cells utilize dietary folic acid; this is the basis for sulfonamide selectivity in bacteria, not mycophenolic acid selectivity in humans.
Purine degradation to uric acid occurs primarily in the liver and intestinal mucosa; T and B cell susceptibility is related to synthesis, not degradation.
Rapidly proliferating T and B cells rely heavily on the de novo synthesis of purines. By blocking IMP dehydrogenase, mycophenolic acid prevents them from producing enough GMP for DNA replication.
Lymphocytes do possess HGPRT; however, during rapid proliferation, the salvage pathway is insufficient to meet their nucleotide demands, making them dependent on de novo synthesis.
The drug inhibits IMP dehydrogenase regardless of the isoform's sensitivity to GMP; the selectivity arises from the cell's reliance on the pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): [The drug deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of key components of nucleic acids. ... is an immunosuppressant used to prevent graft rejection.]

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: Allopurinol reduces uric acid levels in 'overproducers' by inhibiting xanthine oxidase. However, it also reduces de novo purine synthesis indirectly. This secondary regulatory effect is only possible if which of the following is present?
options: Active Adenosine Deaminase (ADA).
A deficiency in UMP synthase.
Functional hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).
High levels of PRPP synthetase activity.
Inhibition of the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
correctOption: Functional hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).
optionExplanations: ADA is involved in the conversion of adenosine to inosine. While important for purine degradation, its presence is not the specific requirement for the allopurinol-salvage-feedback loop.
UMP synthase is part of the pyrimidine pathway; its status does not directly affect the salvage of purines via the HGPRT/Allopurinol mechanism.

Correct. If HGPRT is functional, the accumulated hypoxanthine (resulting from xanthine oxidase inhibition) can be salvaged. This salvage consumes PRPP and produces IMP/GMP, which inhibits the committed step of de novo synthesis.
Increasing PRPP synthetase activity would increase purine synthesis, opposing the therapeutic goal.
Mitochondrial inhibition is unrelated to the salvage pathway of purine bases in the cytosol.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
coreConcept: Urea Cycle and Pyrimidine Synthesis Crossover
statement: A patient with a urea cycle defect involving ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency is found to have significantly elevated levels of urinary orotic acid. What is the precise metabolic mechanism responsible for this increase in pyrimidine intermediates?
options: Low levels of CO2 in the mitochondria shift the equilibrium towards cytosolic carbamoyl phosphate synthesis.
Increased hepatic levels of PRPP stimulate the carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II enzyme.
Accumulation of ornithine directly inhibits the enzyme UMP synthase.
A deficiency in ATP prevents the condensation of aspartate with carbamoyl phosphate.
Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytosol and bypasses the regulated CPS II step.
correctOption: Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytosol and bypasses the regulated CPS II step.
optionExplanations: The mechanism is not based on CO2 equilibrium but on the physical movement of the carbamoyl phosphate molecule from the mitochondrial compartment to the cytosolic compartment due to a metabolic block in the urea cycle.
While PRPP is an activator of CPS II, the primary driver in OTC deficiency is the overflow of pre-formed carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondria, not de novo activation of CPS II.
Ornithine does not inhibit UMP synthase; it is a substrate for OTC. Its accumulation is not the direct cause of orotic aciduria.
ATP deficiency would typically slow down synthesis; however, in this case, the pathway is over-stimulated by the abundance of the intermediate carbamoyl phosphate.

Correct. In OTC deficiency, carbamoyl phosphate (CP) produced by CPS I in the mitochondria cannot be utilized for the urea cycle. This excess CP leaks into the cytosol, where it enters the pyrimidine pathway, bypassing the rate-limiting CPS II step and driving the production of orotic acid.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Which of the following classes of compounds serves as the direct substrate for the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase in the production of deoxyribonucleotides?
options: Ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs)
Ribonucleoside monophosphates (NMPs)
Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs)
Ribonucleoside triphosphates (NTPs)
Deoxyribonucleoside monophosphates (dNMPs)
correctOption: Ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs)
optionExplanations: Ribonucleotide reductase specifically acts on ribonucleoside diphosphates (ADP, GDP, CDP, and UDP) to reduce the 2'-hydroxyl group, forming dADP, dGDP, dCDP, and dUDP respectively.
Ribonucleoside monophosphates (NMPs) are not the substrates for ribonucleotide reductase; they must first be phosphorylated to diphosphates by base-specific kinases before they can be reduced.
Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) are the final products used in DNA synthesis and act as allosteric regulators of ribonucleotide reductase, rather than being substrates themselves.
Ribonucleoside triphosphates (NTPs) like ATP or GTP are not substrates for the reduction reaction; however, they can act as allosteric regulators at the activity or specificity sites.
Deoxyribonucleoside monophosphates (dNMPs) are products further down the line (after dephosphorylation of dNDPs) and do not serve as substrates for the initial reduction of the ribose ring.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): Ribonucleotide reductase (ribonucleoside diphosphate reductase) is composed of two nonidentical dimeric subunits, R1 and R2, and is specific for the reduction of purine nucleoside diphosphates (ADP and GDP), and pyrimidine nucleoside diphosphates, cytidine diphosphate (CDP) and uridine diphosphate (UDP) to their deoxy-forms (dADP, dGDP, dCDP, and dUDP).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Role of dUTPase in DNA Integrity
statement: In the physiological maintenance of DNA integrity, the cell utilizes the enzyme dUTP diphosphatase (dUTPase). What is the primary functional significance of this metabolic step in pyrimidine metabolism?
options: To promote the degradation of thymine to beta-aminoisobutyrate
To bypass the regulatory inhibition of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
To ensure dUMP is available for conversion to dTMP and prevent uracil incorporation into DNA
To maximize the availability of dUTP for DNA polymerase
To facilitate the salvage of uracil from dietary sources
correctOption: To ensure dUMP is available for conversion to dTMP and prevent uracil incorporation into DNA
optionExplanations: The degradation of thymine occurs through the catabolic pathway; dUTPase is an anabolic processing enzyme that handles uracil-containing deoxyribonucleotides.
CPS II regulation is managed by PRPP and UTP; dUTPase is a downstream enzyme involved in deoxyribonucleotide processing and has no effect on the rate-limiting CPS II step.

dUTPase hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP. This serves two purposes: it prevents dUTP from being mistakenly incorporated into DNA (which would place uracil in DNA), and it provides dUMP, the substrate for dTMP synthesis.
The goal of dUTPase is the opposite; it minimizes the availability of dUTP so that DNA polymerase does not use it in place of dTTP.
The salvage of uracil is minimal in human cells; dUTPase is part of the de novo synthesis sequence and not involved in base salvage pathways.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): dUTPase, then, plays an important role in reducing availability of dUTP as a substrate for DNA synthesis, thus preventing erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: In the regulated step of de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis within mammalian cells, what specific molecule serves as the primary source of nitrogen for the reaction catalyzed by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II)?
options: N-acetylglutamate
Aspartic acid
Free ammonium ions (NH4+)
The gamma-amide group of glutamine
Urea
correctOption: The gamma-amide group of glutamine
optionExplanations: N-acetylglutamate is an allosteric activator of CPS I, not a nitrogen donor or a regulator of CPS II.
Aspartic acid provides three carbons and one nitrogen to the pyrimidine ring later in the pathway, but it is not the nitrogen donor for the initial carbamoyl phosphate synthesis step.
Free ammonium ions are the nitrogen source for CPS I in the mitochondria for the urea cycle, not CPS II in the cytosol.
CPS II specifically utilizes the amide group of glutamine as its nitrogen source, which distinguishes it from the ammonia-dependent CPS I.
Urea is an end product of the urea cycle and does not serve as a nitrogen donor for the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [CPS II] Source of nitrogen: γ-Amide group of glutamine.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
coreConcept: Cell Cycle Specificity of Nucleotide Metabolism
statement: The conversion of ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates is a critical rate-limiting step in cell division. During which phase of the cell cycle is the activity of ribonucleotide reductase most significantly expressed?
options: G0 phase
S-phase
M-phase
G2 phase
G1 phase
correctOption: S-phase
optionExplanations: G0 is a quiescent phase where the cell is not preparing for division; therefore, the machinery for DNA precursor synthesis like RNR is inactive.
The S-phase (synthesis phase) is when DNA replication occurs. Ribonucleotide reductase activity peaks during this phase to provide the dNTPs necessary for DNA polymerase.
The M-phase involves chromosomal segregation and cytokinesis; the metabolic synthesis of DNA precursors is completed before this phase starts.
G2 is the post-synthetic gap phase. By this point, DNA replication is complete, and the demand for deoxyribonucleotides produced by RNR decreases.
G1 is a growth phase. While preparations for DNA synthesis begin here, the peak activity and requirement for RNR occur when DNA replication actually begins.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): which are produced from ribonucleoside diphosphates by the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase during the S-phase of the cell cycle

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: Which of the following enzymes is responsible for the final two oxidation steps in the degradation of purines into uric acid in humans?
options: AMP deaminase
Xanthine oxidase
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase
Adenosine deaminase
Guanase
correctOption: Xanthine oxidase
optionExplanations: AMP deaminase converts AMP to IMP, a very early step in the degradative pathway.
Xanthine oxidase is the key enzyme that catalyzes both the oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid.
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) cleaves nucleosides into free bases and ribose-1-phosphate, upstream of the final oxidation steps.
Adenosine deaminase converts adenosine to inosine; it does not produce uric acid.
Guanase (guanine deaminase) converts guanine to xanthine, but the subsequent conversion to uric acid requires xanthine oxidase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): [[5] Hypoxanthine is oxidized by xanthine oxidase to xanthine, which is further oxidized by xanthine oxidase to uric acid, the final product of human purine degradation.]

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: To maintain a continuous supply of deoxyribonucleotides, the oxidized Ribonucleotide Reductase must be regenerated. Which molecule acts as the terminal electron donor in this metabolic loop, providing reducing equivalents to thioredoxin?
options: Glutathione
FADH2
NADH
Ascorbic acid
NADPH
correctOption: NADPH
optionExplanations: Glutathione is a major cellular antioxidant, but the specific regeneration pathway for Ribonucleotide Reductase explicitly utilizes the thioredoxin/thioredoxin reductase system driven by NADPH.
FADH2 is a common electron carrier in the respiratory chain and some metabolic steps, but it is not the direct donor for the thioredoxin system involved in DNA precursor synthesis.
NADH is primarily utilized in catabolic pathways for ATP production via oxidative phosphorylation, whereas NADPH is preferred for reductive biosynthetic pathways like deoxyribonucleotide formation.
Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) functions as a cofactor for certain hydroxylases and an antioxidant, but it does not participate in the specialized redox cycle of ribonucleotide reduction.

NADPH provides the high-energy electrons necessary to reduce the disulfide bond in oxidized thioredoxin, a reaction catalyzed by thioredoxin reductase, allowing thioredoxin to then regenerate Ribonucleotide Reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The necessary reducing equivalents are provided by NADPH + H + , and the reaction is catalyzed by thioredoxin reductase.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Which molecule serves as the source of the high-energy phosphate group used by nucleoside monophosphate kinases to convert GMP to GDP?
options: Phosphoenolpyruvate
ATP
Creatine phosphate
GTP
UTP
correctOption: ATP
optionExplanations: Phosphoenolpyruvate is a high-energy intermediate of glycolysis used to generate ATP, but it is not the direct substrate for nucleoside monophosphate kinases.
ATP is the most abundant nucleoside triphosphate and serves as the universal phosphate donor for base-specific nucleoside monophosphate kinases like guanylate kinase.
Creatine phosphate is used to regenerate ATP from ADP in muscle, but it does not directly donate phosphate to GMP in this kinase reaction.
While GTP is an energy currency, it is generally not the primary phosphate donor for the monophosphate kinases.
UTP is a pyrimidine triphosphate and is not the standard donor for the phosphorylation of purine monophosphates.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): ATP is generally the source of the transferred phosphate, because it is present in higher concentrations than the other nucleoside triphosphates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: To prevent the erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA, the cell maintains a very low concentration of dUTP. This is achieved through the action of which enzyme?
options: Orotidylate decarboxylase
dUTP diphosphatase (dUTPase)
Ribonucleotide reductase
Thymidylate synthase
CTP synthetase
correctOption: dUTP diphosphatase (dUTPase)
optionExplanations: Orotidylate decarboxylase is involved in the de novo synthesis of UMP from OMP, much earlier in the pathway.
Correct. dUTPase hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP, keeping dUTP levels low and providing the substrate for dTMP synthesis.
Ribonucleotide reductase produces dUDP from UDP, but it does not directly eliminate dUTP.
Thymidylate synthase uses dUMP (the product of dUTPase) to make dTMP.
CTP synthetase converts UTP to CTP; it does not handle dUTP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): The dUDP is phosphorylated to dUTP, which is rapidly hydrolyzed to dUMP by UTP diphosphatase (dUTPase). dUTPase, then, plays an important role in reducing availability of dUTP as a substrate for DNA synthesis, thus preventing erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: Unlike the purine ring, which remains intact during human catabolism, the pyrimidine ring is cleaved into highly soluble products. Which of the following is a specific end product of pyrimidine degradation?
options: Urea
Allantoin
Xanthine
Beta-aminoisobutyrate
Uric acid
correctOption: Beta-aminoisobutyrate
optionExplanations: While NH3 produced during pyrimidine degradation may enter the urea cycle, urea itself is not a direct structural degradation product of the pyrimidine ring.
Allantoin is the degradation product of purines in non-primate mammals that possess urate oxidase.
Xanthine is an intermediate in the purine degradation pathway leading to uric acid.
Beta-aminoisobutyrate (along with beta-alanine) is one of the two specific, highly soluble products of pyrimidine ring cleavage and degradation in humans.
Uric acid is the end product of purine degradation in humans, not pyrimidines.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Unlike the purine ring, which is not cleaved [in] human cells, the pyrimidine ring is opened and degraded to highly soluble products, β-alanine and β-aminoisobutyrate, with the production of NH3 and CO2.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A 55-year-old patient with colorectal cancer is prescribed 5-fluorouracil. This drug achieves its antineoplastic effect by being metabolically activated to a compound that covalently binds to its target enzyme. What is the specific mechanism of this inhibition?
options: Allosteric inhibition of PRPP amidotransferase.
Competitive inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase.
Destruction of the free radical on ribonucleotide reductase.
Reversible inhibition of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.
Suicide inhibition of thymidylate synthase.
correctOption: Suicide inhibition of thymidylate synthase.
optionExplanations: Purine nucleotides (AMP/GMP) allosterically inhibit PRPP amidotransferase. 5-fluorouracil targets the pyrimidine pathway specifically at the level of dTMP production.
Methotrexate, not 5-fluorouracil, is the competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase, which prevents the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate.
Hydroxyurea is the drug that destroys the free radical required for the activity of ribonucleotide reductase, thereby inhibiting DNA substrate generation.
Mycophenolic acid is a reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase, used primarily as an immunosuppressant to prevent graft rejection.
5-fluorouracil is a pyrimidine analog that is converted to 5-FdUMP. This metabolite acts as a suicide inhibitor by permanently binding to thymidylate synthase, stopping dTMP synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a “suicide” inhibitor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Elemental sources of the purine ring
statement: The synthesis of the purine ring requires the contribution of specific atoms from various donor molecules. Which of the following amino acids contributes the most atoms to the completed purine ring structure?
options: Alanine
Glutamine
Glycine
Serine
Aspartate
correctOption: Glycine
optionExplanations: Alanine is not a precursor for the purine ring atoms mentioned in the standard biochemical pathway.
Glutamine contributes two nitrogens (N3 and N9) to the purine ring.
Glycine is the most significant amino acid contributor, providing a three-atom 'core' (C4, C5, and N7) to the purine ring structure.
Serine is not a direct donor of atoms for the purine ring, although it plays a role in one-carbon metabolism (folate) which eventually provides carbon atoms (C2, C8).
Aspartate contributes only one nitrogen (N1) to the purine ring.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 292 (Book Page): [The atoms of the purine ring are contributed by a number of compounds, including amino acids (aspartic acid, glycine, and glutamine), CO2, and N10–formyltetrahydrofolate.] (Ref Figure 22.5: Glycine contributes C4, C5, and N7).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which specific enzyme catalyzes the conversion of UTP to CTP, representing the only way mammalian cells can synthesize cytosine nucleotides?
options: Dihydroorotase
CTP synthetase
Orotidylate decarboxylase
CMP kinase
Ribonucleotide reductase
correctOption: CTP synthetase
optionExplanations: Dihydroorotase is an early enzyme in the de novo pathway that closes the pyrimidine ring; it does not differentiate between uracil and cytosine.
CTP synthetase aminates UTP using the amide nitrogen of glutamine to form CTP, which is essential for RNA synthesis.
Orotidylate decarboxylase converts OMP to UMP; it is part of the pathway leading to uracil, not the branch to cytosine.
CMP kinase is involved in the phosphorylation of CMP to CDP, not in the de novo formation of the cytosine ring from uracil.
Ribonucleotide reductase reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates (like CDP) to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (like dCDP) for DNA synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): CTP is produced by amination of UTP by CTP synthetase (Figure 22.22), with glutamine providing the nitrogen.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A physician examines a young boy suspected of having Lesch-Nyhan syndrome. Which physical finding would be most suggestive of the behavioral disturbances specific to this diagnosis?
options: Xanthomas on the extensor tendons
Swollen, erythematous metatarsophalangeal joint
Presence of Tophi on the external ear
Loss of tissue on the lips or fingertips
Hepatomegaly and abdominal distension
correctOption: Loss of tissue on the lips or fingertips
optionExplanations: Xanthomas are associated with lipid disorders (hypercholesterolemia), not defects in purine metabolism.
This describes podagra (acute gout), which can occur in Lesch-Nyhan but is also common in many other forms of hyperuricemia.
Tophi are characteristic of chronic gout, but they are not specific to the behavioral disturbances of Lesch-Nyhan.
Self-mutilation, specifically the compulsive biting of the lips and fingers, is a distinct behavioral hallmark that differentiates Lesch-Nyhan from other hyperuricemic states.
Hepatomegaly is not a standard feature of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome; it is more common in glycogen storage diseases like Von Gierke's.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): the syndrome is characterized by motor dysfunction, cognitive deficits, and behavioral disturbances that include self-mutilation (biting of lips and fingers, Figure 22.11).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: To maintain the correct balance of deoxyribonucleotides, the binding of one nucleotide to the 'substrate specificity site' can enhance the reduction of a different species. The binding of deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) to this site specifically promotes the reduction of which substrate?
options: Uridine diphosphate (UDP)
Cytidine diphosphate (CDP)
Guanosine diphosphate (GDP)
Adenosine diphosphate (ADP)
Thymidine diphosphate (TDP)
correctOption: Guanosine diphosphate (GDP)
optionExplanations: UDP reduction is involved in the earlier steps of dTMP synthesis; however, the specific conformational change induced by dTTP at the specificity site is focused on GDP as per the provided text.
CDP is a pyrimidine substrate. Usually, high levels of pyrimidine products like dTTP would not be the primary signal to increase the reduction of other pyrimidines like CDP.

Correct. This is a classic example of cross-regulation. High levels of the pyrimidine product dTTP signal the enzyme to favor the reduction of the purine substrate GDP, ensuring a balanced purine/pyrimidine ratio for DNA.
ADP reduction is regulated by other combinations at the specificity site; the binding of dTTP is specifically highlighted for its role in promoting the purine GDP reduction.

TDP (thymidine diphosphate) is not a standard substrate for ribonucleotide reductase because thymine is already a deoxy-form; the enzyme reduces ribose to deoxyribose, which is not applicable to thymidine nucleotides in this context.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): For example, deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) binding at the specificity sites causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP to dGDP at the catalytic site.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: The conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) to adenylosuccinate, the first step in the synthesis of AMP, requires the addition of which amino acid as a nitrogen donor?
options: Glycine
Glutamine
Glutamate
Aspartic acid
Alanine
correctOption: Aspartic acid
optionExplanations: Glycine is incorporated as a whole molecule into the purine ring during the earlier de novo synthesis steps (forming glycinamide ribonucleotide), not in the branching from IMP.
Glutamine serves as the nitrogen donor for the conversion of Xanthosine Monophosphate (XMP) to GMP, not for the synthesis of adenylosuccinate.
Glutamate is the product formed when glutamine donates its amide nitrogen in the synthesis of GMP, but it is not a reactant in the IMP to AMP pathway.
Aspartic acid provides the amino group that is joined to IMP to form adenylosuccinate, catalyzed by adenylosuccinate synthetase.
Alanine is a non-essential amino acid involved in glucose-alanine cycles but does not participate in the synthesis of purine nucleotides from IMP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The conversion of IMP to either AMP or GMP uses a two-step, energy-requiring pathway (Figure 22.8)... Aspartic acid [is required for IMP to Adenylosuccinate].

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A 35-year-old male is found to have a genetic mutation in the X-linked PRPP synthetase gene. Kinetic analysis of the mutant enzyme reveals a significantly increased Vmax and a decreased sensitivity to its allosteric inhibitors, AMP and GMP. What is the most likely clinical consequence of this mutation?
options: Megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12
Hypouricemia and increased orotic acid excretion
Motor dysfunction and self-mutilation behavior
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency due to dATP accumulation
Hyperuricemia leading to gouty arthritis and urolithiasis
correctOption: Hyperuricemia leading to gouty arthritis and urolithiasis
optionExplanations: Megaloblastic anemia is associated with pyrimidine defects like UMP synthase deficiency, not purine overproduction.
The mutation leads to hyperuricemia (overproduction), not hypouricemia.
Self-mutilation is characteristic of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (HGPRT deficiency), not simple PRPP synthetase overactivity, although both cause hyperuricemia.
SCID is caused by ADA deficiency; PRPP synthetase overactivity does not cause this immune profile.
Increased PRPP production accelerates the purine pathway, leading to excessive uric acid production, gout, and kidney stones.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): mutations in the gene for X-linked PRPP synthetase result in the enzyme having an increased Vmax... or a decreased sensitivity to purine nucleotides—its allosteric inhibitors... increased availability of PRPP increases purine production, resulting in elevated levels of plasma uric acid.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A pregnant woman is warned that certain medications are 'extremely toxic' to the fetus because they interfere with the synthesis of nucleotides required for development. Which of the following drugs is specifically highlighted for this fetal toxicity in the context of purine synthesis inhibition?
options: Sulfinpyrazone
Probenecid
Methotrexate
Colchicine
Allopurinol
correctOption: Methotrexate
optionExplanations: Sulfinpyrazone, like probenecid, is a uricosuric agent and does not target the synthetic enzymes for purines or pyrimidines.
