statement: The de novo synthesis of the pyrimidine ring requires specific atoms donated by a set of precursors. Which of the following molecules provides both a carbon and a nitrogen atom to the pyrimidine structure?
options: Glutamine (Amide nitrogen)
Glycine
Aspartic acid
Arginine
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
correctOption: Aspartic acid
optionExplanations: Glutamine provides only the amide nitrogen to the pyrimidine ring via carbamoyl phosphate; it does not contribute carbon atoms to the ring itself.
Glycine is a major precursor for the purine ring, providing carbons 4 and 5 and nitrogen 7, but it is not utilized in pyrimidine synthesis.
Aspartic acid is a critical precursor that contributes three carbons and one nitrogen to the pyrimidine ring, forming the majority of the six-membered structure.
Arginine is a member of the urea cycle but is not a direct atom donor for the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides.
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate is a one-carbon donor used in purine synthesis and the conversion of dUMP to dTMP, but it does not provide atoms for the initial pyrimidine ring synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [The sources of the atoms in the pyrimidine ring are glutamine, CO 2 , and aspartic acid (Figure 22.19).]

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: A pharmacological agent is administered to a patient with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) that specifically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase by destroying the free radical required for its enzymatic activity. Which drug matches this description?
options: Allopurinol
Mycophenolic acid
Methotrexate
Hydroxyurea
5-Fluorouracil
correctOption: Hydroxyurea
optionExplanations: Allopurinol is a structural analog of hypoxanthine that inhibits xanthine oxidase to treat gout; it does not affect RNR.
Mycophenolic acid is a reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase, used primarily as an immunosuppressant to prevent graft rejection.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), reducing the availability of tetrahydrofolate (THF).
Correct. Hydroxyurea targets the R2 subunit of ribonucleotide reductase and destroys the essential tyrosyl free radical, halting dNTP production.
5-Fluorouracil is a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase, not ribonucleotide reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): The drug hydroxyurea destroys the free radical required for enzymic activity of ribonucleotide reductase, and thus inhibits the generation of substrates for DNA synthesis.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: According to the cross-regulatory mechanisms of purine biosynthesis, what is the inhibitory effect of guanosine monophosphate (GMP) on the reactions that convert inosine monophosphate (IMP) into mature purines?
options: It activates GMP synthetase
It inhibits adenylate kinase
It inhibits adenylosuccinate synthetase
It activates adenylosuccinase
It inhibits IMP dehydrogenase
correctOption: It inhibits IMP dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: GMP inhibits its own production pathway; it does not activate GMP synthetase.
Adenylate kinase is regulated by the relative concentrations of adenylates (AMP/ADP/ATP) for energy homeostasis, not primarily by GMP levels.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is inhibited by AMP, the end product of that specific branch, not by GMP.
Adenylosuccinase is part of the AMP branch; it is not activated by GMP.
GMP exerts feedback inhibition on IMP dehydrogenase, the first enzyme in its own biosynthetic branch from IMP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Also, the first reaction in each pathway is inhibited by the end product of that pathway. ... [Figure 22.8 shows GMP inhibiting IMP dehydrogenase].

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Which molecule serves as the common 'parent' purine nucleotide from which both adenosine monophosphate (AMP) and guanosine monophosphate (GMP) are derived?
options: 5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP)
Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
Adenylosuccinate
Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)
5'-Phosphoribosylamine
correctOption: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
optionExplanations: PRPP is an activated pentose that provides the ribose 5-phosphate scaffold but is not the parent purine nucleotide itself; it is used at the start of the de novo pathway.
Inosine monophosphate (IMP) is the 'parent' purine because it is the first nucleotide formed with a complete purine ring (hypoxanthine), which is then branched to form either AMP or GMP.
Adenylosuccinate is an intermediate specifically in the pathway from IMP to AMP, formed by the addition of aspartate.
Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) is an intermediate specifically in the pathway from IMP to GMP, not the common parent for both purines.
5'-Phosphoribosylamine is the first committed intermediate in the de novo purine synthesis pathway, but it does not yet contain the purine ring structure.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): C. Synthesis of inosine monophosphate, the “parent” purine nucleotide. The next nine steps in purine nucleotide biosynthesis leading to the synthesis of inosine monophosphate (IMP, whose base is hypoxanthine) are illustrated in Figure 22.7.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Which of the following describes the specific chemical modification performed by Ribonucleotide reductase on a ribonucleoside diphosphate substrate?
options: Addition of a methyl group to the 5-position of the uracil base.
Reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl group to a hydrogen atom.
Cleavage of the N-glycosidic bond to release the free base.
Phosphorylation of the 3'-hydroxyl group using ATP.
Removal of the 3'-hydroxyl group from the ribose ring.
correctOption: Reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl group to a hydrogen atom.
optionExplanations: Methylation of the uracil base is performed by thymidylate synthase during the conversion of dUMP to dTMP, not by ribonucleotide reductase.

The fundamental role of ribonucleotide reductase is the reduction of the ribose sugar's 2'-carbon by replacing its hydroxyl group (-OH) with a hydrogen atom (-H), converting a ribonucleotide into a 2'-deoxyribonucleotide.
Cleavage of the N-glycosidic bond is the function of phosphorylases and nucleosidases during nucleotide degradation, not RNR.
Phosphorylation is performed by kinases. Ribonucleotide reductase is a reductase that removes an oxygen atom; it does not add phosphate groups.
Ribonucleotide reductase specifically targets the 2' position of the ribose sugar; the 3'-hydroxyl group remains intact in deoxyribonucleotides.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The immediate donors of the hydrogen atoms needed for the reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl group are two sulfhydryl groups on the enzyme itself, which, during the reaction, form a disulfide bond.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: In a skeletal muscle cell experiencing high metabolic demand, the enzyme Adenylate Kinase is essential for maintaining energetic homeostasis. What is the precise equilibrium reaction catalyzed by this enzyme?
options: IMP + Aspartate <-> Adenylosuccinate
GDP + ATP <-> GTP + ADP
AMP + GTP <-> ADP + GDP
ATP + H2O -> ADP + Pi
AMP + ATP <-> 2 ADP
correctOption: AMP + ATP <-> 2 ADP
optionExplanations: This is the first step of de novo AMP synthesis from IMP catalyzed by adenylosuccinate synthetase, not a salvage or equilibrium kinase reaction.
This reaction is catalyzed by nucleoside diphosphate kinase, which transfers a phosphate from ATP to GDP to form GTP and ADP.
This reaction is not catalyzed by adenylate kinase. While GDP and ADP are involved in other kinase reactions, adenylate kinase is specific to adenine nucleotides.
This describes the hydrolysis of ATP by ATPases to provide energy, which is a unidirectional catabolic reaction, not the equilibrium-maintaining kinase reaction.

Correct. Adenylate kinase (also known as myokinase in muscle) maintains the balance between the adenine nucleotide pool by interconverting one molecule of ATP and one of AMP into two molecules of ADP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): Adenylate kinase is particularly active in liver and muscle, where the turnover of energy from ATP is high. Its function is to maintain an equilibrium among AMP, ADP, and ATP. [Figure 22.9 shows: AMP + ATP <-> 2 ADP].

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: A medical student is reviewing the regulation of deoxyribonucleotide synthesis. They note that the binding of different nucleoside triphosphates to the 'substrate specificity sites' of ribonucleotide reductase alters which ribonucleoside diphosphate is preferred for reduction. Which of the following is a correct example of this regulation?
options: ATP binding inhibits the reduction of GDP
dGTP binding inhibits the reduction of UDP
dATP binding activates the reduction of CDP
dTTP binding causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP
dCTP binding promotes the reduction of ADP
correctOption: dTTP binding causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP
optionExplanations: ATP at the activity site activates the enzyme; the text does not state that it specifically inhibits GDP reduction at the specificity site.
The text focuses on the role of dTTP and dATP; it does not specify dGTP inhibiting UDP reduction as the primary regulatory example.
dATP at the activity site is a global inhibitor of the enzyme, not a specific activator for CDP reduction.
This is a specific regulatory example provided in the text: dTTP acts as an allosteric effector at the specificity site to promote the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
The regulation of ribonucleotide reductase is complex, but the specific relationship mentioned in the source is the effect of dTTP on GDP reduction.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): For example, deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) binding at the specificity sites causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP to dGDP at the catalytic site.

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: Which folate analog is used primarily as an antimicrobial agent because of its selective inhibition of bacterial dihydrofolate reductase rather than the human version?
options: 5-Fluorouracil
Methotrexate
Sulfinpyrazone
Trimethoprim
Mycophenolic acid
correctOption: Trimethoprim
optionExplanations: 5-Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine (thymine) analog that targets thymidylate synthase, not dihydrofolate reductase.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase in both humans and bacteria (with high affinity for the human version), making it an anticancer/immunosuppressant rather than a selective antimicrobial.
Sulfinpyrazone is a uricosuric agent used to increase the renal excretion of uric acid in gout patients; it has no antimicrobial activity.
Trimethoprim is a synthetic analog that specifically targets the bacterial version of dihydrofolate reductase, allowing for the treatment of infections with minimal impact on human folate metabolism.
Mycophenolic acid inhibits IMP dehydrogenase and is used as an immunosuppressant for graft rejection, not as a folate-targeting antimicrobial.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Trimethoprim, a folate analog, has potent antibacterial activity because of its selective inhibition of bacterial dihydrofolate reductase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which enzyme catalyzes the committed and regulated step of de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis in human cells?
options: Aspartate transcarbamoylase
Dihydroorotase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase
correctOption: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
optionExplanations: Aspartate transcarbamoylase catalyzes the second step of the pathway; while it is the primary regulatory step in prokaryotes, it is not the committed step in mammalian cells.
Dihydroorotase is the third enzyme in the CAD multifunctional complex; it facilitates ring closure to form dihydroorotate but does not serve as the primary rate-limiting step.
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II) is the cytosolic, rate-limiting enzyme for de novo pyrimidine synthesis, regulated allosterically by PRPP (activator) and UTP (inhibitor).
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS I) is a mitochondrial enzyme involved in the urea cycle, not pyrimidine synthesis; it utilizes ammonia as its nitrogen source rather than glutamine.
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase is part of the bifunctional UMP synthase complex; it acts much later in the pathway to attach the ribose-5-phosphate group to the orotate base.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): The regulated step of this pathway in mammalian cells is the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine and CO 2, catalyzed by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) II.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase is characterized as a multi-subunit complex. Which statement accurately describes its structural composition and substrate range?
options: It is a monomeric enzyme specific only for purines
It requires ribose 5-phosphate as a direct starting material
It consists of a single polypeptide chain with three catalytic domains
The R2 subunit is responsible for binding allosteric inhibitors like dATP
It is composed of R1 and R2 subunits and acts on both purines and pyrimidines
correctOption: It is composed of R1 and R2 subunits and acts on both purines and pyrimidines
optionExplanations: RNR is a heterotetramer (dimeric subunits R1 and R2) and acts on both purines and pyrimidines, not just purines.
Ribose 5-phosphate is the starting material for PRPP synthesis, but RNR specifically uses ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) as substrates.
This description fits CAD or UMP synthase in pyrimidine synthesis, but RNR is composed of separate nonidentical subunits.
The R1 subunit typically contains the catalytic site and the allosteric regulatory sites (activity and specificity sites).
RNR is composed of two nonidentical subunits (R1 and R2) and reduces the diphosphate forms of both purine (ADP, GDP) and pyrimidine (CDP, UDP) nucleotides.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): Ribonucleotide reductase (ribonucleoside diphosphate reductase) is composed of two nonidentical dimeric subunits, R1 and R2, and is specific for the reduction of purine nucleoside diphosphates (ADP and GDP), and pyrimidine nucleoside diphosphates...

category: Interpret the role of PABA analogs and mycophenolic acid in purine biosynthesis
statement: Which specific enzyme in the de novo purine biosynthetic pathway is the primary pharmacological target of the drug mycophenolic acid?
options: Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase
Xanthine oxidase
Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
PRPP synthetase
Adenylosuccinate synthetase
correctOption: Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase catalyzes the committed step of purine synthesis and is inhibited by AMP and GMP, but not by mycophenolic acid.
Xanthine oxidase is involved in the degradation of purines to uric acid and is the target of allopurinol and febuxostat, not mycophenolic acid.
Inosine monophosphate (IMP) dehydrogenase is the enzyme responsible for converting IMP to xanthosine monophosphate (XMP), and it is specifically and reversibly inhibited by mycophenolic acid.
PRPP synthetase catalyzes the formation of PRPP from ribose 5-phosphate and ATP; it is inhibited by purine nucleotides but is not the target of mycophenolic acid.
Adenylosuccinate synthetase is involved in the branch of the pathway that leads from IMP to AMP; mycophenolic acid specifically targets the GMP branch instead.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The drug is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The conversion of the parent purine nucleotide, Inosine Monophosphate (IMP), into Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP) and Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) requires distinct energy sources. Which statement correctly identifies the energetic requirements for these transformations?
options: Synthesis of AMP requires NADH, while GMP requires FADH2.
Synthesis of both AMP and GMP requires only GTP.
Synthesis of both AMP and GMP requires only ATP.
Synthesis of AMP requires GTP, while GMP requires ATP.
Synthesis of AMP requires ATP, while GMP requires GTP.
correctOption: Synthesis of AMP requires GTP, while GMP requires ATP.
optionExplanations: NADH is involved in the IMP dehydrogenase step for GMP synthesis, but it is a reducing equivalent, not the primary phosphate donor/energy source for the final amination.
GTP is specifically used for the adenylosuccinate synthetase step in AMP production, but GMP synthesis requires ATP at the GMP synthetase step.
While ATP is the general energy currency, the specific conversion of IMP to AMP utilizes GTP to ensure balanced nucleotide pools.
The use of GTP for AMP synthesis and ATP for GMP synthesis allows the cell to cross-regulate the pathways; if one nucleotide is high, it promotes the synthesis of the other.
This option is incorrect because the pathway uses reciprocal energy sources to balance the production of adenine and guanine nucleotides.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
coreConcept: CPS I Product Shunting in OTC Deficiency
statement: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with developmental delay and recurrent lethargy. Laboratory tests reveal severe hyperammonemia and a massive excretion of orotic acid in the urine. Genetic testing confirms a deficiency in ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC), a mitochondrial urea cycle enzyme. Why does a deficiency in this specific mitochondrial enzyme lead to the overproduction of orotic acid in the cytosol?
options: OTC deficiency prevents the degradation of orotic acid in the small intestine mucosal cells.
Accumulated carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondria leaks into the cytosol, flooding the pyrimidine pathway.
Excessive mitochondrial ammonia inhibits carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II, diverting nitrogen to orotate.
Low citrulline levels allosterically activate CPS II to produce more carbamoyl phosphate.
The lack of OTC causes a direct activation of the cytosolic UMP synthase enzyme.
correctOption: Accumulated carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondria leaks into the cytosol, flooding the pyrimidine pathway.
optionExplanations: The degradation of orotic acid is not a primary function of OTC or the intestinal mucosa in this context; orotic aciduria here is a result of de novo synthesis overactivity.

In OTC deficiency, carbamoyl phosphate produced by CPS I cannot be converted to citrulline. It accumulates in the mitochondria and leaks into the cytosol, where it enters the pyrimidine synthesis pathway, bypassing the regulated CPS II step and leading to massive orotic acid production.

Excess ammonia actually stimulates CPS I, increasing the production of carbamoyl phosphate. It does not inhibit CPS II; if anything, the increased substrate availability (carbamoyl phosphate) drives the pyrimidine pathway forward.
Citrulline is an intermediate of the urea cycle and does not serve as an allosteric regulator for the cytosolic CPS II enzyme. CPS II is regulated by PRPP and UTP levels instead.
UMP synthase is not directly activated by the lack of OTC; it simply processes the excess orotic acid that is produced further upstream due to the overflow of carbamoyl phosphate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides in mammalian cells, which enzyme catalyzes the primary regulated and committed step of the pathway?
options: Thymidylate synthase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
Aspartate transcarbamoylase
Dihydroorotase
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase
correctOption: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
optionExplanations: Thymidylate synthase is a late-stage enzyme specifically required for the conversion of dUMP to dTMP and is a major target for chemotherapy, but it does not regulate the de novo pathway flux from the start.
CPS II is the cytosolic enzyme responsible for the rate-limiting step in human pyrimidine synthesis; it is allosterically inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP.

Aspartate transcarbamoylase is the regulated step in prokaryotic cells, where it is inhibited by CTP, but it is the second step in the mammalian CAD complex and not the primary regulated step in humans.
Dihydroorotase catalyzes the third step of pyrimidine synthesis (cyclization of carbamoyl aspartate), which is part of the trifunctional CAD protein but is not the committed or regulated step.
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase is involved in the second stage of the pathway, converting the free base orotate into the nucleotide OMP using PRPP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [The regulated step of this pathway in mammalian cells is the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine and CO 2 , catalyzed by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) II.]

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
coreConcept: Composition of Renal Stones in Lesch-Nyhan
statement: Urolithiasis in a child with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is primarily composed of which substance?
options: Magnesium ammonium phosphate
Calcium oxalate
Uric acid
Orotic acid
Cystine
correctOption: Uric acid
optionExplanations: Struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate) stones are associated with chronic urinary tract infections by urease-producing bacteria.
Calcium oxalate stones are common in adults and related to hypercalciuria or hyperoxaluria, but they are not the primary stone type in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
The profound hyperuricemia resulting from purine overproduction and salvage failure leads to high concentrations of uric acid in the urine, which precipitates into stones.
Orotic aciduria causes orotic acid crystals in the urine, but this is a defect in pyrimidine synthesis (UMP synthase deficiency), distinct from Lesch-Nyhan.
Cystine stones are caused by cystinuria, a defect in the transport of dibasic amino acids, unrelated to purine metabolism.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): In patients with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, the hyperuricemia frequently results in the formation of uric acid stones in the kidneys (urolithiasis)...

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase demonstrates broad substrate specificity. Which of the following sets of molecules represent the specific group of products generated directly by this enzyme's catalytic action?
options: dADP, dGDP, dCDP, dUDP
Hypoxanthine, Xanthine, Uric acid
dAMP, dGMP, dCMP, dTMP
dATP, dGTP, dCTP, dTTP
Adenosine, Guanosine, Cytidine, Uridine
correctOption: dADP, dGDP, dCDP, dUDP
optionExplanations: Correct. Ribonucleotide reductase converts ADP, GDP, CDP, and UDP into dADP, dGDP, dCDP, and dUDP respectively.
These are intermediates and the end product of purine degradation (catabolism). RNR is an anabolic enzyme involved in nucleotide synthesis.
dAMP, dGMP, and dCMP are monophosphates. RNR produces diphosphates. dTMP is produced by thymidylate synthase from dUMP, not directly by RNR.
These are triphosphates. While these are the final precursors for DNA, RNR only produces the diphosphate intermediates (dNDPs), which must then be phosphorylated by kinases.
These are ribonucleosides (base + sugar), lacking phosphate groups. They are not the products of the ribonucleotide reductase reaction.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): ...specific for the reduction of purine nucleoside diphosphates (ADP and GDP), and pyrimidine nucleoside diphosphates, cytidine diphosphate (CDP) and uridine diphosphate (UDP) to their deoxy-forms (dADP, dGDP, dCDP, and dUDP).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: In the context of the pyrimidine salvage pathway, why is uridine administration effective in decreasing the overproduction of orotic acid in UMP synthase-deficient patients?
options: Uridine directly degrades orotic acid into soluble beta-alanine
Uridine increases the renal clearance of orotic acid crystals
Uridine acts as a methyl donor for the thymidylate synthase reaction
Uridine competes with aspartate for the active site of CAD
Uridine is converted to UTP, which allosterically inhibits CPS II
correctOption: Uridine is converted to UTP, which allosterically inhibits CPS II
optionExplanations: Uridine is not a degradative enzyme; the degradation of the pyrimidine ring occurs through a separate pathway and does not involve uridine-mediated cleavage of orotate.
Uridine's benefit is metabolic (reducing production) rather than mechanical (increasing renal excretion of already formed crystals).
N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate, not uridine, acts as the methyl donor for the conversion of dUMP to dTMP.
Uridine does not compete with aspartate; aspartate transcarbamoylase uses aspartate and carbamoyl phosphate as substrates, and its regulation in mammals is through the CAD complex.
Exogenous uridine is salvaged to UMP and then phosphorylated to UTP; UTP is a potent allosteric inhibitor of the rate-limiting enzyme CPS II, thus shutting down the de novo production of orotate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): CPS II is inhibited by UTP (the end product of this pathway...)... Page 304 (Book Page): The salvage of pyrimidine nucleosides is the basis for using uridine in the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 4-year-old boy presents with a history of recurrent severe infections, cognitive deficits, and a compulsion to bite his lips and fingers. Laboratory analysis reveals a blood uric acid level of 12 mg/dL (Normal: 3-7 mg/dL) and orange crystals in the diaper. What is the primary biochemical mechanism responsible for the increased de novo purine synthesis in this patient?
options: Increased Vmax of the PRPP synthetase enzyme due to an X-linked mutation
Failure of the intestinal mucosal cells to degrade dietary oligonucleotides
Increased levels of dATP inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase
Excessive dietary intake of purine-rich seafood and meat
Lack of HGPRT causing increased PRPP levels and decreased feedback inhibition by IMP/GMP
correctOption: Lack of HGPRT causing increased PRPP levels and decreased feedback inhibition by IMP/GMP
optionExplanations: While PRPP synthetase mutations can cause gout, they do not typically present with the classic 'self-mutilation' and 'cognitive deficit' profile of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
Dietary purines are mostly degraded to uric acid anyway; a failure in intestinal degradation would actually decrease blood uric acid, not increase it to levels causing stones and neurological issues.
Increased dATP and inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase is the mechanism for Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, not Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
Dietary purines contribute to gout in adults, but the severe neurological symptoms and early onset described point to a genetic salvage defect.

In Lesch-Nyhan, HGPRT deficiency prevents the salvage of hypoxanthine and guanine. This leads to a buildup of PRPP (the substrate for the de novo pathway) and a loss of feedback inhibitors (IMP and GMP), drastically ramping up de novo synthesis and subsequent degradation to uric acid.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): In addition, the lack of this salvage pathway causes increased PRPP levels and decreased IMP and GMP levels. As a result, glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase (the committed step in purine synthesis) has excess substrate and decreased inhibitors available, and de novo purine synthesis is increased.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Cytidine triphosphate (CTP) is an essential component for RNA synthesis. Through which biochemical modification is CTP produced from UTP?
options: Amination using glutamine as a nitrogen donor
Methylation using S-adenosylmethionine
Decarboxylation at the C-6 position of the ring
Phosphorylation by a specific CTP kinase
Reduction of the ribose sugar at the 2' carbon
correctOption: Amination using glutamine as a nitrogen donor
optionExplanations: CTP synthetase catalyzes the ATP-dependent amination of UTP, where the amide group of glutamine is transferred to the C-4 position of the uracil ring to form cytosine.
Methylation of the pyrimidine ring is characteristic of dTMP synthesis, not CTP synthesis.
Decarboxylation occurs during the conversion of OMP to UMP, not during the conversion of UTP to CTP.
CTP is a triphosphate; it is formed from UTP, not by the phosphorylation of a cytidine precursor in the de novo pathway.
Reduction of the ribose sugar occurs at the diphosphate level (CDP to dCDP) via ribonucleotide reductase, not during the UTP to CTP conversion.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): CTP is produced by amination of UTP by CTP synthetase (Figure 22.22), with glutamine providing the nitrogen.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: Which specific enzyme in the purine catabolic pathway is the direct pharmacological target of Allopurinol to reduce the production of uric acid?
options: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase
AMP deaminase
Adenosine deaminase
Xanthine oxidase
Guanase
correctOption: Xanthine oxidase
optionExplanations: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) converts inosine and guanosine into their respective free bases (hypoxanthine and guanine). Its deficiency leads to T-cell immunodeficiency but it is not targeted by allopurinol.
AMP deaminase converts AMP to IMP. While it is involved in the initial steps of purine nucleotide degradation, it is not inhibited by allopurinol and does not directly produce uric acid.
Adenosine deaminase (ADA) converts adenosine to inosine. Deficiency in this enzyme leads to SCID, but it is not inhibited by allopurinol; it is upstream of the xanthine oxidase step.

Xanthine oxidase is the enzyme responsible for converting hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. Allopurinol and its metabolite oxypurinol directly inhibit this enzyme, reducing urate production.
Guanase is responsible for the deamination of guanine to form xanthine. While it is part of the degradation pathway, it is not the primary site of allopurinol's clinical effect.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): Allopurinol, a structural analog of hypoxanthine, inhibits uric acid synthesis and is used in patients who are “overproducers” of uric acid. Allopurinol is converted in the body to oxypurinol, which inhibits xanthine oxidase (XO).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: The allosteric regulation of ribonucleotide reductase is complex. How does the binding of deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) to the substrate specificity sites influence the enzyme's catalytic preference?
options: It activates the reduction of UDP to dUDP.
It inhibits the reduction of all four nucleoside diphosphates.
It promotes the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
It prevents the reduction of purine nucleotides only.
It activates the reduction of CDP to dCDP.
correctOption: It promotes the reduction of GDP to dGDP.
optionExplanations: UDP reduction is regulated by other nucleotides; dTTP is specifically highlighted for its role in promoting GDP reduction.
Inhibition of all four diphosphates is the function of the activity site when bound by dATP, not the substrate specificity site bound by dTTP.
Correct. Binding of dTTP to the substrate specificity site induces a conformational change that favors the reduction of GDP to dGDP, helping balance the dNTP pools.
dTTP binding specifically favors GDP reduction; it does not broadly prevent all purine reduction.
The text specifically mentions that dTTP binding promotes the reduction of a purine nucleotide (GDP), not CDP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): For example, deoxythymidine triphosphate (dTTP) binding at the specificity sites causes a conformational change that allows reduction of GDP to dGDP at the catalytic site.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: In the human metabolic degradation of pyrimidine nucleotides, which of the following is a characteristic end product that is highly soluble and eventually excreted?
options: Allantoin
Xanthine
Uric acid
Hypoxanthine
Beta-aminoisobutyrate
correctOption: Beta-aminoisobutyrate
optionExplanations: Allantoin is the product of uric acid cleavage by urate oxidase in non-primate mammals; it is not a product of pyrimidine degradation.
Xanthine is an intermediate in the purine degradation pathway that is oxidized to uric acid.
Uric acid is the end product of purine degradation in humans, not pyrimidine degradation.
Hypoxanthine is a purine base resulting from the degradation of IMP or salvaged by HGPRT; it is not related to pyrimidine catabolism.
The pyrimidine ring is cleaved, unlike the purine ring, and is degraded to soluble products including beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Unlike the purine ring, which is not cleaved human cells, the pyrimidine ring is opened and degraded to highly soluble products, β-alanine and β-aminoisobutyrate, with the production of NH3 and CO2.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A patient undergoing an organ transplant is prescribed mycophenolic acid to prevent graft rejection. Which specific step in purine metabolism is targeted by this drug?
options: Conversion of IMP to xanthosine monophosphate.
Conversion of PRPP to 5-phosphoribosylamine.
Conversion of xanthosine monophosphate to GMP.
Reduction of ribose to deoxyribose by ribonucleotide reductase.
Oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine by xanthine oxidase.
correctOption: Conversion of IMP to xanthosine monophosphate.
optionExplanations: Mycophenolic acid specifically inhibits IMP dehydrogenase, the enzyme that converts IMP to xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) in the pathway toward GMP synthesis.
The conversion of PRPP to phosphoribosylamine is the committed step of de novo synthesis, inhibited by end-products AMP/GMP, but not the primary target of mycophenolic acid.
The conversion of XMP to GMP is catalyzed by GMP synthetase, which is not the target of mycophenolic acid.
Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea or dATP, not mycophenolic acid.
Xanthine oxidase is the target of allopurinol and febuxostat, which are used to treat gout, not as immunosuppressants.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): MYCOPHENOLIC ACID: The drug is a reversible, uncompetitive inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase. The drug deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of key components of nucleic acids.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: During the synthesis of Adenosine monophosphate (AMP) from Inosine monophosphate (IMP), the addition of aspartate followed by the action of Adenylosuccinate lyase results in the release of which citric acid cycle intermediate?
options: Malate
Oxaloacetate
Fumarate
Succinate
Alpha-ketoglutarate
correctOption: Fumarate
optionExplanations: Malate is not produced in this reaction; it is a TCA cycle intermediate produced from fumarate by fumarase.
Oxaloacetate is the precursor to aspartate but is not directly released during the conversion of IMP to AMP.
Correct. The cleavage of adenylosuccinate by adenylosuccinate lyase (adenylosuccinase) produces AMP and releases fumarate.
Succinate is not produced here; although aspartate forms a 'succinate-like' bridge in adenylosuccinate, the cleavage product is fumarate.
Alpha-ketoglutarate is involved in transamination reactions but is not a product of the IMP to AMP conversion sequence.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): [Figure 22.8] Adenylosuccinate is converted to AMP by Adenylosuccinase [Adenylosuccinate lyase], releasing Fumarate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Metabolic crossover between Urea Cycle and Pyrimidine Synthesis
statement: A patient is found to have hyperammonemia and significant orotic aciduria. The physician suspects a urea cycle defect rather than hereditary orotic aciduria. Which enzyme deficiency most likely explains this combination of findings?
options: UMP synthase
Ornithine transcarbamylase
Dihydroorotase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I
Thymidylate synthase
correctOption: Ornithine transcarbamylase
optionExplanations: UMP synthase deficiency causes orotic aciduria but does not cause hyperammonemia; it is a defect in the pyrimidine pathway itself.

Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency causes carbamoyl phosphate to accumulate in the mitochondria; it leaks into the cytosol, over-stimulating de novo pyrimidine synthesis and causing orotic aciduria.
Dihydroorotase deficiency is part of the CAD complex; its absence would prevent the formation of dihydroorotate and thus orotate, leading to pyrimidine deficiency without orotic aciduria.
CPS I deficiency causes hyperammonemia but decreases the production of carbamoyl phosphate, thus orotic acid would be low, not high.
Thymidylate synthase deficiency would affect dTMP production and lead to megaloblastic changes but does not directly cause orotic aciduria or hyperammonemia.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): [Note: Carbamoyl phosphate, synthesized by CPS I, is also a precursor of urea (see Page 245 (Book Page)). Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.]

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: Administration of uridine is the standard treatment for hereditary orotic aciduria. Beyond providing a source for UMP via salvage, how does uridine help reduce the excessive excretion of orotic acid?
options: Uridine serves as an alternative substrate for the OMP decarboxylase domain.
Uridine enhances the activity of the urea cycle to consume excess carbamoyl phosphate.
Uridine increases the renal clearance of orotic acid by competing for transporters.
Uridine is converted to UTP, which allosterically inhibits carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
Uridine competitively inhibits the mitochondrial enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase.
correctOption: Uridine is converted to UTP, which allosterically inhibits carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
optionExplanations: Uridine is the product of the pathway (once converted from UMP); it is not a substrate for OMP decarboxylase (which converts OMP to UMP).
Uridine is a pyrimidine and does not directly affect the speed or capacity of the urea cycle.
Uridine does not primarily work via renal transport competition; its effect is on the metabolic production of the acid.

Uridine is salvaged to UMP and then phosphorylated to UTP. UTP provides the necessary feedback inhibition to CPS II, slowing down the entire de novo pathway and thus reducing the production of orotic acid.
Uridine does not inhibit dihydroorotate dehydrogenase; that enzyme continues to produce orotate unless the total flux through the pathway is reduced.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): Administration of uridine results in improvement of the anemia and decreased excretion of orotate. ... CPS II is inhibited by UTP.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 25-year-old male is evaluated for recurrent gouty arthritis since his teens. Laboratory studies reveal significantly elevated plasma uric acid. Further enzyme kinetics studies on the patient's fibroblasts reveal a mutant form of PRPP synthetase. Which kinetic alteration in this enzyme would most likely explain the patient's condition?
options: A decreased Vmax for the production of PRPP
Increased sensitivity to inhibition by AMP and GMP
Resistance to activation by inorganic phosphate
A lower Km for the substrate ribose 5-phosphate
A significantly increased Km for ATP
correctOption: A lower Km for the substrate ribose 5-phosphate
optionExplanations: A decreased Vmax would reduce the rate of PRPP formation, leading to lower urate levels.
Increased sensitivity to feedback inhibitors (AMP/GMP) would turn the pathway off more easily, preventing overproduction.
PRPP synthetase is activated by inorganic phosphate; resistance to activation would likely decrease its activity.
A lower Km for ribose 5-phosphate means the enzyme reaches half-maximum velocity at lower substrate concentrations, leading to overproduction of PRPP and subsequently uric acid.
An increased Km for ATP would make the enzyme less efficient at producing PRPP, which would decrease purine synthesis and urate levels.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): several identified mutations in the gene for X-linked PRPP synthetase result in the enzyme having an increased Vmax (see Page 50 (Book Page)) for the production of PRPP, a lower Km (see Page 51 (Book Page)) for ribose 5-phosphate, or a decreased sensitivity to purine nucleotides—its allosteric inhibitors.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: The synthesis of GMP from IMP involves an oxidative step followed by a transamination. What is the oxidized intermediate produced in the first step of this branch?
options: Xanthosine monophosphate
Inosine
Hypoxanthine
Adenylosuccinate
Orotidine monophosphate
correctOption: Xanthosine monophosphate
optionExplanations: Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) is the result of the NAD+-dependent oxidation of IMP, which is then aminated to form GMP.
Inosine is a nucleoside (hypoxanthine + ribose) formed by the dephosphorylation of IMP, not a synthetic intermediate in the pathway to GMP.
Hypoxanthine is the nitrogenous base found in IMP, not an intermediate produced *from* IMP in the synthetic branch.
Adenylosuccinate is the intermediate in the AMP branch, formed by the addition of aspartate to IMP.
Orotidine monophosphate (OMP) is an intermediate in pyrimidine synthesis, not purine synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Figure 22.8: IMP [via IMP dehydrogenase] -> Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase possesses distinct allosteric 'activity sites' that control the overall rate of catalytic flux. Which of the following scenarios correctly describes the regulation at these specific sites?
options: Binding of CDP at the activity site stimulates the reduction of UDP.
Binding of dATP inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme.
Binding of dATP activates the enzyme to increase DNA substrate production.
Binding of ATP inhibits the enzyme to conserve cellular energy.
Binding of dTTP at the activity site prevents the reduction of GDP.
correctOption: Binding of dATP inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme.
optionExplanations: CDP is a substrate that binds to the catalytic (active) site, not the allosteric activity site. The activity site is reserved for the general regulators ATP and dATP.
The activity site is specifically regulated by the ratio of ATP/dATP. dATP binding at this site induces an inhibitory conformational change that stops the reduction of all four NDP substrates.
Binding of dATP to the activity site does not activate the enzyme; instead, it is a potent feedback inhibitor that signals a surplus of deoxyribonucleotides, thereby halting further production.
ATP binding at the activity site actually serves as an activator for ribonucleotide reductase, signaling that the cell has sufficient energy to proceed with DNA precursor synthesis.

dTTP regulates the 'substrate specificity site,' not the 'activity site.' Binding of dTTP at the specificity site influences which specific ribonucleotide (like GDP) is reduced, rather than turning the whole enzyme on or off.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme and, therefore, prevents the reduction of any of the four nucleoside diphosphates.

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: A researcher is evaluating synthetic compounds that mimic the structure of natural purines to treat hyperuricemia. Which of the following drugs is characterized as a structural analog of hypoxanthine?
options: Allopurinol
Mycophenolic acid
Methotrexate
5-Fluorouracil
Trimethoprim
correctOption: Allopurinol
optionExplanations: Allopurinol is specifically designed as a structural analog of hypoxanthine. It is converted to oxypurinol, which then competitively inhibits xanthine oxidase to reduce uric acid production.
Mycophenolic acid is an immunosuppressant that acts as a reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase but is not a structural analog of hypoxanthine.
Methotrexate is a structural analog of folic acid that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, thereby interfering with the synthesis of THF required for purine and TMP production.
5-Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine (thymine) analog used as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase, not a purine analog.
Trimethoprim is a folate analog that selectively inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase, used primarily as an antimicrobial agent.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): [Allopurinol, a structural analog of hypoxanthine, inhibits uric acid synthesis and is used in patients who are ‐overproducers‐ of uric acid.]

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
coreConcept: Substrate specificity in purine branch synthesis
statement: The conversion of xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) to guanosine monophosphate (GMP) requires a specific nitrogen donor and a specific energy source. Which combination is correct for this reaction?
options: Glutamate and UTP
Glycine and ATP
Ammonia and GTP
Glutamine and ATP
Aspartate and GTP
correctOption: Glutamine and ATP
optionExplanations: Glutamate is the product of the glutamine-dependent reaction, not the substrate. UTP is not involved in the purine biosynthetic steps converting IMP to GMP.
Glycine is used early in the de novo purine pathway (steps 2 and 3) to build the purine ring, but it is not the nitrogen donor for the specific conversion of XMP to GMP.
While some prokaryotic enzymes might use free ammonia, the human GMP synthetase specifically requires glutamine as the nitrogen source and ATP as the energy donor.
The enzyme GMP synthetase utilizes the amide nitrogen of glutamine and the hydrolysis of ATP (to AMP and PPi) to convert XMP into GMP.
Aspartate and GTP are the nitrogen donor and energy source, respectively, for the synthesis of adenylosuccinate (the AMP branch), not the GMP branch.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP. ... [Figure 22.8 shows XMP to GMP requires ATP and Glutamine].

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
coreConcept: Cellular Localization of Pyrimidine Synthesis Enzymes
statement: A researcher studying the de novo pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway identifies a specific enzyme that is uniquely associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane, whereas all other enzymes of the pathway are cytosolic. Which enzyme is being described?
options: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
Aspartate transcarbamoylase
Thymidylate synthase
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase
correctOption: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is the first enzyme of the CAD complex and is located in the cytosol, distinguishing it from the mitochondrial CPS I used in the urea cycle.

Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is the only enzyme in the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway located on the inner mitochondrial membrane. It catalyzes the oxidation of dihydroorotate to orotate using FAD as a cofactor.
Aspartate transcarbamoylase is the second domain of the CAD complex and is located in the cytosol where it forms carbamoyl aspartate.
Thymidylate synthase is a cytosolic enzyme that converts dUMP to dTMP; it is not part of the mitochondrial membrane-associated steps.
Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase is a domain of the bifunctional UMP synthase and is located in the cytosol; it attaches the completed orotate ring to PRPP.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. All other enzymes in pyrimidine biosynthesis are cytosolic.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 4-year-old male is brought to the clinic with developmental delay and a history of repetitive self-injurious behavior, specifically biting his lips and fingertips. Laboratory analysis reveals significant hyperuricemia. The physician suspects a defect in the purine salvage pathway. What is the precise metabolic consequence of the enzyme deficiency in this patient?
options: Decreased PRPP levels due to lack of substrate utilization
Decreased de-novo purine synthesis due to accumulation of bases
Increased levels of IMP and GMP leading to feedback inhibition
Inhibition of the amidotransferase enzyme by hypoxanthine
Increased PRPP levels and increased de-novo purine synthesis
correctOption: Increased PRPP levels and increased de-novo purine synthesis
optionExplanations: PRPP levels increase significantly because PRPP is a substrate for the missing HGPRT enzyme and is therefore not consumed at the normal rate.
De-novo synthesis is actually accelerated, not decreased, because the feedback inhibitors (IMP, GMP) are low and the activator (PRPP) is high.
In Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (HGPRT deficiency), IMP and GMP levels are actually decreased because they cannot be salvaged from hypoxanthine and guanine.
Hypoxanthine does not inhibit the amidotransferase; it is the nucleotides (AMP, GMP) that provide feedback, and these are deficient in this syndrome.
The absence of HGPRT prevents the salvage of hypoxanthine and guanine, leading to a surplus of PRPP and a lack of feedback inhibition, which drastically ramps up de-novo synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): In addition, the lack of this salvage pathway causes increased PRPP levels and decreased IMP and GMP levels. As a result, glutamine:phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase... has excess substrate and decreased inhibitors available, and de novo purine synthesis is increased.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Prevention of uracil incorporation in DNA
statement: What is the metabolic significance of the enzyme dUTP diphosphatase (dUTPase) in DNA synthesis?
options: It acts as a subunit of the CAD complex to close the pyrimidine ring.
It catalyzes the rate-limiting step of CTP synthesis from UTP.
It reduces the availability of dUTP to prevent the erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.
It converts dUMP to dTMP using a methylene-THF donor.
It phosphorylates uridine to UMP in the salvage pathway.
correctOption: It reduces the availability of dUTP to prevent the erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.
optionExplanations: The CAD complex consists of CPS II, aspartate transcarbamoylase, and dihydroorotase; dUTPase is not part of it.
CTP synthetase catalyzes the conversion of UTP to CTP; dUTPase is involved in deoxyribonucleotide metabolism.
dUTPase hydrolyzes dUTP to dUMP. This serves two purposes: it provides dUMP for dTMP synthesis and keeps dUTP levels low so DNA polymerase doesn't mistakenly use it instead of dTTP.
This is the function of thymidylate synthase, not dUTPase.
The phosphorylation of uridine to UMP is handled by uridine kinase, not dUTPase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): dUTPase, then, plays an important role in reducing availability of dUTP as a substrate for DNA synthesis, thus preventing erroneous incorporation of uracil into DNA.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
coreConcept: Enzymatic Basis of PNP vs ADA Deficiency
statement: A 5-year-old child presents with a history of recurrent pulmonary infections and developmental delay. Laboratory investigations reveal a severe reduction in T-lymphocyte count, while B-lymphocyte and Natural Killer (NK) cell counts remain within normal limits. A deficiency in which enzyme involved in the purine degradative pathway is the most likely cause of this isolated T-cell immunodeficiency?
options: AMP deaminase
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP)
Adenosine deaminase (ADA)
Xanthine oxidase (XO)
Guanase
correctOption: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP)
optionExplanations: AMP deaminase deficiency is typically associated with exercise-induced muscle myopathy, not immunodeficiency.
PNP deficiency specifically results in a T-cell immunodeficiency. While rarer and less severe than ADA deficiency, it is classically associated with recurrent infections and neurodevelopmental delay.
ADA deficiency causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID), which affects T, B, and NK cells, unlike the isolated T-cell defect described here.
Xanthine oxidase deficiency would lead to xanthinuria and low uric acid levels, but it does not cause primary immunodeficiency.
Guanase is involved in converting guanine to xanthine; its deficiency is not associated with the clinical presentation of SCID or T-cell depletion.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): [Note: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency results in a less severe immunodeficiency involving T-cells primarily.]

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Which of the following describes the specific inhibitory action of the drug hydroxyurea on the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase?
options: Permanent covalent modification of the R1 subunit sulfhydryl groups
Inhibition of thioredoxin reductase, preventing enzyme regeneration
Destruction of the tyrosyl free radical required for enzymatic activity
Competitive inhibition at the activity site by mimicking dATP
Allosteric inhibition at the substrate specificity site
correctOption: Destruction of the tyrosyl free radical required for enzymatic activity
optionExplanations: While the enzyme utilizes sulfhydryl groups, hydroxyurea's primary mechanism is the destruction of the free radical, not covalent modification of those groups.
Hydroxyurea targets ribonucleotide reductase directly; it does not inhibit thioredoxin reductase, which is a separate enzyme in the regeneration pathway.
Correct. Hydroxyurea quenches a free radical (specifically a tyrosyl radical on the R2 subunit) that is essential for the reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl group of the ribose sugar.
Hydroxyurea does not act as a structural analog of dATP and does not compete for the allosteric activity site.
The drug does not bind to the specificity sites that regulate which nucleotide is being reduced; it causes overall enzyme inactivation by radical destruction.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): The drug hydroxyurea destroys the free radical required for enzymic activity of ribonucleotide reductase, and thus inhibits the generation of substrates for DNA synthesis.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: In the synthesis of dTMP from dUMP, how does the administration of methotrexate indirectly lead to a decrease in the cellular concentration of thymidine nucleotides?
options: By preventing the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate from dihydrofolate.
By irreversibly binding to the active site of thymidylate synthase.
By acting as a structural analog of uracil to compete for the enzyme.
By inhibiting the transport of folate into the mitochondrial matrix.
By increasing the degradation of dUMP to beta-alanine.
correctOption: By preventing the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate from dihydrofolate.
optionExplanations: The thymidylate synthase reaction oxidizes THF to DHF. Methotrexate blocks DHFR, preventing DHF from being recycled back to THF, which is required to supply the one-carbon methyl group for dTMP synthesis.
5-fluorouracil (as 5-FdUMP) is the drug that binds irreversibly to thymidylate synthase; methotrexate binds to dihydrofolate reductase.
Methotrexate is an analog of folic acid, not uracil; 5-fluorouracil is the drug that mimics the pyrimidine base.
While methotrexate may affect various folate processes, its primary mechanism is the inhibition of DHFR in the cytosol and mitochondria, not specifically a transport defect.
Methotrexate does not increase dUMP degradation; it leads to an accumulation of dUMP because it cannot be methylated to dTMP due to lack of folate cofactors.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): DHF can be reduced to THF by dihydrofolate reductase... an enzyme that is inhibited by drugs such as methotrexate. By decreasing the supply of THF, these folate analogs... prevent methylation of dUMP to dTMP.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: An 8-month-old male infant presents with severe megaloblastic anemia that is unresponsive to vitamin B12 and folate supplementation. Physical examination reveals significant growth retardation and lethargy. Urinalysis demonstrates the presence of orange, needle-shaped crystals. Laboratory studies show normal blood ammonia levels and normal serum amino acids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Hereditary UMP synthase deficiency
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase deficiency
Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome
Adenosine deaminase deficiency
correctOption: Hereditary UMP synthase deficiency
optionExplanations: Hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) presents with megaloblastic anemia (due to lack of pyrimidines for DNA synthesis), failure to thrive, and orotic acid crystalluria, without hyperammonemia.
While this enzyme is in the pathway, hereditary orotic aciduria is specifically defined by the failure of the UMP synthase domains (the steps following dihydroorotate production).
OTC deficiency causes orotic aciduria but is characterized by severe hyperammonemia and lack of megaloblastic anemia, which contradicts this patient's presentation.
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome presents with hyperuricemia (gout/stones) and self-mutilation, but not orotic aciduria or megaloblastic anemia; it involves purine salvage, not pyrimidine synthesis.
Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes SCID (immune failure) due to dATP accumulation and T/B-cell depletion, not megaloblastic anemia or orotic aciduria.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in poor growth, megaloblastic anemia, and the excretion of large amounts of orotate in the urine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The antineoplastic agent 5-fluorouracil exerts its cytotoxic effect by being metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which then acts as a 'suicide inhibitor' of which enzyme?
options: Thymidylate synthase
Orotidylate decarboxylase
PRPP synthetase
Dihydrofolate reductase
Ribonucleotide reductase
correctOption: Thymidylate synthase
optionExplanations: 5-FdUMP binds covalently and irreversibly to thymidylate synthase, preventing the methylation of dUMP to dTMP, thus halting DNA synthesis.
Orotidylate decarboxylase is a domain of UMP synthase and is not the primary target of 5-fluorouracil.
PRPP synthetase is regulated by purine nucleotides and is involved in both purine and pyrimidine synthesis, but it is not targeted by 5-fluorouracil.
Dihydrofolate reductase is inhibited by methotrexate, not by the 5-FdUMP metabolite of 5-fluorouracil.
Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea or dATP; 5-fluorouracil targets a later step in pyrimidine nucleotide processing.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a 'suicide' inhibitor.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A pediatric patient presents with high levels of orotic acid in the urine. To determine if this is caused by a urea cycle defect (OTC deficiency) or a pyrimidine synthesis defect (UMP synthase deficiency), which laboratory finding would be most definitive?
options: Activity of xanthine oxidase in the liver
Intracellular PRPP levels
Blood ammonia levels
Presence of urate crystals in the urine
Presence of megaloblastic anemia
correctOption: Blood ammonia levels
optionExplanations: Xanthine oxidase is involved in purine degradation to uric acid and has no physiological role in the production or metabolic block leading to the excretion of orotic acid in either disorder. (201 words)

PRPP levels may be altered in both conditions due to different regulatory responses (consumption or lack of feedback), but ammonia levels provide a direct functional readout of the mitochondrial urea cycle.

OTC deficiency prevents the detoxification of ammonia in the urea cycle, leading to hyperammonemia. In contrast, UMP synthase deficiency is a primary defect in pyrimidine synthesis and does not affect the urea cycle's ability to handle ammonia.
Urate crystals (monosodium urate or uric acid) are associated with purine degradation and gout, not the pyrimidine synthesis defects or urea cycle failures that cause orotic acid accumulation.

While megaloblastic anemia is characteristic of UMP synthase deficiency due to the lack of pyrimidines for DNA synthesis, it is not typically a feature of OTC deficiency, making it a supportive but less definitive biochemical marker.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 306 (Book Page): Blood ammonia level would expected to be elevated in ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency but not in UMP synthase deficiency.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: The chemotherapeutic agent 5-Fluorouracil is often termed a 'suicide inhibitor' because it undergoes metabolic conversion to a form that binds permanently to its target. Which specific molecule is this permanent bond formed with?
options: Xanthine oxidase
Inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase
Thymidylate synthase
Ribonucleotide reductase
Dihydrofolate reductase
correctOption: Thymidylate synthase
optionExplanations: Allopurinol and febuxostat are the inhibitors of xanthine oxidase.
Mycophenolic acid is an uncompetitive inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase, not 5-Fluorouracil.
5-Fluorouracil is converted to 5-FdUMP, which acts as a suicide inhibitor by forming a stable, covalent complex with thymidylate synthase and its coenzyme.
Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase by destroying the free radical required for activity.
Methotrexate is the classic inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase, not 5-Fluorouracil.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a 'suicide' inhibitor.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: In the regulation of mammalian nucleotide synthesis, how does the presence of 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) specifically influence the pyrimidine pathway?
options: It induces the degradation of the CAD complex.
It serves as the obligate nitrogen donor for carbamoyl phosphate.
It stabilizes the mitochondrial membrane for CPS I activity.
It functions as an allosteric activator of CPS II.
It acts as a competitive inhibitor of CPS II.
correctOption: It functions as an allosteric activator of CPS II.
optionExplanations: PRPP does not cause degradation; it enhances the catalytic activity of the first domain (CPS II) within the CAD complex.
Glutamine is the nitrogen donor for the CPS II reaction; PRPP provides the ribose-phosphate moiety much later in the pathway (at the OMP stage).
PRPP is cytosolic and regulates the cytosolic CPS II; it does not influence the mitochondrial CPS I/urea cycle directly in this manner.
PRPP acts as an allosteric activator for CPS II, ensuring that pyrimidine synthesis is coordinated with the availability of the ribose-phosphate donor.
PRPP is an activator, not an inhibitor; high levels of PRPP signal a readiness to synthesize nucleotides.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): CPS II ... is activated by PRPP. [Note: Carbamoyl phosphate, synthesized by CPS I, is also a precursor of urea]

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: What is the biochemical mechanism by which Allopurinol reduces the production of uric acid in patients with gout?
options: It inhibits adenosine deaminase to prevent the conversion of adenosine to inosine.
It competitively inhibits PRPP synthetase to lower the pool of activated pentoses.
It activates hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase to increase purine salvage.
It is converted to oxypurinol, which acts as a suicide inhibitor of xanthine oxidase.
It acts as a structural analog of thymine to inhibit DNA polymerase activity.
correctOption: It is converted to oxypurinol, which acts as a suicide inhibitor of xanthine oxidase.
optionExplanations: Adenosine deaminase is inhibited by dATP in SCID, not by allopurinol, which focuses on the final stages of purine degradation.
Allopurinol does not directly inhibit PRPP synthetase; its effect on de novo synthesis is secondary to hypoxanthine salvage consuming PRPP.
Allopurinol does not activate HGPRT; however, in the presence of functional HGPRT, the salvaged hypoxanthine (accumulated due to XO inhibition) helps consume PRPP.
Allopurinol is metabolized by xanthine oxidase to oxypurinol, which binds tightly to the enzyme's active site, preventing the further oxidation of hypoxanthine and xanthine into uric acid.
Allopurinol is a purine (hypoxanthine) analog, not a pyrimidine (thymine) analog, and it does not directly target DNA polymerase in the treatment of gout.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): Allopurinol, a structural analog of hypoxanthine, inhibits uric acid synthesis... Allopurinol is converted in the body to oxypurinol, which inhibits xanthine oxidase (XO), resulting in an accumulation of hypoxanthine and xanthine.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which set of compounds contributes the nitrogen and carbon atoms required for the de novo construction of the pyrimidine ring in mammalian cells?
options: Glutamine, CO2, and aspartic acid
Aspartate, glycine, and ammonia
Ammonia, CO2, and glutamate
Glycine, aspartate, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Glutamine, glycine, and CO2
correctOption: Glutamine, CO2, and aspartic acid
optionExplanations: Correct. The pyrimidine ring is synthesized from three main precursors: glutamine (providing the amide nitrogen), carbon dioxide (CO2), and the amino acid aspartate.
Incorrect. Ammonia is not the direct nitrogen donor for the pyrimidine ring in eukaryotes; glutamine provides the nitrogen via the action of CPS II.
Incorrect. Ammonia is the nitrogen source for CPS I in the urea cycle, whereas CPS II in pyrimidine synthesis specifically utilizes glutamine.
Incorrect. This combination (glycine, aspartate, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate) describes the atomic donors for the purine ring, not the pyrimidine ring.
Incorrect. Glycine is a characteristic donor for the purine ring (contributing carbons 4, 5, and nitrogen 7) but is not involved in pyrimidine ring synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): The sources of the atoms in the pyrimidine ring are glutamine, CO 2 , and aspartic acid (Figure 22.19). [Note: Glutamine and aspartic acid are thus required for both purine and pyrimidine synthesis.]

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A 45-year-old female receiving high-dose chemotherapy for breast cancer is prescribed Methotrexate. She soon develops painful oral ulcers and a significant drop in her white blood cell count. What is the underlying biochemical rationale for these specific adverse effects?
options: Accumulation of dihydrofolate which directly lyses rapidly dividing cells.
Direct covalent binding of the drug to RNA polymerase in the gastrointestinal tract.
Depletion of tetrahydrofolate levels, which arrests DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing tissues.
Feedback inhibition of xanthine oxidase, causing a buildup of toxic purine bases.
Inhibition of PRPP synthetase leading to a total loss of pentose sugars.
correctOption: Depletion of tetrahydrofolate levels, which arrests DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing tissues.
optionExplanations: While dihydrofolate does accumulate when DHFR is inhibited, it is not directly cytolytic; the toxicity arises from the lack of reduced folate (THF) required for nucleotide synthesis.
Methotrexate does not inhibit RNA polymerase; its primary target is dihydrofolate reductase, which impacts the supply of DNA/RNA precursors rather than the assembly of RNA.

Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, preventing the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate (THF). THF is essential for the synthesis of purines and thymidine; without it, DNA replication fails, specifically affecting high-turnover tissues like bone marrow and GI mucosa.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, not Methotrexate. Methotrexate affects the de novo synthesis pathway of purines, not their terminal degradation to uric acid.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, not PRPP synthetase. PRPP levels might actually increase if purine synthesis is slowed, but MTX does not target pentose synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Inhibitors of human purine synthesis are extremely toxic to tissues... including those of bone marrow, skin, gastrointestinal (GI) tract, immune system, or hair follicles. As a result, individuals taking such anticancer drugs can experience adverse effects, including anemia, scaly skin, GI tract disturbance, immunodeficiencies, and hair loss.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
coreConcept: Adenylate kinase function in metabolic equilibrium
statement: In skeletal muscle during high-intensity exercise, the turnover of ATP is extremely high. Which enzyme is critical for maintaining an equilibrium among AMP, ADP, and ATP under these conditions?
options: Adenylosuccinate lyase
IMP dehydrogenase
Adenylate kinase
GMP synthetase
Guanylate kinase
correctOption: Adenylate kinase
optionExplanations: Adenylosuccinate lyase is responsible for cleaving adenylosuccinate to AMP and fumarate; it does not participate in nucleoside monophosphate/diphosphate/triphosphate interconversion.
IMP dehydrogenase is involved in the synthesis of GMP and does not interact with the phosphorylation states of adenine nucleotides.
Adenylate kinase (also known as myokinase in muscle) catalyzes the reaction (AMP + ATP <-> 2 ADP), allowing the cell to rapidly balance its adenine nucleotide pool.
GMP synthetase converts XMP to GMP and is not involved in the energetic balancing of adenine nucleotides.
Guanylate kinase is specific for the phosphorylation of GMP to GDP and is not involved in the ATP/ADP/AMP equilibrium.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page) / 531: Adenylate kinase is particularly active in liver and muscle, where the turnover of energy from ATP is high. Its function is to maintain an equilibrium among AMP, ADP, and ATP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: What is the biochemical name of the base found in the 'parent' purine nucleotide Inosine Monophosphate (IMP)?
options: Xanthine
Orotate
Guanine
Hypoxanthine
Adenine
correctOption: Hypoxanthine
optionExplanations: Xanthine is the base found in Xanthosine Monophosphate (XMP), an intermediate in GMP synthesis, and is also an intermediate in purine degradation.
Orotate is a pyrimidine base and is the 'parent' base for the pyrimidine pathway, not the purine pathway.
Guanine is the base found in GMP; it is formed by oxidizing and then aminating the hypoxanthine ring of IMP.
Hypoxanthine is the nitrogenous base that, when attached to a ribose 5-phosphate, forms the parent purine nucleotide IMP.
Adenine is the base found in AMP; it is formed by adding an amino group to the hypoxanthine ring of IMP via the adenylosuccinate intermediate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): synthesis of inosine monophosphate (IMP, whose base is hypoxanthine) are illustrated in Figure 22.7.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: Regulation of Purine Synthesis via Salvage
statement: In patients with normal levels of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT), how does the administration of allopurinol indirectly lead to a decrease in de novo purine synthesis?
options: By increasing the renal excretion of the metabolic precursor glutamine
By promoting the salvage of hypoxanthine, which consumes PRPP and produces inhibitory nucleotides
By inhibiting the enzyme PRPP synthetase directly through allosteric binding
By inhibiting the synthesis of N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
By chemically degrading the ribose 5-phosphate required for PRPP formation
correctOption: By promoting the salvage of hypoxanthine, which consumes PRPP and produces inhibitory nucleotides
optionExplanations: Allopurinol has no effect on the renal handling or transport of glutamine.
Allopurinol leads to hypoxanthine accumulation; if HGPRT is present, this hypoxanthine is salvaged to IMP. This process consumes PRPP and produces IMP/GMP which feedback-inhibit de novo synthesis.
Allopurinol and its metabolite oxypurinol inhibit xanthine oxidase, not PRPP synthetase.
Folate metabolism is targeted by drugs like methotrexate and sulfonamides, not allopurinol.
The drug does not cause chemical degradation of sugars; its action is enzymatic inhibition.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: A metabolic researcher observes that a deficiency in a urea cycle enzyme leads to an unusual overproduction of pyrimidine nucleotides. Which mechanism best explains this cross-pathway phenomenon?
options: Low urea levels remove the feedback inhibition on CPS II
N-acetylglutamate levels rise, allosterically activating CPS II
Accumulation of ammonia activates CPS II in the cytosol
Glutamine levels drop, forcing the cell to utilize ammonia via CPS II
Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency increases carbamoyl phosphate availability for pyrimidine synthesis
correctOption: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency increases carbamoyl phosphate availability for pyrimidine synthesis
optionExplanations: Urea does not provide feedback inhibition for CPS II; CPS II is regulated by UTP and PRPP.
N-acetylglutamate is an essential activator for CPS I, but it has no regulatory effect on the cytosolic CPS II.
Ammonia does not activate CPS II; it is the substrate for CPS I. CPS II uses glutamine.
Glutamine levels typically do not drop significantly enough to trigger an ammonia switch; moreover, CPS II is specific for glutamine, not ammonia.
When ornithine transcarbamylase is deficient, carbamoyl phosphate (produced by CPS I in mitochondria) accumulates and leaks into the cytosol, where it enters the pyrimidine pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 55-year-old male with a history of acute gouty arthritis is prescribed colchicine for symptom management. Which of the following best describes the biochemical mechanism by which this drug exerts its anti-inflammatory effect in the affected joint?
