optionExplanations: ADA deficiency causes a severe form of SCID (T, B, and NK cell depletion). Without treatment like bone marrow transplant or gene therapy, the severe immunodeficiency leads to fatal infections in infancy.
SCID is a genetic metabolic defect that does not resolve spontaneously; it results in metabolic toxicity that prevents the development of the immune system.
PNP (Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase) deficiency is rarer and affects T-cells primarily. ADA deficiency is more severe, affecting all major lymphocyte classes (T, B, and NK).
Self-mutilation and motor dysfunction are hallmark features of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (HGPRT deficiency), not ADA deficiency SCID.
ADA deficiency causes dATP accumulation, which inhibits DNA synthesis. While it involves purine metabolism, the clinical emergency is immunodeficiency, not kidney stones.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): Without appropriate treatment, children with this disorder [ADA deficiency SCID] usually die by the age of two. ... involving a decrease in T cells, B cells, and natural killer (NK) cells.

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: A patient with a history of recurrent gouty arthritis and high plasma urate levels is treated with allopurinol. Laboratory data shows a significant reduction in purine de novo synthesis. This additional therapeutic benefit is only possible because the patient has functional levels of which enzyme?
options: AMP deaminase
PRPP synthetase
Adenosine deaminase
Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT)
Xanthine oxidase
correctOption: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT)
optionExplanations: AMP deaminase converts AMP to IMP and is not part of the PRPP-lowering mechanism seen with allopurinol salvage.
PRPP synthetase produces the substrate (PRPP); while it is inhibited by purine nucleotides, the mechanism of reduction here depends on the salvage of the accumulated hypoxanthine.
ADA deficiency leads to dATP accumulation; it is not involved in the feedback mechanism of allopurinol-mediated purine reduction.

Allopurinol leads to hypoxanthine accumulation. If HGPRT is present, it salvages hypoxanthine into IMP, consuming PRPP and providing the end-product (IMP) for feedback inhibition, thus lowering de novo synthesis.
Xanthine oxidase is the target of allopurinol; its inhibition is the primary effect, but the reduction in de novo synthesis requires the salvage pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: A pharmaceutical scientist is designing a new antibacterial agent. She notes that while humans must obtain folic acid from their diet, bacteria must synthesize it de novo. Which class of synthetic analogues takes advantage of this specific biochemical difference to inhibit bacterial purine synthesis?
options: Nucleoside diphosphate inhibitors like Hydroxyurea
Purine analogs like Mycophenolic acid
Pyrimidine analogs like 5-Fluorouracil
PABA analogs like Sulfonamides
Folate analogs like Methotrexate
correctOption: PABA analogs like Sulfonamides
optionExplanations: Hydroxyurea targets the reduction of ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides by ribonucleotide reductase and has no direct impact on the PABA-to-folate synthesis pathway.
Mycophenolic acid inhibits the conversion of IMP to GMP and is not involved in the folate synthesis pathway or PABA competition.
5-Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine analog that inhibits thymidylate synthase and does not interfere with the pathway of folic acid synthesis from PABA.

Sulfonamides are structural analogs of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA). Bacteria require PABA to synthesize folic acid de novo, whereas humans lack this synthesis pathway and must ingest folate. By competitively inhibiting the bacterial enzyme that uses PABA, sulfonamides selectively starve bacteria of the tetrahydrofolate needed for purine synthesis.
Folate analogs like methotrexate inhibit dihydrofolate reductase in both humans and bacteria; they do not target the de novo synthesis of folic acid itself and are therefore toxic to human cells.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): [Sulfonamides are structural analogs of para-aminobenzoic acid that competitively inhibit bacterial synthesis of folic acid. . . Humans cannot synthesize folic acid, and must rely on external sources of this vitamin. Therefore, sulfa drugs do not interfere with human purine synthesis.]

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: Which of the following molecules serves as the primary allosteric activator of the X-linked enzyme PRPP synthetase (ribose phosphate pyrophosphokinase)?
options: Inorganic phosphate (Pi)
Guanosine monophosphate (GMP)
Uridine triphosphate (UTP)
Guanosine triphosphate (GTP)
Adenosine monophosphate (AMP)
correctOption: Inorganic phosphate (Pi)
optionExplanations: Inorganic phosphate is the critical activator of PRPP synthetase, signaling the need for nucleotide precursor production when energy/phosphate levels are available.
GMP is a purine nucleotide that provides feedback inhibition to PRPP synthetase to prevent unnecessary synthesis of the ribose 5-phosphate donor.
UTP is a regulator of the pyrimidine pathway (specifically inhibiting CPS II) but is not the primary activator of the purine-initiating enzyme PRPP synthetase.
GTP, like other purine nucleotides, acts as an allosteric inhibitor of this enzyme to regulate the overall pool of purines.
AMP is an inhibitor, not an activator, of PRPP synthetase as it represents the end-product of the purine pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): This X-linked enzyme is activated by inorganic phosphate and inhibited by purine nucleotides (end-product inhibition).

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
coreConcept: Differential Case: OTC Deficiency vs Orotic Aciduria
statement: A newborn presents with severe vomiting, lethargy, and a blood pH of 7.55 (alkalosis). Laboratory testing shows a blood ammonia level of 600 µmol/L (Normal < 50) and a very low blood urea nitrogen (BUN). High levels of orotic acid are found in the urine. Which enzyme deficiency is most likely?
options: Argininosuccinate lyase
UMP synthase
Dihydroorotase
Ornithine transcarbamylase
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I
correctOption: Ornithine transcarbamylase
optionExplanations: Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency causes hyperammonemia, but it typically does not present with the massive orotic aciduria seen in OTC deficiency because the metabolic block is further downstream.
UMP synthase deficiency causes orotic aciduria and megaloblastic anemia, but blood ammonia levels remain normal because the urea cycle is unaffected.
Dihydroorotase is an enzyme in the pyrimidine synthesis pathway; its deficiency would not cause hyperammonemia or elevated orotic acid (it would cause accumulation of carbamoyl aspartate).

Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency causes hyperammonemia (as it is a urea cycle defect) and results in the accumulation of carbamoyl phosphate, which then shunts into the cytosol to produce excessive orotic acid.
CPS I deficiency causes hyperammonemia, but since carbamoyl phosphate cannot be made, orotic acid levels would be low, not high.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Defects in ornithine transcarbamylase of the urea cycle promote pyrimidine synthesis due to increased availability of carbamoyl phosphate... [Comparison Table Figure 22.20]

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which of the following sets of molecules provide the essential atoms required for the de novo construction of the pyrimidine ring in mammalian cells?
options: Ammonia, Aspartic acid, and Carbon Dioxide
Glutamine, Aspartic acid, and Carbon Dioxide
Aspartic acid, Glycine, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Glutamine, Aspartic acid, and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
Glutamine, Glycine, and Carbon Dioxide
correctOption: Glutamine, Aspartic acid, and Carbon Dioxide
optionExplanations: While ammonia is used by Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I in the urea cycle, pyrimidine synthesis specifically utilizes the amide group of glutamine via CPS II.
Correct. Glutamine provides the amide nitrogen, CO2 provides a carbon, and aspartic acid provides the remaining three carbons and one nitrogen to form the pyrimidine ring.
This combination (Glycine and N10-formyltetrahydrofolate) is characteristic of purine synthesis; pyrimidines do not use glycine in their ring structure.
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate is a carbon donor for purine synthesis and the methylation of dUMP to dTMP, but it does not contribute to the initial de novo pyrimidine ring construction.
Glycine is a precursor specifically for the purine ring, contributing carbons 4 and 5 and nitrogen 7, but it is not used in pyrimidine synthesis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): The sources of the atoms in the pyrimidine ring are glutamine, CO 2 , and aspartic acid (Figure 22.19).

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: What is the 'parent' purine nucleotide from which both Adenosine Monophosphate (AMP) and Guanosine Monophosphate (GMP) are derived during de novo synthesis?
options: Hypoxanthine
Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
Adenylosuccinate
5-Phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP)
Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)
correctOption: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
optionExplanations: Hypoxanthine is the nitrogenous base of IMP, but the term 'parent nucleotide' refers to the sugar-phosphate-base complex, which is IMP.
IMP is defined as the parent purine nucleotide because the de novo pathway first constructs the purine ring on a ribose to form IMP, which is then branched to form either AMP or GMP.
Adenylosuccinate is an intermediate only in the AMP synthesis branch.
PRPP is the 'activated pentose' used to start the purine ring construction, but it is not a complete nucleotide base-containing 'parent' like IMP.
XMP is an intermediate only in the GMP synthesis branch, not the AMP branch.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): Synthesis of inosine monophosphate, the “parent” purine nucleotide... leading to the synthesis of inosine monophosphate (IMP, whose base is hypoxanthine).

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
coreConcept: Reciprocal substrate regulation of IMP branching
statement: If a cell has adequate levels of ATP but very low levels of GTP, how is the conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) regulated to correct this imbalance?
options: The de novo pathway will be completely inhibited at the PRPP amidotransferase step.
ATP will inhibit IMP dehydrogenase to stop GMP production.
ATP will activate adenylosuccinate synthetase to increase AMP production.
IMP will be diverted toward GMP synthesis because the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.
IMP will be diverted toward AMP synthesis because the synthesis of AMP requires ATP.
correctOption: IMP will be diverted toward GMP synthesis because the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.
optionExplanations: The de novo pathway is only completely turned off if *both* AMP and GMP are present in adequate amounts to inhibit the committed amidotransferase step.
ATP does not inhibit IMP dehydrogenase; GMP is the inhibitor for that enzyme.
ATP is not an activator of adenylosuccinate synthetase; GTP is its required substrate/energy source.

Because GMP synthesis requires ATP as an energy source, high levels of ATP drive the production of GMP from IMP. Conversely, AMP synthesis requires GTP. This reciprocal energy requirement ensures that the cell produces whichever nucleotide is in shorter supply.
AMP synthesis requires GTP, not ATP. Therefore, if GTP is low, AMP synthesis is restricted.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP... This provides a mechanism for diverting IMP to the synthesis of the species of purine present in lesser amounts.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase is unique in its ability to handle both purine and pyrimidine substrates. Which specific class of nucleotides does this enzyme utilize as its primary substrate to produce DNA precursors?
options: Ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs)
Ribonucleoside triphosphates (NTPs)
Deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs)
Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs)
Ribonucleoside monophosphates (NMPs)
correctOption: Ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs)
optionExplanations: Ribonucleotide reductase specifically reduces the 2'-OH of ribonucleoside diphosphates (ADP, GDP, CDP, UDP) to form deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates.
Ribonucleoside triphosphates (like ATP or CTP) serve as allosteric regulators of RNR but are not the substrates for reduction.
Deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates are the *products* of the RNR reaction, not the substrates.

Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates are the final building blocks of DNA, formed by the phosphorylation of the products of the RNR reaction; they also serve as regulators of the enzyme's activity and specificity.
Ribonucleoside monophosphates (like AMP or UMP) must be phosphorylated to diphosphates by kinases before RNR can act on them.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): Ribonucleotide reductase (ribonucleoside diphosphate reductase) is... specific for the reduction of purine nucleoside diphosphates (ADP and GDP), and pyrimidine nucleoside diphosphates, cytidine diphosphate (CDP) and uridine diphosphate (UDP)

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A patient with chronic overproduction of uric acid is treated with allopurinol. In individuals with functional HGPRT, how does this drug treatment help down-regulate the de novo purine synthesis pathway?
options: Salvage of accumulated hypoxanthine consumes PRPP and produces inhibitory nucleotides
Allopurinol competitively inhibits the amidotransferase enzyme
Allopurinol directly inhibits PRPP synthetase
Allopurinol increases the degradation of orotate
Allopurinol prevents the conversion of IMP to AMP
correctOption: Salvage of accumulated hypoxanthine consumes PRPP and produces inhibitory nucleotides
optionExplanations: By blocking xanthine oxidase, hypoxanthine levels rise; HGPRT then salvages this hypoxanthine into IMP, consuming PRPP (a substrate for de novo synthesis) and generating IMP (an inhibitor of de novo synthesis).
Allopurinol's active metabolite oxypurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, not the amidotransferase directly.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, it does not directly target PRPP synthetase.
Allopurinol is a purine analog; it does not significantly impact orotate degradation which is a pyrimidine process.
Allopurinol does not block the conversion of IMP to AMP; that process requires adenylosuccinate synthetase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A 55-year-old patient with colorectal cancer is treated with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). This drug is metabolically activated to 5-FdUMP, which then binds to an enzyme to inhibit the synthesis of dTMP. Which enzyme is the direct target of this 'suicide' inhibition?
options: Thymidylate synthase
Dihydrofolate reductase
Ribonucleotide reductase
CTP synthetase
Orotidylate decarboxylase
correctOption: Thymidylate synthase
optionExplanations: Correct. 5-FdUMP acts as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase, preventing the methylation of dUMP to dTMP, which is essential for DNA synthesis.
Dihydrofolate reductase is the target of Methotrexate, not 5-FU. While 5-FU affects the folate cycle indirectly by depleting THF, it is not the direct target.
Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea or dATP, not 5-FU. This enzyme converts ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides.
CTP synthetase converts UTP to CTP; while this is a pyrimidine enzyme, it is not the target of 5-FU.
Orotidylate decarboxylase is a domain of UMP synthase; its deficiency causes orotic aciduria, but it is not the target of 5-FU.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 303 (Book Page): 5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a 'suicide' inhibitor.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: A 45-year-old male undergoing renal transplantation is prescribed mycophenolic acid to prevent graft rejection. This drug's clinical efficacy is primarily due to its ability to deprive T and B cells of which nucleotide intermediate?
options: Inosine monophosphate
Xanthosine monophosphate
Adenylosuccinate
Adenosine triphosphate
Guanosine triphosphate
correctOption: Guanosine triphosphate
optionExplanations: Inosine monophosphate (IMP) is the substrate for the inhibited enzyme; its levels would likely rise, not be the component that is deprived.
Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) levels actually decrease because the enzyme that produces it (IMP dehydrogenase) is inhibited by mycophenolic acid.
Adenylosuccinate is an intermediate in the AMP branch. Mycophenolic acid inhibits IMP dehydrogenase, which is part of the GMP branch.
ATP synthesis is part of the AMP branch; mycophenolic acid does not target this pathway directly, although overall purine balance may be affected indirectly.

By inhibiting IMP dehydrogenase, the synthesis of XMP and subsequently GMP is blocked. This leads to a deficiency in guanine nucleotides (GMP, GDP, and GTP), which are essential for DNA replication in lymphocytes.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): The drug [Mycophenolic Acid] deprives rapidly proliferating T and B cells of key components of nucleic acids. [Figure 22.8 identifies it as a reversible inhibitor of IMP dehydrogenase].

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: In the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines, where is the enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase located within the cell?
options: Cytosol
Plasma membrane
Endoplasmic reticulum
Inner mitochondrial membrane
Nucleus
correctOption: Inner mitochondrial membrane
optionExplanations: While most enzymes of the pyrimidine pathway (CAD complex and UMP synthase) are cytosolic, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is the exception.
The plasma membrane contains transporters for nucleosides but does not house the enzymes for pyrimidine ring construction.
The endoplasmic reticulum is involved in protein and lipid synthesis, not the de novo synthesis of the pyrimidine ring.
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is uniquely localized to the inner mitochondrial membrane, where it links pyrimidine synthesis to the electron transport chain.
Nucleotides are used in the nucleus, but their de novo synthesis occurs in the cytosol and mitochondria.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. All other enzymes in pyrimidine biosynthesis are cytosolic.

category: Differentiate between CPS I and II
statement: Which molecule serves as the direct source of nitrogen for the reaction catalyzed by the mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate synthetase isozyme?
options: Ammonia
Glutamate
Glutamine
Aspartate
Alanine
correctOption: Ammonia
optionExplanations: CPS I (mitochondrial) specifically fixes free ammonia (NH3) into carbamoyl phosphate.
Glutamate often provides the ammonia via glutamate dehydrogenase, but the ammonia itself is the direct substrate for CPS I.
Glutamine is the nitrogen donor for CPS II (the cytosolic isozyme), not CPS I.
Aspartate provides the second nitrogen of urea later in the cycle, but not for the CPS I reaction.
Alanine is a carrier of nitrogen in the blood but must be processed (transaminated/deaminated) before the nitrogen enters the urea cycle as ammonia or aspartate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): [Figure 22.20 Summary of the differences between carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS) I and II] CPS I ... Source of nitrogen: Ammonia

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: In the complex allosteric regulation of ribonucleotide reductase, how does the binding of dATP differ from the binding of ATP at the activity sites?
options: Both ATP and dATP serve as activators, but ATP is specific for the R1 subunit and dATP for R2.
ATP bound to activity sites activates the enzyme, while dATP bound to the same sites inhibits overall catalytic activity.
dATP binding causes a conformational change that increases GDP reduction, while ATP decreases it.
ATP inhibits the reduction of purines, while dATP inhibits the reduction of pyrimidines.
ATP activates the enzyme at the specificity site, whereas dATP inhibits at the activity site.
correctOption: ATP bound to activity sites activates the enzyme, while dATP bound to the same sites inhibits overall catalytic activity.
optionExplanations: The subunits R1 and R2 are nonidentical and form the functional enzyme; regulation occurs via the R1 subunit which contains both allosteric sites, not via subunit-specific activation by these nucleotides.
ATP functions as a positive allosteric effector at the activity site, signaling high energy and readiness for DNA synthesis, whereas dATP is a potent feedback inhibitor that shuts down the enzyme.
Conformational changes regarding specific substrates like GDP are handled at the 'substrate specificity site,' not the primary 'activity site.'
The activity site controls the overall 'on/off' status of the enzyme for all four substrates (ADP, GDP, CDP, UDP), not just purines or pyrimidines.
ATP and dATP both bind to the activity site to regulate total flux; the specificity site is a separate allosteric site that controls which specific substrate is preferred.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme... In contrast, ATP bound to these sites activates the enzyme.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The construction of the purine ring requires atoms donated from multiple metabolic precursors. Which of the following compounds specifically provides carbon atoms at positions 4 and 5, as well as the nitrogen at position 7?
options: Glutamine
Aspartate
Glycine
Carbon dioxide
N10-Formyltetrahydrofolate
correctOption: Glycine
optionExplanations: Glutamine acts as a nitrogen donor, providing the amide nitrogens at positions 3 and 9 of the purine ring.
Aspartate contributes only a single nitrogen atom at position 1 of the purine ring structure, not multiple carbons or the nitrogen at position 7.
Glycine is unique among the precursors as it provides a three-atom component (C4, C5, and N7) to the purine ring during the early stages of de novo synthesis.
Carbon dioxide (CO2) provides only a single carbon atom at position 6 of the purine ring.
N10-Formyltetrahydrofolate provides one-carbon units specifically at positions 2 and 8 of the purine ring.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): The atoms of the purine ring are contributed by a number of compounds, including amino acids (aspartic acid, glycine, and glutamine), CO2, and N10–formyltetrahydrofolate (Figure 22.5).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: A 58-year-old male with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) is initiated on hydroxyurea therapy. Clinical monitoring shows a significant decrease in the proliferation of leukemic cells. At the molecular level, this therapeutic effect is achieved by the drug's interaction with which component of the nucleotide biosynthetic machinery?
options: Binding to the substrate specificity site to prevent GDP reduction.
Irreversible alkylation of the DNA polymerase active site.
Competitive inhibition of the PRPP binding site on the R1 subunit.
Destruction of the free radical required for enzymic activity on the R2 subunit.
Inhibition of Thioredoxin Reductase, preventing the regeneration of reduced thioredoxin.
correctOption: Destruction of the free radical required for enzymic activity on the R2 subunit.
optionExplanations: Hydroxyurea is not an allosteric regulator of the specificity site; it is a catalytic inhibitor that shuts down the entire enzyme's ability to process any of its four substrates.
Hydroxyurea is not an alkylating agent like cyclophosphamide; it targets the synthesis of the building blocks (dNTPs) rather than the DNA polymer itself.
Hydroxyurea does not interfere with PRPP (5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate) binding; PRPP is primarily involved in the earlier de novo synthesis of the purine and pyrimidine rings.

Hydroxyurea specifically quenches a tyrosyl free radical located on the R2 subunit of Ribonucleotide Reductase, which is essential for initiating the reduction reaction at the 2' position of the ribose sugar.
While Thioredoxin Reductase is vital for the enzyme's cycle, hydroxyurea's primary and direct target is the free radical within Ribonucleotide Reductase itself.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 298 (Book Page): The drug hydroxyurea destroys the free radical required for enzymic activity of ribonucleotide reductase, and thus inhibits the generation of substrates for DNA synthesis.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: In the metabolic loop that interconverts purine nucleotides, how does the cell utilize triphosphates to ensure that the production of Adenine and Guanine nucleotides is cross-regulated?
options: AMP synthesis is powered by GTP, while GMP synthesis is powered by ATP.
AMP synthesis requires ATP and GMP synthesis requires GTP.
ATP inhibits IMP dehydrogenase, while GTP inhibits Adenylosuccinate synthetase.
Both synthesis pathways require both ATP and GTP simultaneously.
The conversion of monophosphates to diphosphates requires only GTP.
correctOption: AMP synthesis is powered by GTP, while GMP synthesis is powered by ATP.
optionExplanations: This 'cross-regulation' ensures that if GTP (and thus G-nucleotides) is high, it facilitates the synthesis of AMP. Conversely, if ATP (and thus A-nucleotides) is high, it facilitates the synthesis of GMP.
This is incorrect; if a branch used its own product for energy, it would not be self-balancing.
ATP and GTP are substrates for the opposing branches, while the end-product inhibitors are the monophosphates (AMP and GMP).
They require specific triphosphates at specific steps (GTP for AMP branch, ATP for GMP branch), not both at the same step.
Base-specific kinases primarily use ATP because its concentration is generally higher in the cell.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Note that the synthesis of AMP requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) as an energy source, whereas the synthesis of GMP requires ATP.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: In the two-step sequence converting inosine monophosphate (IMP) to adenosine monophosphate (AMP), what specific molecule is released during the second reaction to finalize the formation of the purine ring substituent?
options: Fumarate
Ammonia
Pyrophosphate
Malate
Succinate
correctOption: Fumarate
optionExplanations: Fumarate is the four-carbon dicarboxylic acid byproduct released when adenylosuccinate lyase cleaves the carbon-nitrogen bond of the aspartate moiety to leave the amino group on the purine ring.
Ammonia is not released in this step; the nitrogen from aspartate remains attached to the purine ring at the C-6 position to form the amine group of adenine.
Pyrophosphate is released during the synthesis of PRPP and during the formation of OMP in pyrimidine synthesis, but not in the conversion of adenylosuccinate to AMP.
Malate is an intermediate of the TCA cycle but is not produced or released during any step of the purine nucleotide biosynthetic pathway.
Succinate is not released; the molecule attached is aspartate, and only its carbon skeleton minus the amino group is removed as fumarate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 295 (Book Page): Adenylosuccinate is then converted to AMP by adenylosuccinase (adenylosuccinate lyase), with the release of fumarate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which of the following compounds provides the most atoms to the skeletal structure of the purine ring during de novo synthesis?
options: Aspartic acid
Glycine
Carbon dioxide
Glutamine
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate
correctOption: Glycine
optionExplanations: Aspartic acid contributes only a single nitrogen atom (N1) to the purine ring structure.
Glycine is unique among the precursors as it provides a three-atom sequence (C4, C5, and N7), making it a major contributor to the ring's internal scaffold.
Carbon dioxide (CO2) contributes only a single carbon atom (C6) to the purine ring.
Glutamine provides two nitrogen atoms (N3 and N9) from its amide group, but does not provide carbons to the ring.
N10-formyltetrahydrofolate contributes two separate carbon atoms (C2 and C8) via formylation reactions, but no nitrogens.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 292 (Book Page): The atoms of the purine ring are contributed by a number of compounds, including amino acids (aspartic acid, glycine, and glutamine), CO 2 , and N 10 –formyltetrahydrofolate... Glycine contributes carbons 4 and 5 and nitrogen 7.

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: In the human cell, the synthesis of pyrimidines involves enzymes located in different compartments. While most enzymes are cytosolic, the enzyme producing orotic acid is unique. Where is the carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II enzyme located compared to the enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase?
options: CPS II is on the inner mitochondrial membrane, while dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is in the cytosol
CPS II is in the cytosol, while dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is on the inner mitochondrial membrane
Both are located in the cytosol
Both are located in the mitochondria
CPS II is in the nucleus, while dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is in the lysosomes
correctOption: CPS II is in the cytosol, while dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is on the inner mitochondrial membrane
optionExplanations: This reverses the actual locations; CPS II is the cytosolic regulated step.
Correct. CPS II, as part of the CAD complex, is found in the cytosol. Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is specifically not cytosolic; it is the only mitochondrial enzyme in the pyrimidine de novo pathway.
Only CPS I of the urea cycle and dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (associated with the membrane) are mitochondrial.
These enzymes are not localized to the nucleus or lysosomes for the purpose of the de novo pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page) / 531: The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. All other enzymes in pyrimidine biosynthesis are cytosolic.

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A pediatric patient with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome presents with symptoms of hyperuricemia. Which clinical finding uniquely distinguishes this condition from primary pediatric gout or other forms of inherited hyperuricemia?
options: Development of uric acid stones in the kidneys (urolithiasis)
Formation of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals in the joints
Increased urinary excretion of the end product of purine catabolism
Inflammatory response to crystal deposition in the soft tissues
Compulsive self-mutilation, such as biting of the lips and fingers
correctOption: Compulsive self-mutilation, such as biting of the lips and fingers
optionExplanations: Urolithiasis (kidney stones) occurs in many causes of overproduction of uric acid, including von Gierke's disease or chemotherapy-induced tumor lysis syndrome.
Urate crystal formation is common to all forms of gout and hyperuricemia, including Lesch-Nyhan, so it is not a distinguishing feature.
Increased uric acid excretion is the definition of hyperuricosuria, which is seen in almost all purine overproduction states, not just Lesch-Nyhan.
The inflammatory response to crystals (tophaceous gout) is the mechanism of joint pain in all gout patients; it does not help differentiate Lesch-Nyhan from other causes.
Self-mutilation is a hallmark behavioral disturbance of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and is not typically seen in other hyperuricemic conditions like primary gout or PRPP synthetase overactivity.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): In addition, the syndrome is characterized by motor dysfunction, cognitive deficits, and behavioral disturbances that include self-mutilation (biting of lips and fingers, Figure 22.11).

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: Which of the following clinical findings serves as the definitive diagnostic criterion for gout when evaluating a patient with an acutely inflamed joint?
options: Rapid resolution of symptoms following allopurinol administration
Presence of orange-colored sand-like crystals in the urine
Identification of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid
Serum uric acid level exceeding 10 mg/dL
Evidence of soft tissue nodular masses (tophi) on physical exam
correctOption: Identification of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid
optionExplanations: Response to medication is not a definitive diagnostic criterion; furthermore, allopurinol is used for long-term management, not acute attack resolution.
Orange sand in urine (urolithiasis) is more characteristic of the extreme overproduction of uric acid seen in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, though it can occur in gout.
The visualization of negatively birefringent, needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals within the joint fluid is the only definitive way to confirm gouty arthritis.
While hyperuricemia is a risk factor and common finding, it is not diagnostic because many hyperuricemic patients never develop gout.
Tophi are characteristic of chronic tophaceous gout, but they are not the definitive diagnostic gold standard required for an acute diagnosis.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): The definitive diagnosis of gout requires aspiration and examination of synovial fluid... using polarized light microscopy to confirm the presence of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: A definitive diagnosis of gout is established by the identification of which specific finding in aspirated synovial fluid?
options: Elevated levels of uric acid exceeding 7 mg/dL
Presence of allantoin crystals within neutrophils
Positive birefringent rhomboid-shaped crystals
Complete absence of adenosine deaminase activity
Negative birefringent needle-shaped crystals
correctOption: Negative birefringent needle-shaped crystals
optionExplanations: Hyperuricemia (serum urate > 7 mg/dL) is common but not definitive for gout, as many hyperuricemic individuals remain asymptomatic.
Humans do not produce allantoin as we lack urate oxidase; finding 'allantoin crystals' is not possible in human medical diagnostics.
Positive birefringent rhomboid crystals are characteristic of pseudogout (calcium pyrophosphate deposition), not true gout.
Absence of ADA activity leads to SCID, which is a separate immunodeficiency disorder, not the inflammatory arthritis of gout.
Monosodium urate crystals in gout are needle-shaped and show strong negative birefringence under polarized light, often found within polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): The definitive diagnosis of gout requires aspiration and examination of synovial fluid... using polarized light microscopy to confirm the presence of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals (Figure 22.18).

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: Ribonucleotide reductase is a highly regulated enzyme that ensures a balanced supply of the four deoxyribonucleotides. Which molecule acts as a general 'off switch' by binding to the activity sites and inhibiting the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme?
options: dGTP
dTTP
dATP
ATP
dCTP
correctOption: dATP
optionExplanations: dGTP regulates substrate specificity at the specificity sites; it does not serve as the primary global inhibitor of the activity site.
dTTP binds to the substrate specificity sites to regulate which specific ribonucleotide is reduced, rather than acting as a general inhibitor at the activity site.
dATP is the classic feedback inhibitor. When its levels are high, it binds to the activity sites (not the specificity sites), shutting down all deoxyribonucleotide production.
ATP binding to the activity sites actually activates ribonucleotide reductase, signaling that the cell has sufficient energy for DNA synthesis.
dCTP is one of the products but is not the primary allosteric inhibitor of the enzyme's overall activity site.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme and, therefore, prevents the reduction of any of the four nucleoside diphosphates.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A pharmacological researcher is investigating the metabolic conversion of various purine analogs. Which active metabolite is primarily responsible for the long-term inhibition of xanthine oxidase in patients treated for chronic gout?
options: Isourate
Hypoxanthine
Oxypurinol
Alloxanthine
Xanthosine monophosphate
correctOption: Oxypurinol
optionExplanations: Isourate is not a recognized metabolite in human purine degradation or pharmacological inhibition pathways mentioned in the text.
Hypoxanthine is a natural purine base and the substrate for xanthine oxidase, not an inhibitor; allopurinol is a structural analog of this compound.

Oxypurinol is the converted active form of Allopurinol. It acts as a transitional-state analog that binds tightly to xanthine oxidase, effectively reducing the production of uric acid by keeping the enzyme in an inhibited state longer than the parent drug.
Alloxanthine is another name for oxypurinol, but Oxypurinol is the standard pharmacological nomenclature used in the primary text provided to describe the active metabolite.
Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) is an intermediate in the de novo synthesis of GMP from IMP and is not involved in the inhibition of xanthine oxidase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): [Allopurinol is converted in the body to oxypurinol, which inhibits xanthine oxidase (XO), resulting in an accumulation of hypoxanthine and xanthine]

category: Interpret Orotic aciduria in relevance to nucleotides and urea
statement: In a patient with hereditary orotic aciduria, the rate of pyrimidine ring synthesis is significantly accelerated. Which regulatory mechanism explains this phenomenon?
options: Inhibition of aspartate transcarbamoylase by high PRPP levels
Activation of the urea cycle enzymes by accumulated orotate
Activation of CPS II by elevated levels of intracellular UTP
Decrease in feedback inhibition of CPS II due to low intracellular UTP levels
Competitive inhibition of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase by orotic acid
correctOption: Decrease in feedback inhibition of CPS II due to low intracellular UTP levels
optionExplanations: PRPP is an activator of CPS II, not an inhibitor of aspartate transcarbamoylase.
Orotate does not activate urea cycle enzymes; the pathways are linked by carbamoyl phosphate, but orotate itself is an end-product metabolite in this context.
UTP is an allosteric inhibitor, not an activator, of CPS II; high levels would slow the pathway down.
In hereditary orotic aciduria, the block at UMP synthase prevents UTP formation. The lack of UTP removes the normal feedback inhibition on CPS II, leading to uncontrolled pathway activity.
Hereditary orotic aciduria is caused by a block downstream of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase; orotic acid accumulation is a result, not an inhibitor of the earlier step.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): CPS II is inhibited by UTP (the end product of this pathway...). ... Page 295 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in... excretion of large amounts of orotate.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
coreConcept: CPS I vs CPS II Functional Contrast
statement: A laboratory researcher is distinguishing between the two isoforms of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS). Which characteristic is unique to the isoform involved in the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway?
options: Localization within the mitochondrial matrix
Utilization of ammonia as the primary nitrogen source
Participation in the first step of the urea cycle
Requirement of N-acetylglutamate for catalytic activity
Inhibition by uridine triphosphate (UTP)
correctOption: Inhibition by uridine triphosphate (UTP)
optionExplanations: CPS I is located in the mitochondria, while CPS II is a cytosolic enzyme, reflecting their separate roles in the urea cycle and nucleotide synthesis respectively.
CPS I (the urea cycle enzyme) uses free ammonia, whereas CPS II uses the amide group of glutamine as its nitrogen source.
Participation in the urea cycle is the hallmark of CPS I; CPS II is dedicated to de novo pyrimidine synthesis.
N-acetylglutamate is a mandatory cofactor for CPS I; CPS II activity does not depend on this molecule.
CPS II is uniquely inhibited by the pyrimidine end-product UTP, allowing for metabolic flux control based on cellular nucleotide needs.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 294 (Book Page): CPS II is inhibited by UTP (the end product of this pathway...)... A comparison of the two enzymes is presented in Figure 22.20.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A clinician is deciding between prescribing probenecid or allopurinol for a patient with gout. Which diagnostic contrast justifies the use of allopurinol over uricosuric agents like probenecid?
options: Patient exhibits primary underexcretion of uric acid with normal renal function
Patient shows presence of negatively birefringent crystals in synovial fluid
Patient has low levels of xanthine and hypoxanthine in the urine
Patient is classified as an 'overproducer' of uric acid
Patient has frequent acute attacks but normal plasma urate levels
correctOption: Patient is classified as an 'overproducer' of uric acid
optionExplanations: Probenecid is specifically indicated for 'underexcretors' because it increases renal excretion of uric acid. It would not be the primary choice for overproducers.
The presence of crystals confirms the diagnosis of gout but does not differentiate between the need for an overproduction inhibitor (Allopurinol) vs. an excretion enhancer (Probenecid).
Low levels of xanthine in the urine are normal; allopurinol actually causes an increase in xanthine and hypoxanthine because it inhibits their conversion to uric acid.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase to reduce the production of uric acid, making it the preferred drug for patients who synthesize too much purine (overproducers).
Gout treatment is based on lowering urate levels below the saturation point; drugs are chosen based on the underlying mechanism of hyperuricemia, not just attack frequency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): Uricosuric agents, such as probenecid or sulfinpyrazone... are used in patients who are “underexcretors” of uric acid. Allopurinol... is used in patients who are “overproducers” of uric acid.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A rare genetic defect results in the deficiency of a bifunctional polypeptide containing both orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase activities. What is the hallmark laboratory finding in this condition?
options: Deficiency of thymidine monophosphate (TMP) in skeletal muscle only
Hypouricemia
Increased uric acid crystals in the urine
Megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to Vitamin B12
Elevated blood ammonia levels
correctOption: Megaloblastic anemia non-responsive to Vitamin B12
optionExplanations: The deficiency of pyrimidines in orotic aciduria is systemic, affecting all rapidly dividing cells, not just skeletal muscle.
Hypouricemia is characteristic of xanthine oxidase deficiency or purine metabolic defects, not orotic aciduria.
The urine shows orotic acid (orotate), not uric acid. Uric acid crystals are typical of gout or Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
Orotic aciduria causes a megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to B12 or folate because the defect lies in the inability to synthesize the pyrimidine ring for DNA.
Ammonia levels are elevated in urea cycle defects (like OTC deficiency), which can cause secondary orotic aciduria, but not in primary UMP synthase deficiency.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): Low activities of orotidine phosphate decarboxylase and orotate phosphoribosyltransferase result in poor growth, megaloblastic anemia, and the excretion of large amounts of orotate in the urine.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
coreConcept: Immediate Hydrogen Donors in RNR Catalysis
statement: During the catalytic cycle of ribonucleotide reductase, what is the direct source of the hydrogen atoms used to reduce the 2'-hydroxyl group of the substrate?
options: A hydroxyl radical generated by the R2 subunit
Two sulfhydryl groups on the ribonucleotide reductase enzyme itself
Two sulfhydryl groups on the thioredoxin protein
A specific methyl group donated by N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate
Reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)
correctOption: Two sulfhydryl groups on the ribonucleotide reductase enzyme itself
optionExplanations: The R2 subunit contains a stable tyrosyl free radical required to initiate the reaction, but this radical does not serve as the hydrogen donor for the reduction of the sugar moiety.

Correct. The immediate reduction of the 2'-OH group is performed by two cysteine residues (sulfhydryl groups) within the active site of the ribonucleotide reductase enzyme, which then form a disulfide bridge.

Thioredoxin serves to regenerate the reduced state of ribonucleotide reductase after the catalytic event has occurred, but it does not donate hydrogens directly to the ribonucleoside diphosphate substrate.
N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate is the methyl donor for thymidylate synthase in the production of dTMP, not for the reduction of ribonucleotides.
NADPH is the ultimate source of reducing equivalents in the entire pathway, but it is not the 'immediate' donor to the ribose sugar; it reduces thioredoxin reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The immediate donors of the hydrogen atoms needed for the reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl group are two sulfhydryl groups on the enzyme itself, which, during the reaction, form a disulfide bond.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The chemotherapeutic agent 5-Fluorouracil is widely used to treat solid tumors. Which statement accurately describes its primary mechanism of action in the context of pyrimidine metabolism?
options: It acts as a competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase.
It prevents the conversion of IMP to GMP by inhibiting IMP dehydrogenase.
It blocks the transport of aspartate into the mitochondria.
It inhibits the cytosolic enzyme carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
It is converted to 5-FdUMP, which serves as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase.
correctOption: It is converted to 5-FdUMP, which serves as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase.
optionExplanations: Methotrexate, not 5-Fluorouracil, is the classic competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase, though both affect the thymidylate cycle.
Mycophenolic acid is the drug that inhibits IMP dehydrogenase to prevent GMP synthesis; 5-FU is specific to the pyrimidine pathway.
Aspartate transport is relevant in the malate-aspartate shuttle and urea cycle, but is not inhibited by 5-Fluorouracil.
CPS II is regulated by UTP and PRPP, but is not the target of 5-Fluorouracil, which acts much later in the pathway at the point of dTMP synthesis.
5-Fluorouracil is a prodrug converted to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine monophosphate (5-FdUMP), which covalently binds and irreversibly inhibits thymidylate synthase, stopping dTMP production.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): [5-Fluorouracil is metabolically converted to 5-FdUMP, which becomes permanently bound to the inactivated thymidylate synthase; for this reason, the drug is called a “suicide” inhibitor.]

category: Interpret the Lesh-Nhyan syndrome
statement: A laboratory study compares the enzyme activity in a patient with classic Lesch-Nyhan syndrome to a healthy control. Which of the following findings regarding the deficiency level of HGPRT is most consistent with the clinical diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome?
options: Virtually complete deficiency of the enzyme
Increased Km for hypoxanthine with normal Vmax
Normal HGPRT activity but deficient APRT activity
A 50% reduction in enzyme activity
Increased sensitivity to allosteric inhibition
correctOption: Virtually complete deficiency of the enzyme
optionExplanations: The hallmark of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is a 'virtually complete' deficiency of HGPRT activity.
The syndrome is defined by a lack of the enzyme itself, not merely a change in its kinetic affinity (Km).
HGPRT must be deficient; APRT is a different enzyme in the salvage pathway that acts on adenine.
A 50% reduction might be seen in carriers or milder variants, but the classic syndrome requires a more profound loss.
The enzyme is absent or non-functional; allosteric sensitivity is irrelevant if the enzyme activity is zero.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): This syndrome is a rare, X-linked, recessive disorder associated with a virtually complete deficiency of HGPRT.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: Which allosteric site on ribonucleotide reductase is the primary target for dATP-mediated inhibition, and what is the outcome of this binding?
options: The activity site; it inhibits the reduction of all four nucleoside diphosphates
The substrate specificity site; it limits the reduction of GDP to dGDP
The R2 subunit; it destroys the free radical required for enzyme activity
The catalytic site; it prevents the formation of the disulfide bond
The thiol site; it prevents the regeneration of reduced thioredoxin
correctOption: The activity site; it inhibits the reduction of all four nucleoside diphosphates
optionExplanations: The activity site on the R1 subunit of ribonucleotide reductase binds dATP, which causes a global conformational change that inhibits the reduction of ADP, GDP, CDP, and UDP.
The substrate specificity site regulates which specific nucleotide is reduced based on current cellular needs; it does not shut down the entire enzyme's activity like dATP does at the activity site.
The R2 subunit contains the free radical, but it is the drug hydroxyurea, not dATP, that destroys this radical.
The catalytic site is where the reduction occurs via sulfhydryl groups; dATP binds to a separate regulatory site to control this activity.
The regeneration of thioredoxin involves thioredoxin reductase and NADPH; dATP does not interfere with this regeneration cycle.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): [The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme and, therefore, prevents the reduction of any of the four nucleoside diphosphates.]

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A 55-year-old male with a history of obesity and a diet rich in shellfish presents with a swollen, exquisitely tender right knee. Arthrocentesis is performed to distinguish between septic arthritis and gout. Which finding in the synovial fluid would definitively confirm a diagnosis of gout?
options: Presence of rhomboid-shaped calcium pyrophosphate crystals.
Absence of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase activity in leukocytes.
Needle-shaped crystals with negative birefringence under polarized light.
Detection of high concentrations of urea and xanthine oxidase.
Elevation of beta-aminoisobutyrate levels in the synovial fluid.
correctOption: Needle-shaped crystals with negative birefringence under polarized light.
optionExplanations: Rhomboid-shaped calcium pyrophosphate crystals are characteristic of pseudogout, not true gout (monosodium urate).
HGPRT deficiency is the cause of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome; while it causes gout, the diagnosis of the acute attack depends on crystal visualization, not leukocyte enzyme assays.
The gold standard for gout diagnosis is the visualization of monosodium urate crystals, which appear as needle-like structures that show negative birefringence under polarized light.
Urea is the product of amino acid nitrogen metabolism, not purine degradation; uric acid is the product that crystallizes in gout.
Beta-aminoisobutyrate is a product of thymine (pyrimidine) degradation and is not used to diagnose gout, which is a purine degradation disorder.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): The definitive diagnosis of gout requires aspiration and examination of synovial fluid (Figure 22.17) from an affected joint ... using polarized light microscopy to confirm the presence of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals (Figure 22.18).

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
coreConcept: Allopurinol and De Novo Purine Regulation
statement: In a patient with functional Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT), allopurinol treatment results in a decrease in de novo purine synthesis. What is the intermediate mechanism for this secondary effect?
options: Oxypurinol acts as a competitive inhibitor for the aspartate binding site on the purine ring.
Direct allosteric inhibition of Glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase by allopurinol itself.
The accumulation of uric acid causes a retroactive shutdown of the carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II enzyme.
Allopurinol prevents the synthesis of PRPP from ribose 5-phosphate.
The inhibition of xanthine oxidase leads to higher levels of hypoxanthine, which is salvaged to IMP, consuming PRPP and providing feedback inhibition.
correctOption: The inhibition of xanthine oxidase leads to higher levels of hypoxanthine, which is salvaged to IMP, consuming PRPP and providing feedback inhibition.
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Oxypurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase; it does not compete with aspartate in purine synthesis.
Incorrect. Allopurinol does not directly inhibit the amidotransferase; the effect is mediated through the salvage of hypoxanthine and subsequent PRPP depletion.
Incorrect. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is the regulated step of pyrimidine synthesis, not purine synthesis, and it is inhibited by UTP, not uric acid.
Incorrect. PRPP synthetase is inhibited by purine nucleotides, but allopurinol is not a direct inhibitor of the PRPP synthetase enzyme itself.

Correct. By inhibiting xanthine oxidase, allopurinol causes hypoxanthine to accumulate. In HGPRT+ patients, this hypoxanthine is salvaged to IMP. This process consumes PRPP (the activator of de novo synthesis) and produces IMP (an inhibitor), thus slowing the de novo pathway.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): [In patients with normal levels of HGPRT, the hypoxanthine can be salvaged, thus reducing the levels of PRPP and, therefore, de novo purine synthesis.]

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: In the regeneration of active ribonucleotide reductase, which molecule acts as the direct peptide coenzyme that reduces the disulfide bond formed on the enzyme?
options: Glutaredoxin
Thioredoxin
FMN
NADH
Coenzyme A
correctOption: Thioredoxin
optionExplanations: While related, thioredoxin is the specific peptide coenzyme identified in the text for this pathway.
Thioredoxin is the small protein that transfers reducing equivalents from NADPH (via thioredoxin reductase) to RNR to restore its sulfhydryl groups.
FMN (Flavin mononucleotide) is a prosthetic group in complex I and other enzymes but not the coenzyme for RNR disulfide reduction.
NADH is used in different metabolic pathways; NADPH is the specific source of power for thioredoxin reductase.
Coenzyme A is a carrier of acyl groups, not a redox coenzyme for ribonucleotide reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The source of the reducing equivalents for this purpose is thioredoxin—a peptide coenzyme of ribonucleotide reductase. ... The two sulfhydryl groups of thioredoxin donate their hydrogen atoms to ribonucleotide reductase, in the process forming a disulfide bond.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of purines (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: In the human catabolic pathway for purine nucleotides, several enzymes facilitate the step-wise degradation to the final excretory product. Which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of both hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid?
options: Adenosine deaminase
Xanthine oxidase
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase
Guanase
5'-Nucleotidase
correctOption: Xanthine oxidase
optionExplanations: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) converts adenosine to inosine; it is involved much earlier in the pathway.
Correct. Xanthine oxidase (XO) is a molybdenum-containing enzyme that catalyzes the two-step oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and then xanthine to uric acid.
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) converts nucleosides (inosine/guanosine) into free bases (hypoxanthine/guanine) by removing the ribose-1-phosphate.
Guanase deaminates guanine to form xanthine, but it does not catalyze the oxidation steps leading to uric acid.
5'-Nucleotidase removes the phosphate group from nucleotides (IMP/GMP/AMP) to produce nucleosides (inosine/guanosine/adenosine).
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): [5] Hypoxanthine is oxidized by xanthine oxidase to xanthine, which is further oxidized by xanthine oxidase to uric acid, the final product of human purine degradation.

category: Discuss the regulation of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and degradation
statement: A mutation in the gene encoding PRPP synthetase results in a variant enzyme that exhibits a significantly lower Km for ribose 5-phosphate. Which of the following metabolic consequences is most likely in this patient?
options: Reduced salvage of hypoxanthine due to decreased PRPP availability
Inhibition of the amidotransferase step by high levels of inorganic phosphate
Elevated de novo purine synthesis leading to primary hyperuricemia
Accumulation of orotic acid in the urine due to competitive inhibition
Decreased production of uric acid due to substrate depletion
correctOption: Elevated de novo purine synthesis leading to primary hyperuricemia
optionExplanations: The mutation leads to an increase in PRPP availability, which would theoretically facilitate salvage, though the dominant effect is de novo overproduction.
Inorganic phosphate is an activator of PRPP synthetase, but the primary pathology here is the altered enzyme kinetics (lower Km) leading to overactivity.
Increased PRPP availability accelerates the rate of the amidotransferase reaction (the rate-limiting step), leading to excess purine production and subsequent degradation to uric acid.
Orotic aciduria is associated with UMP synthase deficiency or the urea cycle, not directly with PRPP synthetase overactivity.
A lower Km indicates higher affinity for ribose 5-phosphate, which leads to overproduction of PRPP and consequently more uric acid, not less.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 299 (Book Page): However, several identified mutations in the gene for X-linked PRPP synthetase result in the enzyme having an increased Vmax for the production of PRPP, a lower Km for ribose 5-phosphate... increased availability of PRPP increases purine production, resulting in elevated levels of plasma uric acid.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: A laboratory analysis of cancer cells treated with 5-fluorouracil shows a significant depletion of deoxythymidine monophosphate (dTMP). This depletion leads to the inhibition of DNA replication. Which direct enzymatic reaction is being blocked to cause this depletion?
options: The reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate.
The phosphorylation of thymidine by thymidine kinase.
The methylation of dUMP by thymidylate synthase.
The reduction of UDP to dUDP by ribonucleotide reductase.
The hydrolysis of dUTP to dUMP by dUTPase.
correctOption: The methylation of dUMP by thymidylate synthase.
optionExplanations: The reduction of DHF to THF is the target of methotrexate, not 5-fluorouracil.
Thymidine kinase is a salvage enzyme; 5-FU targets the de novo synthesis pathway for dTMP.
5-FU (as 5-FdUMP) inhibits thymidylate synthase, which is the sole enzyme that methylates dUMP to produce dTMP.
While dUDP is a precursor to dTMP, 5-FU specifically targets the downstream step where dUMP is converted to dTMP.
dUTPase is essential for maintaining low dUTP levels to prevent uracil incorporation into DNA, but 5-FU does not inhibit this enzyme.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): Folate analogs not only inhibit purine synthesis... but, by preventing methylation of dUMP to dTMP, they also lower the cellular concentration of this essential component of DNA.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: In the pathophysiology of Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) caused by adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the accumulation of specific metabolites leads to the arrest of DNA synthesis. Which of the following molecular mechanisms best describes why lymphocytes are specifically targeted in this disorder?
options: Competitive inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase by deoxyadenosine
Depletion of the total pool of PRPP by excess adenosine salvage
Direct apoptosis of B cells due to high concentrations of hypoxanthine
Upregulation of xanthine oxidase causing oxidative damage to T cells
Inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase by elevated dATP levels
correctOption: Inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase by elevated dATP levels
optionExplanations: Dihydrofolate reductase is inhibited by folate analogs like methotrexate, not by deoxyadenosine; the latter affects ribonucleotide reductase.
While adenosine can be salvaged, the primary pathology is the toxic buildup of dATP inhibiting DNA synthesis, not the exhaustion of the PRPP pool.
Hypoxanthine is a normal purine intermediate and is not directly toxic; the toxicity in ADA deficiency arises from deoxy-metabolites, not hypoxanthine.
Xanthine oxidase levels are not the primary driver of lymphocyte death in ADA deficiency; the issue is localized to the buildup of adenosine/deoxyadenosine and their phosphorylated forms.

Elevated dATP acts as a potent allosteric inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase. This prevents the conversion of ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates, starving the cell of substrates for DNA replication.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): A deficiency of ADA results in an accumulation of adenosine, which is converted to its ribonucleotide or deoxyribonucleotide forms by cellular kinases. As dATP levels rise, ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited, thus preventing the production of all deoxyribose-containing nucleotides.

category: Discuss the role of Ribonucleotide reductase in Nucleotide metabolism (hydroxyurea)
statement: A researcher is studying the allosteric regulation of human ribonucleotide reductase. She observes that adding a specific nucleotide to the reaction mixture completely halts the reduction of ADP, GDP, CDP, and UDP. Which molecule was most likely added?
options: ATP
dATP
dGTP
dCTP
dTTP
correctOption: dATP
optionExplanations: ATP binding to the activity sites actually activates the enzyme, increasing the production of deoxyribonucleotides.

dATP is the physiological 'off switch' for ribonucleotide reductase. When it binds to the activity sites, it inhibits the reduction of all four ribonucleoside diphosphate substrates, preventing overproduction of deoxyribonucleotides.
dGTP regulates substrate specificity and does not act as a global inhibitor of the enzyme's catalytic function.
dCTP is a product of the pathway but is not the primary global inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase at the activity site; that role is specifically held by dATP.
dTTP binds to the substrate specificity site, regulating which specific NDP is reduced, but it does not cause overall inhibition of the enzyme's total activity.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 297 (Book Page): The binding of dATP to allosteric sites (known as the activity sites) on the enzyme inhibits the overall catalytic activity of the enzyme and, therefore, prevents the reduction of any of the four nucleoside diphosphates.

category: Discuss the synthesis and degradation of pyrimidine (De-Novo and salvage pathway)
statement: The first three enzymatic activities of the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway are housed within a single multifunctional polypeptide. Which enzymic activity is NOT a component of this CAD complex?
options: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
None of the above
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
Dihydroorotase
Aspartate transcarbamoylase
correctOption: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
optionExplanations: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane, unlike the CAD complex which is cytosolic, and it is a separate enzyme entirely.
This option is incorrect because Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is clearly excluded from the CAD cytosolic complex.
CPS II is the 'C' in the CAD complex, representing the first domain of this cytosolic multifunctional protein.
Dihydroorotase is the 'D' in the CAD complex, representing the third domain that closes the pyrimidine ring.
Aspartate transcarbamoylase is the 'A' in the CAD complex, representing the second domain that forms carbamoylaspartate.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 302 (Book Page): The first three enzymic activities in this pathway (CPS II, aspartate transcarbamoylase, and dihydroorotase) are actually three different catalytic domains of a single polypeptide chain known as CAD... The enzyme that produces orotate, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane.

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Nucleoside monophosphate kinases are essential for converting NMPs to NDPs. Which molecule is generally the primary phosphate donor for these base-specific kinases due to its high intracellular concentration?
options: GTP
ATP
Creatine Phosphate
UTP
CTP
correctOption: ATP
optionExplanations: GTP is a phosphate donor in specific reactions (like AMP synthesis) but is not the general donor for monophosphate kinases.
Correct. ATP is the universal energy currency and the primary phosphate donor for both adenylate kinase and guanylate kinase due to its abundance.
Creatine phosphate stores high-energy phosphate in muscle, but kinases in the nucleotide pathway specifically use nucleoside triphosphates like ATP.
UTP is involved in carbohydrate metabolism (UDP-glucose) but not as the primary donor for NMP kinases.
CTP is a pyrimidine triphosphate and does not serve as the primary phosphate donor for these kinases.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 296 (Book Page): ATP is generally the source of the transferred phosphate, because it is present in higher concentrations than the other nucleoside triphosphates.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 6-month-old infant is brought to the pediatric clinic with a history of recurrent fungal infections, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive. Laboratory evaluation reveals a total lymphocyte count significantly below the 5th percentile, with a complete absence of T, B, and Natural Killer (NK) cells. Biochemical analysis shows a massive accumulation of dATP. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency
Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
X-linked agammaglobulinemia
Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome
correctOption: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency
optionExplanations: The combination of profound T, B, and NK cell depletion (SCID) and the metabolic marker of elevated dATP is pathognomonic for ADA deficiency.
Hereditary Orotic Aciduria presents with megaloblastic anemia and growth retardation, but not the specific SCID phenotype or dATP accumulation.
X-linked agammaglobulinemia primarily results in a lack of B-cells and antibodies, but T-cell and NK-cell counts typically remain functional or normal.
PNP deficiency is generally less severe and primarily affects T-cells, rather than causing the total depletion of T, B, and NK cells seen in ADA-SCID.
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome presents with hyperuricemia and neurological symptoms (self-mutilation), not with the profound immunodeficiency described.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): [In its most severe form, this autosomal recessive disorder causes a type of severe combined immunodeficiency disease (SCID), involving a decrease in T cells, B cells, and natural killer (NK) cells... ADA deficiency accounts for approximately 14% of all cases of SCID.]

category: Interpret the role of synthetic analogues of nucleotides in medicine based on sign/symptoms and data e
statement: When administering allopurinol for the long-term management of hyperuricemia, the drug is metabolically transformed into a compound that provides more potent inhibition of xanthine oxidase. What is this active metabolite?
options: Hypoxanthine
Alloxanthine
Uracil
Oxypurinol
Xanthosine monophosphate
correctOption: Oxypurinol
optionExplanations: Hypoxanthine is the natural substrate for xanthine oxidase; allopurinol is its structural analog.
While 'alloxanthine' is an older name for oxypurinol, the standardized medical term in the context of this pathway and most textbooks is oxypurinol.
Uracil is a pyrimidine base and is unrelated to the metabolism of the purine analog allopurinol.
Allopurinol is oxidized by xanthine oxidase itself to oxypurinol, which then acts as a potent suicide-like inhibitor of the enzyme.
XMP is an intermediate in the GMP synthesis pathway, not a metabolite of allopurinol.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): Allopurinol is converted in the body to oxypurinol, which inhibits xanthine oxidase (XO), resulting in an accumulation of hypoxanthine and xanthine.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: A 6-month-old infant is brought to the clinic due to recurrent, severe fungal and viral infections since birth. Laboratory tests reveal a significant reduction in the absolute lymphocyte count (lymphocytopenia) involving T, B, and NK cells. Genetic testing confirms a deficiency in the enzyme Adenosine Deaminase (ADA). Which of the following best describes the intracellular biochemical environment in this patient’s lymphocytes?
options: Elevated uric acid levels within the cytoplasm causing mechanical cell rupture.
Inability to convert hypoxanthine to IMP, leading to a surge in xanthine oxidase activity.
Accumulation of dATP, which inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase and prevents DNA synthesis.
Deficiency of PRPP, which prevents the de novo synthesis of all purine nucleotides.
Decreased dATP levels leading to the overactivation of Ribonucleotide Reductase.
correctOption: Accumulation of dATP, which inhibits Ribonucleotide Reductase and prevents DNA synthesis.
optionExplanations: While ADA is part of the purine degradation pathway, the clinical pathology in SCID is caused by dATP toxicity and DNA synthesis arrest, not uric acid-mediated mechanical rupture.
The inability to convert hypoxanthine to IMP describes HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan), not ADA deficiency.

ADA deficiency leads to an accumulation of adenosine and its deoxy-form dATP. High levels of dATP allosterically inhibit Ribonucleotide Reductase, starving the cell of the deoxyribonucleotides needed for DNA replication.
PRPP levels are not primarily depleted in ADA deficiency; PRPP depletion is more relevant to feedback loops in other pathways (like salvage pathway defects).
In ADA deficiency, dATP levels are increased, not decreased. Increased dATP inhibits, rather than activates, Ribonucleotide Reductase.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 301 (Book Page): A deficiency of ADA results in an accumulation of adenosine, which is converted to its ribonucleotide or deoxyribonucleotide forms by cellular kinases. As dATP levels rise, ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited, thus preventing the production of all deoxyribose-containing nucleotides... Consequently, cells cannot make DNA and divide.

category: g Methotrexate, 5 Flurouracil and Allupurinol
statement: In the synthesis of thymidine monophosphate (TMP), the conversion of dUMP to dTMP is unique because the folate cofactor acts as both a one-carbon donor and a reducing agent. Which pharmacological agent blocks the necessary 'recycling' of the resulting oxidized folate?
options: Allopurinol
Probenecid
5-Fluorouracil
Methotrexate
Colchicine
correctOption: Methotrexate
optionExplanations: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, which is unrelated to the folate cycle.
Probenecid is a uricosuric agent that affects renal transport of uric acid.
5-Fluorouracil inhibits the thymidylate synthase enzyme itself, not the recycling of the folate cofactor.
The dTMP synthesis reaction oxidizes THF to DHF. To continue synthesis, DHF must be reduced back to THF by dihydrofolate reductase. Methotrexate inhibits this enzyme, stopping the 'recycling' loop.
Colchicine is an anti-inflammatory drug used in acute gout that inhibits microtubule formation; it has no effect on nucleotide metabolism enzymes.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 304 (Book Page): DHF can be reduced to THF by dihydrofolate reductase (see Figure 28.3, Page 366 (Book Page)), an enzyme that is inhibited by drugs such as methotrexate.

category: Gout, SCID/ADA on basis of sign symptoms and data
statement: How does the clinical presentation of Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency differ from the presentation of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency?
options: PNP deficiency is less severe and primarily affects T-cells
PNP deficiency leads to hyperuricemia and kidney stones
PNP deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder
PNP deficiency causes self-mutilation, while ADA deficiency does not
PNP deficiency affects only B-cells, whereas ADA deficiency affects T-cells
correctOption: PNP deficiency is less severe and primarily affects T-cells
optionExplanations: PNP deficiency is clinically distinct because it is generally less severe than ADA-SCID and shows a predilection for T-cell dysfunction.
PNP is an enzyme in the degradation pathway; its deficiency would likely decrease uric acid production rather than cause hyperuricemia.
PNP deficiency, like ADA deficiency, is an autosomal recessive disorder, not X-linked (which describes Lesch-Nyhan).
Self-mutilation is characteristic of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (HGPRT deficiency), not PNP deficiency.
ADA deficiency affects T, B, and NK cells; PNP deficiency does not spare T-cells and affect B-cells only.
citation: In book "Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry", Page 293 (Book Page): [Note: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency results in a less severe immunodeficiency involving T-cells primarily.]

category: Outline the sequence of reactions that converts IMP to AMP and GMP and to their corresponding triphosphates
statement: Which intermediate is formed during the two-step enzymatic conversion of inosine monophosphate (IMP) to guanosine monophosphate (GMP)?
options: Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)
Orotidine monophosphate (OMP)
Hypoxanthine
5-Phosphoribosylamine
Adenylosuccinate
correctOption: Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP)
optionExplanations: Xanthosine monophosphate (XMP) is the intermediate formed by the oxidation of IMP. It is subsequently aminated to form GMP.
OMP is an intermediate in the pyrimidine synthesis pathway, the parent pyrimidine nucleotide.
